map.summary: POS offline & cash ledger at SHA 482b3f38 (branch p9 = d916b9b + P7 checkout redesign + one P9 commit). Server: online sales (POST /sales) and offline replay (POST /sync/push, honor_price_snapshot=True) both funnel into services/sales.py::_create_sale_once, a single transaction that locks inventory in global product order, dual-writes the cash leg through retrofit.on_cash_sale -> CashPostingService (sole writer to append-only cash.cash_ledger_entries), and enforces force_shift, post-T0 TILL custody, discount cap and disabled-method rules on replay too. Legacy shifts (shifts.py) and cash-native shifts (cash.shifts) are dual-written; closed-shift expected_cash is frozen, ledger-native tenants read expected cash from ON_SHIFT ledger legs. Client outbox is localStorage (packages/shared/src/lib/offline.ts), flushed in 1000-chunks with transient-vs-permanent triage and a dead-letter list. P9 tip commit (diff 758739b..482b3f38): adds GET /shifts/offline-sale-policy (server-side {mode,reason} decision: OPEN_SHIFT_REQUIRED, post-T0 TILL gates, DEVICE_CLOCK_UNRELIABLE clock check vs sync.py::_clamp_sold_at window), stable OPEN_SHIFT_REQUIRED code on the force_shift 400, api capability level 2 'offline_sale_policy', subscription ALLOW_READ for the route; client side caches the policy with timestamp+owner (CACHE.offlinePolicy), fail-closed offlineSaleAllowed() (8h TTL, owner match, future-timestamp reject), gates offline finish in POSKassa unless money already captured (QR confirmed / offline-card pref), refreshes policy on login and shift open, clears it on shift close, and makes dead-letter clearing two-step. Mobile Flutter app has no offline sale queue at this SHA (LATE_SYNC exists only in server ledger/docs).

Dimension A central question answered affirmatively by findings 1-3: yes, there are interleavings where a sale lands in a closed shift (finding 1, finding 2) and where Sale.shift_id != the SALE ledger entry's shift_id (findings 2 and 3).

Retry exhaustion yields 409 marked retry:true, and the next flush resolves via the idempotency check.

client_uuid is never replaced client-side: POSKassa saleUuidRef (line 313) is stable for the whole checkout and regenerated only AFTER success (line 696) — the comment documents that per-finish regeneration was a past bug; outbox and dead-letter entries carry the original uuid, and no requeue path regenerates one (clearFailed only deletes).

Online-attempt-timeout-then-queue double write is closed: submitSale queues the SAME client_uuid payload on transient failure, so a server-side commit whose response was lost is answered idempotently at flush (ok:true, entry removed once).

Partial-index predicate (deleted_at IS NULL) vs the idempotency SELECT (no deleted filter) is latent-only: no code path at this SHA sets Sale.deleted_at, so a soft-deleted sale cannot free the uuid while the SELECT misses it.

flushOutbox loss-safety verified: single-flight flag, removal only on ok:true or after deadLetter() returns true (quota-failure keeps the entry), whole-request errors keep the chunk and break the loop; 1000-chunking matches the server max_length so oversized queues cannot 422-wedge.
Owner scoping verified: flushOutbox and usePendingCount filter by owner_id so cashier A's queued sales are not written under cashier B's token (legacy owner-less entries are grandfathered by design).

Legacy open_shift double-open race is closed by ux_shifts_cashier_open plus rollback-and-return-existing (shifts.py open_shift IntegrityError handler); the cash-side duplicate open is isolated in a SAVEPOINT so it cannot break the legacy transaction.
Cross-tenant client_uuid collision is harmless: both the unique index and the idempotency SELECT are company-scoped, so another tenant's uuid neither blocks nor leaks a sale.

posting.post idempotency around the constraint is correctly error-handled in both modes: early + in-lock business-key reads, and in commit=True mode an IntegrityError at commit is re-read by business key and answered as IDEMPOTENCY_DUPLICATE rather than surfacing a 500 (posting.py _persist).

Dimension G: create_sale's 3x IntegrityError retry (services/sales.py:36-50) does db.rollback() before re-running, so inventory is never deducted twice across retries; a commit that raises IntegrityError was not applied server-side, so no committed+retried double either.

Concurrent duplicate offline replay is safe: partial unique index ux_sales_company_client_uuid (initdb.py:722, WHERE client_uuid IS NOT NULL AND deleted_at IS NULL) + the pre-insert idempotency SELECT + post-rollback re-read make the loser of a same-client_uuid race return the winner's Sale; the loser's inventory/ledger work is fully rolled back with its transaction.

Immutable-ledger triggers (cash_ddl_v1.sql:447-466) forbid UPDATE and DELETE row-wise and TRUNCATE statement-wise on cash_ledger_entries, cash_transfers, reconciliation_assignments, negative_cash_approvals, audit_logs; INSERT is intentionally allowed. No application ORM code mutates CashLedgerEntry rows (writers are only posting.py and migration/backfill.py); exceptions/recon tables are guarded column-wise (fn_guard_exception/fn_guard_recon). Bypass requires the credential-level hole reported separately.

cle_uq_business (tenant_id, source_type, source_id, leg_index) covers every posting path with disjoint identities: SALE/sale.id, RETURN/return_id, CUSTOMER_PAYMENT/payment_id, SUPPLIER_PAYMENT/payment_id, PURCHASE/purchase_id leg-0 + next_leg_index deltas, PURCHASE_RETURN/event-id, CASH_OP/movement_id, TRANSFER/movement_id legs 0-1, SHIFT_OPEN/shift-id. commit=True paths re-read by business key after IntegrityError (posting.py::_persist / post_transfer); commit=False paths propagate the IE and callers (add_cash_movement shifts.py:132-168, cash_op cashops.py:158-186) roll back the paired legacy row too and answer fail-closed 409 — never ok:true for an unwritten op.

posting.post re-checks idempotency under the account/shift lock BEFORE OUT-sufficiency (posting.py steps 5/9), so a duplicate OUT retry cannot fail with INSUFFICIENT_CASH; early duplicate with commit=True rolls back only its own standalone transaction.

Opening-float double count is avoided: on_shift_open posts only the positive delta over the ledger balance, and both close paths use shift_movement_total which excludes category OPENING (repositories.py).

lifecycle.open_shift's two-commit shape (CashShift committed, then opening float posted with adapters' default commit=True in a second transaction) is a real partial-commit hazard but has no production caller at this SHA — only tests reach it; retrofit.on_shift_open (the POS path) is single-transaction under a SAVEPOINT.

sync.push per-record isolation is otherwise correct: HTTPException 409/5xx and OperationalError are marked retry:true; the lot-invariant gate deliberately raises 409 so a paid offline receipt stays queued; the ledger-unavailable guard uses 503 on the sale path for the same reason.

Client outbox (packages/shared/src/lib/sync.ts / offline.ts): entries are removed only on ok:true; deadLetter returning false (localStorage quota) keeps the entry queued; flushOutbox is single-flight; per-owner filtering prevents cross-cashier attribution; whole-request failures dead-letter nothing. The P9 policy cache is fail-closed (shape check, 8h TTL, owner_id match, future-timestamp reject, cleared on logout/shift close); the moneyCaptured bypass is deliberate and preserves dead-letter evidence.

P9 tip commit (git diff 758739b..482b3f38) is additive: server gains GET /shifts/offline-sale-policy, the stable OPEN_SHIFT_REQUIRED/DEVICE_CLOCK_UNRELIABLE codes and capability level 2; client gains the fail-closed policy cache, the POSKassa offline gate and two-step dead-letter clearing. No transaction-boundary or dedupe behavior of the sale/cash pipeline changed in the tip.

Mobile Flutter app has no offline sale queue at this SHA; LATE_SYNC exists only in the server ledger (posting Case C) and correctly attaches to the closed cash shift with an open LATE_SYNC_UNACK exception rather than mutating the frozen reconciliation.

P9 tip commit (git diff 758739b..482b3f38): adds GET /shifts/offline-sale-policy (server decision {mode,reason}: OPEN_SHIFT_REQUIRED, post-T0 TILL_REQUIRED/LEGACY_SHIFT codes, DEVICE_CLOCK_UNRELIABLE), stable OPEN_SHIFT_REQUIRED header on the force_shift 400 in services/sales.py, api capability level 2, subscription ALLOW_READ; client: CACHE.offlinePolicy with timestamp+owner_id, fail-closed offlineSaleAllowed (8h TTL, future-timestamp reject, owner match), policy refresh on login/shift-open/syncTick, clear on shift-close/logout, POSKassa gate with moneyCaptured escape hatch, two-step dead-letter clearing. The design is sound; findings 2 and 4 above are the residual holes.

T0 enforcement time is genuinely server-side: enforcement_active (cutover_guard.py) ignores occurred_at/sold_at entirely, and sales.py calls require_post_t0_till on the replay path too — a backdated sold_at cannot reopen the pre-T0 TILL exemption (the /sync/push honor_price_snapshot bypass documented in T0_CUTOVER_ENFORCEMENT.md §1 is closed at this SHA).

sync.py::_clamp_sold_at correctly bounds client sold_at to [now-60d, now+5min] and falls back to server time (at=None) outside it, so absurd accounting dates cannot enter sold_at; posting._validate_timestamp additionally rejects device time >1 day in the future as INVALID rather than Case-B.

Client policy cache is robust against clock manipulation on the device: offlineSaleAllowed returns false when now < cached.at (clock rolled back), enforces the 8h TTL, requires owner_id == current employee, and refreshOfflinePolicy never extends permission on error/404 (cache untouched, expires naturally). clearOfflinePolicy on shift close and logout is present.

sync/push triage verified: HTTPException 409/5xx and OperationalError → retry:true (kept in outbox), other 4xx → permanent; client removes from outbox only after ok:true or after deadLetter() confirmed the write (QA OFF-3), and flushOutbox is single-flight with per-1000 chunks — no silent client-side loss found on this path.

Backfill (migration/backfill.py) handles the T0 boundary deliberately: shifts straddling T0 or still open go to REVIEW and their legs are not inserted; LATE_SYNC is never used in backfill; inserts are ON CONFLICT (cle_uq_business) DO NOTHING with deterministic uuid5 ids — idempotent, no double-posting hole found.

Replay-path fraud guards hold: max_disc cap, disabled payment methods, QR txn validation (COMPLETED, amount match, single consume under FOR UPDATE) and force_shift all execute for honor_price_snapshot=True as well; price snapshot honoring is offline-only and audited (offline_price_snapshot audit row).

Dimension K, other timestamps: shift opened_at/closed_at, CashMovement.created_at, ledger server_received_at/recorded_at are all server-clock; client time only enters as sold_at/device_occurred_at (findings 1-3) and the policy client_time (evaluated server-side). No other invariant found relying on client time.

Sale idempotency is properly tenant-scoped: SELECT in services/sales.py:59-64 filters client_uuid AND company_id, and ux_sales_company_client_uuid is UNIQUE (company_id, client_uuid) (initdb.py:722-725); tenant A cannot hit or reveal tenant B's sale via client_uuid, and the IntegrityError->retry->existing-sale path is closed.

ux_cashmov_client_uuid_all is deliberately global (cash_movements has no company column), but both writers handle the constraint fail-closed: on IntegrityError they re-check a company-scoped movement (custody_preview.cash_op_movement joins Shift->Branch on company) AND material-field match before answering 'duplicate'; a cross-tenant collision yields 409 CASH_OP_WRITE_FAILED, never a false success (shifts.py:137-160, cashops.py:166-195).

cle_uq_business is tenant-scoped: UNIQUE (tenant_id, source_type, source_id, leg_index) (cash_ddl_v1.sql:232); posting/retrofit derive tenant from emp.company_id and source_id from server-generated ids, so ledger idempotency cannot be steered by client payloads.

All client-supplied foreign IDs in the sale path are validated against the auth context before use: customer_id (services/sales.py:71-76), product_id (:266-269, before any Inventory row creation), terminal_id (:127-133 must belong to the actor branch), till_id (till_identity.validate_till_for_branch with emp.company_id + branch), qr_txn_id (QrPayment filtered by company_id with FOR UPDATE, :601-603); sale branch comes from actor_branch(emp), never from payload.

Shift object endpoints enforce ownership, which implies tenant isolation: /shifts/{id}/cash POST+GET, /shifts/{id}/summary and /shifts/{id}/close all 404 unless Shift.cashier_id == emp.id; a tenant-B shift_id can never satisfy that for a tenant-A token. /shifts/overview and /cash/ops today-list are company- and visible_branches-scoped.

Sales read endpoints are IDOR-safe: /sales, /sales/summary, /sales/cashiers filter Sale.company_id + visible_branches; audit filters (shift_id/till_id/terminal_id/branch_id) are ANDed onto the company-scoped base; /sales/find and /sales/{id} apply SALES_DOC_TIER permission before any query, company + visible_branches scope, and uniform 404s (sales.py get_sale/find_sale). The Employee-by-full_name subqueries lack a company filter but are only used to filter an already company-scoped Sale set — no cross-tenant leak.

Returns path (in sales.py) is scoped: Return idempotency SELECT and ux_returns_client_uuid are company-scoped; original sale is locked FOR UPDATE and checked for company + visible_branches; products checked for company; refund price comes from the original SaleItem snapshot, not the payload.

/inventory/transfer validates both branches (company, deleted_at, is_active) under FOR UPDATE and the source against visible_branches; foreign-tenant product_ids are rejected (400) before commit so the pre-validation Inventory row inserts roll back — no cross-tenant write persists (dedup scope defect reported separately).

collection destination_safe_id and shift till_id are validated by cutover_guard.require_custody_account: tenant (acc.tenant_id == company_id), branch, type TILL/SAFE, ACTIVE status and currency (cutover_guard.py:254-294) — a tenant-B safe/till id is rejected on both /shifts/{id}/cash and /cash/ops collection paths.

P9 tip commit (git diff 758739b..482b3f38) is isolation-clean for dimension L: GET /shifts/offline-sale-policy requires kassa.sell, decides only from Shift.cashier_id == emp.id + the caller's own company settings, and leaks neither the security settings object nor other cashiers' state; the client cache is owner_id-bound, TTL'd (8h), rejects future timestamps, is cleared on logout/shift close, and unknown server responses leave the cache untouched (fail-closed). client_time only influences the caller's own decision.

/sync/push is scoped end-to-end: requires kassa.sell, every record goes through create_sale under emp's company; duplicate results echo only same-company sale id/receipt_no; /sync/pull counts are company-filtered.

Dimension L conclusion: no cross-tenant read or write path was found in sales.py, shifts.py, sync.py or cashops.py at this SHA; the real defects found are intra-tenant authorization/idempotency-scope issues (reported above).
No retry cap exists: transient (retry:true) entries are never silently dropped after N attempts — the failure mode is the opposite (eternal retry, see finding 4), not silent loss.

Whole-request failures in flushOutbox (network/timeout/401/5xx on POST /sync/push) remove nothing and `break` out of the chunk loop — the queue survives intact; outboxRemove happens only on per-record ok:true.

Lost-response replay is safe: server dedups by company-scoped client_uuid lookup at the top of _create_sale_once (plus ux_sales_company_client_uuid), and the client re-push gets ok:true for the existing sale, so a mid-response network drop cannot double-book or lose a sale.

localStorage-quota on outboxAdd is not a silent loss: submitSale dead-letters best-effort and always throws a visible error before the sale UI completes (deadLetter's return is ignored there, but the sale never entered the outbox and the cashier is told storage is full).

App update: the queue lives in localStorage of the Electron userData partition under stable keys; committed code contains no version-keyed purge or storage migration that would drop it on update (only the one-time legacy->namespaced key migration in offline.ts, which preserves data).
A push result that omits a record's client_uuid, or a 200 response with no results[] (old server), leaves the records queued — the client never infers rejection from absence.

Dead-letter clearing is genuinely two-step at this SHA (POSKassa confirmClear warn + separate confirm button, data-testid failed-clear-confirm); residual: clearing still erases payload evidence with no export, but that is an accepted operator action.

flushOutbox is single-flight (flushing flag), preventing the double-dead-letter race between the 30s tick, online event, login and submitSale triggers; uuid matching is lowercase-normalized on both sides.

Client half of LATE_SYNC (shift closed after sales were queued) is handled: Shift.tsx blocks close while the local outbox is non-empty, and server-side replay resolves the shift historically (opened_at <= sold_at <= closed_at), so a shift closed AFTER the sale was taken still accepts the replay — the residual gaps are the multi-device policy case (finding 5) and the unfiltered-close gate (finding 1).
Mobile Flutter app at 482b3f38 has no offline sale queue (apps/mobile mentions offline only in connectivity banners/api error text), so no client-loss surface there — consistent with the area map.

P9 tip commit (git diff 758739b..482b3f38): server gains GET /shifts/offline-sale-policy (force_shift, post-T0 TILL, clock checks), stable OPEN_SHIFT_REQUIRED header on the force_shift 400, capability level and subscription ALLOW_READ; client gains the fail-closed policy cache (8h TTL, owner match, future-timestamp reject), gating in POSKassa.finish, policy refresh on login/shift-open and clear on close/logout, and the two-step dead-letter clear. It does NOT change outbox mechanics, retry triage, the dead-letter 200 cap, or the URL namespacing — findings 1-4 predate and survive the P9 commit.

findings.title: Sale transaction never locks or re-checks the legacy Shift: a sale can commit into an already-closed shift, permanently corrupting frozen expected_cash
findings.claim: The online sale path reads the cashier's open Shift with a plain unlocked query (services/sales.py:104-107) and stamps Sale.shift_id=shift.id (:212) without ever locking the row or re-checking status before commit. close_shift (apps/server/app/api/v1/shifts.py:540) locks the Shift FOR UPDATE and freezes expected_cash from committed SalePayment/CashMovement/ledger sums, but that lock only serializes against add_cash_movement/cash_op/refund (which lock the shift) — sales take no legacy-shift lock at all, so close and sale interleave freely.
findings.invariant: A sale must not be attributed to a shift whose close/reconciliation snapshot has already been (or is concurrently being) frozen; Shift.expected_cash must include every cash SalePayment whose Sale.shift_id is that shift.
findings.attack_scenario: T1: POST /sales starts (large basket; tx held open by inventory/FEFO locks); it has read Shift S as OPEN. T2: cashier's other window calls POST /shifts/{S}/close — it locks S, sums committed cash payments (T1 uncommitted, excluded), sets expected_cash/difference, status=closed, commits. T1 then commits: Sale.shift_id=S (closed), its cash is in the physical drawer but missing from the frozen expected_cash → permanent false surplus in the Z-report; on ledger-native tenants ledger_expected_shift_cash (tenant.py:179) was also summed before T1's leg existed, so the recon snapshot is equally stale. Even the ordering where the sale already holds the cash.shifts FOR UPDATE row lock does not help: retrofit.on_shift_close (retrofit.py:168-205) computes `expected` BEFORE its flush blocks on that lock and never recomputes after acquiring it.
findings.evidence: services/sales.py:104-107: `shift = db.query(Shift).filter(Shift.cashier_id == emp.id, Shift.status == ShiftStatus.open).first()` — no with_for_update, no later status re-check. close_shift docstring (shifts.py:534-537) claims the lock serializes with "add_cash_movement/cash_op/cash-refund (hammasi smenani qulflaydi)" — sales are absent from that list. retrofit.py:186-205: `expected = ...` computed, then `sh.status = "CLOSED"` and `db.flush()` — expected not recomputed after the flush's row lock is granted.
findings.suggested_repro: PG, two sessions: S1 begins create_sale for open shift X and pauses after the Inventory FOR UPDATE; S2 closes shift X (commits, expected_cash frozen); S1 commits. Assert Sale.shift_id==X, X.status==closed, and X.expected_cash < sum(cash SalePayment where shift_id=X).

verdicts.reasoning: The finding's central mechanism claim and its only concrete attack are wrong, but a narrow residual race survives, so it cannot be fully refuted. (1) REFUTED part — protective constraint the finding missed: Sale.shift_id is a genuine FK to shifts.id (apps/server/app/models/sales.py:25-26; db/schema.sql:625), and _create_sale_once flushes the Sale row at apps/server/app/services/sales.py:240-241, BEFORE the inventory/FEFO with_for_update loop (:274+). On Postgres that INSERT's RI check takes FOR KEY SHARE on the parent shifts row for the rest of the transaction, and close_shift's `db.query(Shift)...with_for_update()` (FOR UPDATE, apps/server/app/api/v1/shifts.py) conflicts with FOR KEY SHARE. So for the entire heavy portion of the sale (inventory locks, FEFO, payments, receipt numbering, ledger leg) the close BLOCKS at its very first statement, and once unblocked it recomputes the SalePayment/CashMovement/ledger sums under READ COMMITTED fresh snapshots, INCLUDING the just-committed sale. The attack scenario as written ("tx held open by inventory/FEFO locks ... T1 uncommitted, excluded") and the suggested repro ("pause after the Inventory FOR UPDATE") are therefore impossible — that pause point demonstrates the protection. The finding's retrofit.on_shift_close argument is also moot in that ordering: close never reaches retrofit because it is blocked at the legacy-shift FOR UPDATE. (2) SURVIVING defect: between the unlocked shift SELECT (sales.py:103-107) and the Sale flush (:241) the sale transaction holds no lock on the shift (only a few read-only statements: force_shift Setting, cutover/till/terminal lookups). A close that acquires FOR UPDATE in that few-millisecond window freezes expected_cash from committed rows and commits; the sale then inserts Sale.shift_id pointing at the now-closed shift and commits. No mechanism re-validates: reject_closed_shift_replay (apps/server/app/services/cash/cutover_guard.py:207-224) inspects only the stale in-memory ORM object (loaded as open, never re-queried); the FK RI check verifies row existence, not status; there is no trigger/CHECK on public.sales tied to shift status; and on ledger-native tenants retrofit.on_cash_sale re-resolves the open cash.shift, gets None (CLOSED), and posts the leg with origin_shift_id=None (OFF_SHIFT anomaly) instead of failing — so both the legacy expected_cash and ledger_expected_shift_cash miss the payment while the cash is physically in the drawer. The invariant violation is real but the practical exposure is a millisecond-scale window per sale, not the "interleave freely" P1 the finding describes; severity should be downgraded and the fix is cheap (re-check Shift.status, or SELECT the shift FOR KEY SHARE/with a status re-read after the Sale flush).
verdicts.protective_constraint_found: FK sales.shift_id REFERENCES shifts(id) + early flush: the Sale INSERT at services/sales.py:240-241 (before the inventory FOR UPDATE loop at :274) takes FOR KEY SHARE on the shifts row, which conflicts with close_shift's SELECT ... FOR UPDATE — so for everything after that flush (the finding's whole attack window) close blocks and then recomputes expected_cash including the committed sale. Protection does NOT cover sales.py:103-107→241.
verdicts.repro_hint: PG, two sessions. The pause point must be BEFORE the Sale flush, not after the inventory locks: monkeypatch/breakpoint _create_sale_once between the shift query (services/sales.py:104-107) and db.flush() (:241) — e.g. hook the Setting("security") or cutover_at read. While T1 is paused there, T2 runs POST /shifts/{X}/close to completion (commits; expected_cash frozen). Resume T1; it commits. Assert: Sale.shift_id==X, X.status=='closed', X.expected_cash < opening_cash + sum(SalePayment.amount where method_code='cash' and sale.shift_id=X); on a ledger-native tenant also assert the sale's cash_ledger_entries leg has shift_id NULL (OFF_SHIFT). Control test: pause T1 instead after :241 (e.g. inside the inventory loop) and observe T2's close block until T1 commits and then include the sale — confirming the FK KEY SHARE protection and refuting the original scenario.

verdicts.protective_constraint_found: Implicit FK row lock: sales.shift_id FK → INSERT INTO sales takes FOR KEY SHARE on the shifts row at the early flush (services/sales.py:240-241, before all inventory/FEFO locks), which conflicts with close_shift's SELECT ... FOR UPDATE (api/v1/shifts.py:545). This serializes shift-close against every sale that has already flushed its Sale row — exactly the long-transaction phase the finding's attack relies on. Additionally, the cash posting service locks the candidate cash.shifts row (posting.py _lock_candidate_shift, "sale-vs-close") and converts close-race legs into LATE_SYNC/OFF_SHIFT with open exception records rather than silent attachment.
verdicts.repro_hint: PG, two sessions. S1: run _create_sale_once for open shift X and pause AFTER the shift query (services/sales.py:104-107) but BEFORE db.flush() at :241 (e.g. breakpoint/monkeypatch on actor_branch or the till-validation step) — pausing any later is useless because the FK FOR KEY SHARE then blocks the close. S2: POST /shifts/{X}/close to completion (commits, expected_cash frozen). Resume S1; it must NOT error. Assert: Sale.shift_id==X, X.status=='closed', X.expected_cash < opening_cash + sum(cash SalePayment joined via Sale.shift_id==X), and (ledger-native) the sale's cash.cash_ledger_entries leg has posting_kind='OFF_SHIFT' with an UNRESOLVED_OFF_SHIFT exception. Also verify the refutation half: pause S1 instead just after :241 (or during inventory locks) and confirm S2's close blocks until S1 commits and then includes S1's payment in expected_cash.

findings.title: Stale SQLAlchemy identity-map in _lock_candidate_shift: cash leg posted ON_SHIFT into a shift that closed while the poster waited on the row lock, silently bypassing LATE_SYNC
findings.claim: retrofit.on_cash_sale first loads the open CashShift via repo.open_shift_for_account (retrofit.py:91-93, full ORM entity into the identity map), then posting._lock_candidate_shift (posting.py:291-305) re-selects that shift by id `.with_for_update()` WITHOUT populate_existing. If a concurrent close holds the row lock (retrofit.on_shift_close flush, or lifecycle.close_shift), the poster blocks, the closer commits status='CLOSED', the FOR UPDATE query then matches the row (WHERE has only tenant_id+id, no status predicate) — but SQLAlchemy returns the cached instance with the pre-lock attribute status='OPEN'. _resolve_shift (posting.py:333-336) therefore takes Case A and stamps the immutable ledger entry ON_SHIFT into a CLOSED shift with no LATE_SYNC_UNACK exception, and the shift's already-written ReconciliationRecord excludes it.
findings.invariant: Posting contract Case C: an entry for a shift that is CLOSED at lock time must be LATE_SYNC + LATE_SYNC_UNACK (the code's own comment at posting.py:337 — "CLOSED (yoki CLOSING — lock ostида CLOSED bo'lib qoladi)" — assumes the lock reveals CLOSED; the stale identity map defeats exactly that assumption).
findings.attack_scenario: Ledger-native tenant, open shift S on till T. T2 (close): legacy close_shift enters retrofit.on_shift_close, flushes the cash.shifts UPDATE (row lock held), continues toward commit. T1 (sale): on_cash_sale reads S via open_shift_for_account (sees OPEN — T2 uncommitted), passes origin_shift_id=S.id; _lock_candidate_shift blocks on T2's row lock; T2 commits (S CLOSED, recon frozen); T1 acquires the lock, cand.status reads stale 'OPEN', posts IN·SALE ON_SHIFT S. Result: closed shift S has an ON_SHIFT leg not in its frozen reconciliation snapshot, no exception row, entry immutable — the authoritative expected-cash source (repo.shift_expected_cash) permanently disagrees with the reconciliation record and nothing flags it.
findings.evidence: posting.py:294-298 (origin branch): `sh = db.execute(select(CashShift).where(CashShift.tenant_id == tenant_id, CashShift.id == origin_shift_id).with_for_update()).scalar_one_or_none()` — no populate_existing, no db.refresh; grep shows no populate_existing anywhere in app/services/cash. The project itself documents this exact bug class for Customer (services/sales.py QA CC-001 comment: "with_for_update DB qulfini oladi, LEKIN o'sha KESH obyektni qaytaradi ... (populate_existing yo'q)") and fixed it there with db.refresh — the same fix is missing here. Note the no-origin branch (posting.py:300-305) is accidentally safe because status is in the WHERE clause and EvalPlanQual re-evaluates it; only the origin_shift_id branch — the one on_cash_sale always uses when a shift exists — is affected.
findings.suggested_repro: PG, two sessions: S2 runs retrofit.on_shift_close up to flush (hold); S1 runs on_cash_sale for the same till (loads shift OPEN) and reaches _lock_candidate_shift (blocks); S2 commits; S1 completes. Assert the new cash_ledger_entries row has posting_kind='ON_SHIFT', shift_id=S, while cash.shifts.status='CLOSED' and no LATE_SYNC_UNACK exception row exists.

verdicts.reasoning: The stale-identity-map mechanism is real and statically verified at SHA 482b3f38: (1) retrofit._open_cash_shift_id -> repo.open_shift_for_account (apps/server/app/services/cash/repositories.py) loads the full CashShift ORM entity into the session identity map; (2) CashPostingService._lock_candidate_shift's origin_shift_id branch (apps/server/app/services/cash/posting.py) re-selects by (tenant_id, id).with_for_update() with no populate_existing(), and grep confirms no populate_existing/db.refresh anywhere in app/services/cash except lifecycle.py post-commit refreshes; SessionLocal is autoflush=False, expire_on_commit=False (app/db/session.py:72), so the cached 'OPEN' attributes survive and _resolve_shift takes Case A instead of Case C. The project itself documents this exact ORM pitfall at services/sales.py:621 (QA CC-001, fixed with db.refresh for Customer) — the same fix is missing here. DB side offers no protection: cash_ddl_v1.sql's cle_shift_fk references (tenant_id, id, cash_account_id) only, and the only triggers on cash.cash_ledger_entries are immutability and transfer-pairing — nothing rejects an ON_SHIFT insert into a CLOSED shift. HOWEVER, the finding's headline attack (a sale racing the close of the SAME shift — 'the one on_cash_sale always uses when a shift exists') is blocked by a protective mechanism the finder missed: api/v1/shifts.py close_shift takes SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the LEGACY shifts row before anything else (QA SHIFT-1), and Sale.shift_id is a genuine FK to shifts.id (models/sales.py:25), so the sale's INSERT — flushed at the explicit db.flush() in services/sales.py BEFORE on_cash_sale is invoked — holds FOR KEY SHARE on that same legacy row until commit. FOR UPDATE conflicts with FOR KEY SHARE, so same-shift sale-vs-close fully serializes: close-first makes the sale re-read after commit and take flagged Case D (OFF_SHIFT + UNRESOLVED_OFF_SHIFT exception), sale-first makes the close wait so its reconciliation snapshot includes the leg. The defect therefore survives only where the sale's legacy shift differs from the closing shift while both map to the same till's cash.shift: (a) multi-cashier branch — retrofit.on_shift_open §19 explicitly creates NO cash.shift for the second cashier, so cashier B's sale (KEY SHARE on legacy S_B) posts origin_shift_id=S_A while cashier A's close locks only legacy S_A — no lock conflict, race fully live; (b) shift-less cash sale (force_shift off, sale.shift_id NULL, till_id declared/resolved) — no KEY SHARE at all. In those paths any close of S_A committing between _open_cash_shift_id's read and _lock_candidate_shift's FOR UPDATE (blocking not even required — pure commit-in-the-gap suffices) yields the stale OPEN -> immutable ON_SHIFT leg into the CLOSED shift, absent from the frozen ReconciliationRecord, with no exception row, and repo.shift_expected_cash permanently disagrees with the recon snapshot. Verdict PLAUSIBLE rather than CONFIRMED_STATIC because the finding's stated scenario is materially mitigated by the legacy-row lock and the surviving paths need a two-session PG test to demonstrate end-to-end; the missing-refresh defect itself and the unprotected interleavings are established from code alone.
verdicts.protective_constraint_found: Partial only: api/v1/shifts.py close_shift acquires FOR UPDATE on the legacy public.shifts row at entry (QA SHIFT-1), and Sale.shift_id is an FK to shifts.id, so a cash sale's flushed INSERT holds FOR KEY SHARE on that row (Postgres RI check) until commit — the conflict serializes sale-vs-close whenever sale.shift_id equals the closing legacy shift (the same-cashier case; cash.shift.id == legacy shift id per retrofit.on_shift_open). This closes the finding's exact T1/T2 scenario (outcome is either a correct recon that includes the leg, or a flagged Case D OFF_SHIFT+UNRESOLVED_OFF_SHIFT entry — never a silent ON_SHIFT into a closed shift). It does NOT cover: (a) a second cashier's sale on the same till (legacy shift S_B, KEY SHARE on S_B, but posting into till's open cash.shift S_A — supported per on_shift_open §19), or (b) a shift-less cash sale (sale.shift_id NULL, no KEY SHARE). No DB-level constraint or trigger checks shift status on cash_ledger_entries insert (cle_shift_fk is tenant/id/account only), and no populate_existing/refresh exists in posting.py.
verdicts.repro_hint: PG, ledger-native tenant, one till T. Setup: cashier A opens legacy shift S_A with till T (creates cash.shift S_A OPEN); cashier B opens legacy shift S_B on the same branch/till (retrofit.on_shift_open skips cash.shift creation — sh_one_open_per_account). Session 1 (cashier B sale): run services/sales.py create-sale up to retrofit.on_cash_sale; pause immediately after _open_cash_shift_id has returned S_A (it read status OPEN into the identity map) and before posting._lock_candidate_shift executes. Session 2 (cashier A): POST /shifts/{S_A}/close to completion (its legacy FOR UPDATE on S_A does not conflict with session 1's FOR KEY SHARE on S_B; cash.shift S_A becomes CLOSED, ReconciliationRecord written excluding B's leg). Resume session 1 and commit. Assert: new cash.cash_ledger_entries row has posting_kind='ON_SHIFT' and shift_id=S_A while cash.shifts.status='CLOSED' for S_A; no cash_ledger_exceptions row (no LATE_SYNC_UNACK) for that entry; repo.shift_expected_cash(S_A) != the frozen reconciliation_records.ledger_balance_snapshot. Variant (b): same race with a shift-less cash sale (force_shift off, client-declared till_id=T, sale.shift_id NULL) racing cashier A's close. Fix to verify: db.refresh(sh) (or .execution_options(populate_existing=True)) after the with_for_update() select in _lock_candidate_shift's origin branch — mirroring the QA CC-001 fix at services/sales.py.

verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed by static walk of the actual runtime path; all refutation attempts (EvalPlanQual, lock ordering, session expiry, DB constraints/triggers) failed. See main reasoning field.
verdicts.protective_constraint_found: None. No populate_existing/refresh in app/services/cash/posting.py; no DB trigger or CHECK ties cash_ledger_entries.posting_kind='ON_SHIFT' to shifts.status='OPEN' (cle_posting_shift only requires shift_id NOT NULL); closers do not lock the CashAccount row, and even account-lock serialization would not fix the pre-cached identity-map instance loaded in retrofit.on_cash_sale before posting begins.
verdicts.repro_hint: PG, two sessions, ledger-native tenant, open shift S on till T. Session2: begin lifecycle.close_shift(shift_id=S) but pause after its with_for_update + status='CLOSED' assignment, before commit (or retrofit.on_shift_close paused after db.flush()). Session1: run the cash-sale flow (retrofit.on_cash_sale with till_id=T) — open_shift_for_account returns S as OPEN; it blocks inside posting._lock_candidate_shift. Session2 commits. Session1 completes. Assert: new cash.cash_ledger_entries row has posting_kind='ON_SHIFT' and shift_id=S while cash.shifts.status='CLOSED' for S, no cash_ledger_exceptions row of kind LATE_SYNC_UNACK exists, and the entry's amount is absent from S's reconciliation_records.expected_cash_snapshot. Control: apply .populate_existing() to the origin branch and observe LATE_SYNC + LATE_SYNC_UNACK instead.

findings.title: Offline replay posts the cash leg to the CURRENTLY open cash shift, not the shift the sale is attributed to: Sale.shift_id=A but ledger leg ON_SHIFT B, silently, when B opened within the 60-min tolerance
findings.claim: For /sync/push replay, _create_sale_once resolves the shift HISTORICALLY by sold_at (services/sales.py:95-101, may be a closed shift A, QA PAY-02) and sets Sale.shift_id=A, but on_cash_sale (retrofit.py:228-247) ignores that resolution: it computes origin_shift_id via _open_cash_shift_id(till) — the shift open NOW on the till (shift B). Since cash.shifts.id == legacy Shift.id (on_shift_open, retrofit.py:141), the correct anchor A was directly addressable (posting would yield contract Case C LATE_SYNC into A), yet the caller never passes sale.shift_id. If sold_at falls inside B's window (B.opened_at − 60min ≤ sold_at, posting.py:_in_window with _TS_TOLERANCE_MIN=60), _resolve_shift returns Case A: ON_SHIFT B with NO exception row.
findings.invariant: The SALE cash-ledger entry's shift attribution must match the shift the Sale is recorded in (or be LATE_SYNC into it / flagged OFF_SHIFT) — never silently ON_SHIFT a different shift.
findings.attack_scenario: Pre-T0 tenant with dual-write active (SHADOW/PRIMARY, cutover not reached — enforcement_active false so cutover_guard.reject_closed_shift_replay:207 does not run). Shift A on till T closes 14:00; same cashier opens shift B on T at 14:30; POS was offline, an offline cash sale with sold_at=13:50 flushes at 14:40. Legacy resolution: opened_at<=13:50 and closed_at>=13:50 → Sale.shift_id=A. Ledger: origin=_open_cash_shift_id(T)=B; _in_window(13:50,B): 14:30−60min=13:30 ≤ 13:50 → ON_SHIFT B, no exception. B's ledger expected is inflated by cash that was physically counted at A's close → false shortage at B's close; Sale.shift_id != leg.shift_id with zero anomaly signal, and shadow_compare/backfill parity for both shifts is skewed. (Post-T0 tenants are instead hard-rejected by reject_closed_shift_replay — the sale dead-letters; the silent variant is pre-T0 only.)
findings.evidence: retrofit.py:239-243: `if till_id is not None: till,_err = _ti.get_till(...); shift_id = _open_cash_shift_id(db, emp.company_id, till)` — sale.shift_id is available at the call site (services/sales.py:696 passes till_id=sale.till_id but not sale.shift_id). posting.py:333-335: OPEN + in-window → `return CashPostingKind.ON_SHIFT.value, cand.id, []` (no exception).
findings.suggested_repro: SQLite/PG single-session: open shift A (dual-write on), close it, open B on the same till 30 min later (or set opened_at accordingly), push an offline receipt with sold_at inside A but within B.opened_at−60min. Assert sale.shift_id==A while the SALE ledger entry has shift_id==B, posting_kind='ON_SHIFT', and no cash_ledger_exceptions row.

verdicts.reasoning: (duplicate-safe)
verdicts.protective_constraint_found: None. reject_closed_shift_replay (cutover_guard.py:207) is the only mechanism aimed at this and it early-returns when enforcement_active is False (pre-T0). findings.title: Post-T0 'one open shift per TILL' gate is unlocked check-then-insert: two concurrent opens by different cashiers both succeed on the same till

Two concurrent open_shift requests from DIFFERENT cashiers naming the same till both pass the check and both commit.
findings.invariant: Post-T0, at most one open legacy Shift per till_id (the error message promises it; sh_one_open_per_account only protects cash.shifts, not the legacy table).
findings.attack_scenario: Cashiers C1 and C2 both POST /shifts/open with till_id=T concurrently. C1's on_shift_open creates CashShift(id=L1); C2's begin_nested INSERT blocks on sh_one_open_per_account, gets IntegrityError after C1 commits, savepoint rolls back, returns None (retrofit.py:161-162) — C2's legacy shift commits open on till T with NO cash shift and no opening float. Every cash sale by C2 then resolves _open_cash_shift_id → C1's cash shift: C2's Sale.shift_id=L2 but ledger legs ON_SHIFT L1 (cross-cashier attribution). Whichever cashier closes first, retrofit.on_shift_close closes the till's open cash shift (repo.open_shift_for_account, retrofit.py:181) — i.e. C2's close can close C1's cash anchor mid-shift; the other close then finds no open cash shift and writes no reconciliation at all.

findings.title: on_shift_close closes whichever cash shift is open on the till without verifying it matches the closing legacy shift (pre-T0 shared drawer): second cashier's close steals the first cashier's cash anchor
findings.claim: on_shift_close resolves the cash shift with repo.open_shift_for_account(till) (retrofit.py:181) and closes it, never checking sh.id == the closing legacy shift's id even though the ids are defined to be equal (on_shift_open creates CashShift(id=legacy_shift_id)). findings.attack_scenario: Pre-T0 SHADOW tenant, branch with one till: C1 opens L1 (cash shift C1'=L1 created); C2 opens L2 (cash shift skipped per §19). C1's subsequent sales post Case D OFF_SHIFT/UNRESOLVED (no open cash shift); when C1 finally closes L1, open_shift_for_account returns None → return None → no cash close, no recon. A one-line `if sh.id != <legacy shift id>: return None` (the legacy id is available at the call site, shifts.py:571-575 passes till_id but not s.id) would eliminate it.

(2) In apps/server/app/services/cash/retrofit.py, `on_shift_open` for C2 hits the §19 fast path (`if repo.open_shift_for_account(db, tenant, till.id) is not None: return None`) — no CashShift with id==L2 is ever created; the only open cash shift on the till is CashShift(id==L1).

(3) The decisive point: `on_shift_close(db, emp, *, branch_id, counted_cash=0, terminal_id=None, till_id=None, opening_cash=0)` does not even take the legacy shift id as a parameter — the call site (shifts.py, close_shift, `_cr.on_shift_close(db, emp, branch_id=s.branch_id, counted_cash=..., terminal_id=s.terminal_id, till_id=s.till_id, opening_cash=s.opening_cash)`) never passes s.id. (4) Downstream, C1's later sales find no open cash shift (Case D), and C1's close gets `sh is None -> return None`: no cash close, no recon for L1's own count. The id-equality contract the code itself declares (retrofit.py comment: "cash.shift id == LEGACY shift id ... runtime va backfill IZCHIL ... shadow_compare va T0 chegarasi shu bir xil id orqali trivial mos keladi") is broken.

Protective mechanisms checked and absent: no `sh.id == legacy_shift_id` comparison (the id is not passed); the FOR UPDATE lock in close_shift is on L2's legacy Shift row, not on L1 or the CashShift; the unique index sh_one_open_per_account is precisely what forces the §19 skip and cannot help at close time; no trigger or gate in lifecycle/repositories ties CashShift closure to the owning legacy shift. findings.title: P9 offline-sale policy cache is per-device: same cashier's second device keeps a stale ALLOWED for up to 8h after the shift is closed elsewhere, reopening the exact money-taken/dead-letter failure P9 targets
findings.claim: The P9 gate's stated soundness argument — "Smenani esa FAQAT egasi yopadi va buning uchun internet kerak" (the shift can only be closed by its owner, which needs internet, so an ALLOWED verdict stays valid while offline) — is false when the SAME cashier is logged in on two devices (dimension J). close_shift only requires s.cashier_id == emp.id; Shift.tsx clears the cached policy only on the device that performed the close. The other device's cacheGet'd {mode:'ALLOWED', owner_id:me} passes every offlineSaleAllowed check (owner matches, TTL 8h) while offline.
findings.invariant: offlineSaleAllowed()==true must imply the server would accept the offline receipt on replay (that is the gate's entire purpose).
findings.attack_scenario: force_shift tenant; cashier logged into POS-1 and POS-2 (same account). POS-2 loses network at 10:00 with a fresh ALLOWED. At 10:30 the cashier closes the shift from POS-1 (online) and opens none. POS-2, still offline, keeps finishing cash sales until 18:00 (TTL). On reconnect, /sync/push replays: sold_at > closed_at, so the historical shift lookup (services/sales.py:96-101) finds nothing → force_shift 400 OPEN_SHIFT_REQUIRED → dead-letter: money physically taken from customers, no sale, no stock decrement, no cash record — the pre-P9 failure mode, now with a UI that told the cashier it was safe. Mitigation existing: dead-letter retains evidence with the stable code and two-step clearing.

Server side: push a cash receipt with sold_at after closed_at under force_shift → 400 OPEN_SHIFT_REQUIRED dead-letter.

findings.title: Replayed offline cash sale's ledger leg is posted ON_SHIFT into the CURRENT open cash shift, not the shift the sale belongs to

Since cash-shift ids equal legacy shift ids (on_shift_open creates CashShift(id=legacy_shift_id)), passing sale.shift_id was trivially possible and would have yielded the correct LATE_SYNC Case C.
findings.invariant: A sale's cash ledger leg must carry the same shift attribution as Sale.shift_id (or be flagged LATE_SYNC/OFF_SHIFT); a leg must never be silently counted in another shift's expected cash.

Assert Sale.shift_id == S1 while the cash_ledger_entries row for that sale has shift_id == S2 and posting_kind='ON_SHIFT'; assert repo.shift_expected_cash(S2) includes the amount.

I tried to refute this and could not; every link is provable by reading the code at 482b3f38.

1) Replay entry: apps/server/app/api/v1/sync.py::push calls `create_sale(db, emp, s, at=_clamp_sold_at(s.sold_at), honor_price_snapshot=True)`. For a sale sold 25 min before flush, _clamp_sold_at returns the historical sold_at, so in _create_sale_once `now = at` = 13:55.

No race is required — the misposting is deterministic given that state, and shift handovers within an hour of the last offline sale are routine POS operation. (3) apps/server/app/api/v1/shifts.py close_shift computes expected once and freezes `s.expected_cash`, `s.difference`, `s.status = closed`; a repo-wide grep shows close_shift line 568 is the ONLY runtime writer of Shift.expected_cash, and QA SHIFT-4 (shifts.py:228-232) makes the summary endpoint prefer the frozen value for closed shifts, cementing the divergence. (4) close_shift has no server-side pending-sale/outbox gate; the only close-before-sync guard is packages/shared/src/screens/Shift.tsx:246 (localStorage outbox check), bypassed by any second device, another tab, or a direct API call — close_shift only checks cashier_id == emp.id, so the same cashier closing from POS-2 succeeds. Protective mechanisms examined and rejected: (a) close_shift's FOR UPDATE (QA SHIFT-1) only serializes writes concurrent with the close instant, not later arrivals; (b) the cash ledger DOES have late-arrival machinery (posting.py _resolve_shift Case C: LATE_SYNC + LATE_SYNC_UNACK exception; Case D: OFF_SHIFT + UNRESOLVED_OFF_SHIFT), but it is gated by retrofit.dual_write_enabled (Postgres + cash schema + mode != LEGACY_ONLY) — SQLite/legacy tenants get nothing — and even when active, retrofit.on_cash_sale resolves the cash shift via _open_cash_shift_id (OPEN shifts only), so a post-close sale posts OFF_SHIFT with an exception not linked to the closed shift, and nothing ever revisits the frozen legacy Z-report; FRESH_PRODUCTION_LAUNCH.md line 166 itself states the full LATE_SYNC approval workflow is post-launch work. The invariant ("no accepted transaction may retroactively belong to a frozen shift without a visible reconciliation adjustment or exception") is therefore violated on the legacy side by code reading alone: the sale is accepted, bound to the closed shift, and no adjustment/exception exists in the legacy schema. The finding's scoping is accurate.
verdicts.protective_constraint_found: Partial only: (1) client-side outbox gate packages/shared/src/screens/Shift.tsx:246 — per-device localStorage, bypassable by second device/tab/direct API; (2) close_shift FOR UPDATE — serializes only concurrent commits at close time; (3) ledger-side posting.py _resolve_shift LATE_SYNC/OFF_SHIFT exception rows — active only for dual_write_enabled tenants (Postgres + cash schema + non-LEGACY_ONLY mode), and on_cash_sale passes only the OPEN cash shift id (retrofit.py _open_cash_shift_id), so the post-close sale lands OFF_SHIFT with an exception not linked to the closed shift; the frozen legacy Shift.expected_cash/difference is never revisited in any tenant mode. None prevents the attack.
verdicts.repro_hint: SQLite TestClient at 482b3f38: enable security.force_shift; open a shift (POST /shifts/open), note t1 inside it; close it (POST /shifts/{id}/close, counted_cash=opening) and record expected_cash; then POST /api/v1/sync/push with one cash sale {client_uuid, sold_at=t1, payment_method:"cash", items:[...]}. Assert response ok:true; Sale.shift_id equals the closed shift id; Shift.expected_cash/difference unchanged (excludes the sale); GET /shifts/{id}/summary returns the frozen expected while a SalePayment sum filtered by Sale.shift_id includes the late cash amount — permanent divergence with no exception row anywhere in the legacy schema.

verdicts.reasoning: The finding's central claim — "the only thing preventing close-before-sync is a client-side localStorage check (Shift.tsx:246)" — is false at SHA 482b3f38. There is a dedicated server-side guard the finder missed: `reject_closed_shift_replay` in apps/server/app/services/cash/cutover_guard.py (§9). Execution order in `_create_sale_once` (apps/server/app/services/sales.py): (1) the QA PAY-02 honor lookup may select a CLOSED shift (`closed_at >= sold_at`); (2) for any cash sale on a cash-enabled DB, `_cg.require_post_t0_till(..., shift=shift, till_id=_till_id)` runs BEFORE the `Sale(...)` object is even constructed; (3) `require_post_t0_till` calls `reject_closed_shift_replay(db, company_id=..., shift=shift, ...)`, which raises 400 with stable code `CLOSED_SHIFT_CASH_REPLAY_REQUIRES_RECOVERY` when `shift.status == closed` or `closed_at is not None`. Nothing is written — no Sale, no SalePayment, no ledger leg, no stock movement. `/sync/push` (apps/server/app/api/v1/sync.py:65-76) isolates the 400 as `ok:false` + the stable code, and the POS dead-letters it with a visible red badge (documented in app/db/cash/FRESH_PRODUCTION_LAUNCH.md §5a). Enforcement is keyed to SERVER receive time (`enforcement_active` reads only `cutover_at`; client `sold_at` explicitly cannot open the gate), so a backdating cashier cannot bypass it. The exact attack in the finding (queue offline cash sales on POS-1, close from POS-2, replay later) is therefore rejected server-side on any enforcement-active (post-T0 / ledger-native) tenant, and this is pinned by a dedicated test file at this SHA, apps/server/tests/test_offline_shift_policy_pg.py, which asserts both the rejection and that the rejection writes nothing. Residual scope, correctly bounded: (a) pre-T0 tenants (`cutover_at` unset) and SQLite dev DBs (no cash schema, so `require_post_t0_till` is never reached) do accept the replay into the closed legacy shift with frozen expected_cash — but this is the documented, deliberate legacy-compatibility state the migration exists to repair (T0_CUTOVER_ENFORCEMENT.md §9, and the test file's own docstring records the cash-already-taken residue as an open, owner-decision risk), not a silent hole: the shift summary endpoint (shifts.py ~204-233) recomputes by_method/naqd_sales live from SalePayment while `expected` stays frozen, so a late sale shows up as a divergence inside the same Z-report payload; and on SHADOW dual-write tenants the late leg additionally creates an OPEN CashLedgerException (posting.py `_resolve_shift` Cases B/C/D: LATE_SYNC_UNACK / TIMESTAMP_OUT_OF_WINDOW / UNRESOLVED_OFF_SHIFT). (b) Non-cash (card/QR) replays still bind to a closed shift, but SalePayment with method_code != 'cash' never enters expected_cash, so the claimed cash-reconciliation invariant is untouched. The finding's suggested repro (SQLite + force_shift) would go green only because SQLite has no cash schema — it exercises the deliberately unguarded dev/legacy mode and proves nothing about the production cash regime, a point the repo's own test docstring makes explicitly.
verdicts.protective_constraint_found: cutover_guard.reject_closed_shift_replay (apps/server/app/services/cash/cutover_guard.py:207), invoked from require_post_t0_till which sales.py `_create_sale_once` calls for every cash sale before the Sale row is created: post-T0 (server-receive-time enforcement), a cash replay into a closed/reconciled shift is rejected 400 `CLOSED_SHIFT_CASH_REPLAY_REQUIRES_RECOVERY`, /sync/push returns ok:false+code, POS dead-letters it visibly; pinned by apps/server/tests/test_offline_shift_policy_pg.py, which also asserts the rejection writes nothing (no double-entry on retry).
verdicts.repro_hint: To watch the guard: Postgres-backed test in apps/server/tests/test_offline_shift_policy_pg.py (open shift with till, set tenant cutover_at (T0) in the past, close shift, call create_sale with honor_price_snapshot=True and at inside the closed window; expect HTTPException 400 with X-Error-Code CLOSED_SHIFT_CASH_REPLAY_REQUIRES_RECOVERY and zero new Sale/ledger/stock rows). The finding's SQLite repro only demonstrates the documented pre-T0/legacy-compat path where the cash subsystem intentionally does not exist.

findings.title: /sync/push classifies non-OperationalError infrastructure failures as PERMANENT, dead-lettering money-captured offline sales
findings.claim: The per-record triage treats only HTTPException(409/5xx) and sqlalchemy.exc.OperationalError as transient. Any other DB-layer failure — sqlalchemy.exc.InterfaceError (connection already closed), sqlalchemy.exc.TimeoutError (pool checkout timeout under load), PendingRollbackError, non-Operational DBAPIError disconnect wrappers — falls into the bare `except Exception` branch, which returns ok:false with NO retry flag. flushOutbox then moves the record to the dead-letter list and removes it from the outbox (`else if (deadLetter(i, ...)) outboxRemove(i.client_uuid)`), so a sale for which cash was physically taken is dropped from automatic replay because of a transient infrastructure hiccup.
findings.invariant: A money-captured offline sale may only be dead-lettered for a deterministic business rejection; any failure that could succeed on retry must keep it in the outbox.
findings.attack_scenario: During a Railway/Postgres restart mid-batch, record N's failure invalidates the connection; record N+1's first query raises InterfaceError('connection already closed') or the pool is saturated and raises sqlalchemy.exc.TimeoutError. Server replies {ok:false, error:'server'} with no retry; the client dead-letters the sale. Cashier sees 'N rad etildi' and must manually re-enter the receipt (or lose it) although a retry 30 s later would have succeeded.
findings.evidence: sync.py: `except OperationalError: db.rollback(); results.append({..., "retry": True, ...})` followed by `except Exception:  # DataError ... db.rollback(); results.append({..., "ok": False, "error": "server"})` — the intent comment names DataError (genuinely permanent) but the catch is Exception-wide; InterfaceError/TimeoutError are not OperationalError subclasses in SQLAlchemy.
findings.suggested_repro: Monkeypatch create_sale to raise sqlalchemy.exc.InterfaceError('x','y',Exception()) for one record; assert the result row has ok:false and no retry:true (client-side: assert flushOutbox dead-letters it).

verdicts.reasoning: See verdict reasoning above.
verdicts.protective_constraint_found: Partial only: (a) create_sale's IntegrityError->409 retry wrapper and the lot-invariant 409 keep those specific failures transient; (b) pool_pre_ping=True reduces stale-connection errors at checkout; (c) whole-request errors keep the chunk in the outbox; (d) dead-letter is visible to the cashier, not silent. None of these prevents a per-record sqlalchemy.exc.TimeoutError / InterfaceError / PendingRollbackError from taking the bare-except -> no-retry -> deadLetter+outboxRemove path.
verdicts.repro_hint: Server-side (no PG needed): in a TestClient test, monkeypatch app.api.v1.sync.create_sale to raise sqlalchemy.exc.TimeoutError() (or InterfaceError("stmt", None, Exception())) for one record of a two-record /sync/push batch; assert that record's result row is {"ok": false, "error": "server"} with no "retry" key while the other is accepted. Client-side (vitest): mock post to return that results array and assert flushOutbox calls outboxRemove for the failed client_uuid and it appears in failedSales(). Fix direction: catch (OperationalError, InterfaceError, TimeoutError, PendingRollbackError) — or any DBAPIError with connection_invalidated — as retry:true, leaving only genuinely deterministic errors (DataError, StatementError with data cause) as permanent.

verdicts.reasoning:
The defect is real and provable by reading code plus library class hierarchies, though the finding's headline scenario (InterfaceError during a Postgres restart) is largely neutralized by runtime reality; a different transient class makes the broken path concrete.

CONFIRMED broken path (static):
1. Server ladder (apps/server/app/api/v1/sync.py, push): `except HTTPException` (retry only for 409/5xx) -> `except OperationalError` (retry:true) -> bare `except Exception` -> `{"ok": False, "error": "server"}` with NO retry flag. Verified against the audited SHA 482b3f38.
2. Class hierarchy (verified by executing against the project's installed SQLAlchemy): `sqlalchemy.exc.TimeoutError` MRO = TimeoutError->SQLAlchemyError; `InterfaceError` = DBAPIError->StatementError->SQLAlchemyError; `PendingRollbackError` = InvalidRequestError->SQLAlchemyError. None subclass OperationalError, so all land in the bare except.
3. Reachability of a genuinely transient failure in that branch: `create_sale` commits per record (apps/server/app/services/sales.py:737), releasing the pooled connection; the next record's first statement re-checks-out a connection INSIDE the per-record try. apps/server/app/db/session.py configures QueuePool with pool_size=15, max_overflow=25, pool_timeout=30 and its own comment admits QueuePool checkout timeout happens under high concurrency ("yuqori konkurentlikда QueuePool timeout -> 500"). A saturated pool (>30 s) raises `sqlalchemy.exc.TimeoutError` — raised by SQLAlchemy itself, no DBAPI wrapping — which is classified PERMANENT. This is transient by definition (a retry after load subsides succeeds), violating the stated invariant.
4. Client consequence confirmed (packages/shared/src/lib/sync.ts, flushOutbox ~line 185-191): for a result row with ok:false and no retry, `else if (deadLetter(i, ...)) outboxRemove(i.client_uuid)` moves the money-captured sale to the failed list and removes it from automatic replay; only manual cashier action remains. The response is HTTP 200, so the whole-request catch (which preserves the outbox) does not apply.

REFUTED sub-claims (narrowing severity context): the Railway-restart/InterfaceError leg is weak at runtime. The engine URL is normalized to `postgresql+psycopg` (psycopg v3), which raises psycopg.OperationalError — not InterfaceError — for "the connection is closed", broken sockets mid-query, admin_shutdown (57P01), and fresh connect failures; SQLAlchemy wraps those as sqlalchemy.exc.OperationalError -> retry:true. `pool_pre_ping=True` additionally recovers stale pooled connections at checkout, and a failed pre-ping reconnect also surfaces as OperationalError. So the common restart interleaving is correctly classified transient. The psycopg2-flavored InterfaceError('connection already closed') cited in the finding does not occur with this driver. PendingRollbackError is also hard to reach because every except branch rollbacks before the next record.

Net: the invariant "any failure that could succeed on retry must keep it in the outbox" is violated by at least one concrete, codebase-acknowledged transient failure (pool checkout TimeoutError), so the P1 stands with a corrected mechanism.
verdicts.protective_constraint_found: Partial protections that narrow but do not close the hole: (a) driver is psycopg v3 (apps/server/app/db/session.py _normalize -> postgresql+psycopg), whose disconnect/closed-connection/connect-failure errors are OperationalError -> caught by the `except OperationalError` retry branch; (b) pool_pre_ping=True heals stale connections at checkout; (c) client-side: a whole-request failure (network/5xx on /sync/push itself) never dead-letters. None of these covers sqlalchemy.exc.TimeoutError (pool checkout timeout), which SQLAlchemy raises directly and which the bare `except Exception` classifies as permanent.
verdicts.repro_hint: Server-side unit test, no Postgres needed: in a TestClient test of POST /api/v1/sync/push with 1 valid offline sale, monkeypatch app.api.v1.sync.create_sale to raise sqlalchemy.exc.TimeoutError('QueuePool limit reached, connection timed out') (also parametrize with sqlalchemy.exc.InterfaceError('stmt', None, Exception()) and PendingRollbackError()). Assert response 200 with results[0].ok is False and 'retry' absent/falsey — that row is what packages/shared/src/lib/sync.ts flushOutbox (line ~191) dead-letters and outboxRemove's. Fix expectation: retry:true for any SQLAlchemyError that is not DataError/IntegrityError/ProgrammingError (or invert: permanent only for a deterministic allowlist).
verdicts.reasoning_note: verdict basis: exception ladder + verified class MROs + per-record commit/checkout cycle + client dead-letter branch

findings.title: LATE_SYNC ledger entries are created automatically with no authorization, and LATE_SYNC_UNACK exceptions are write-only (no API reads or acknowledges them)
findings.claim: posting.py:339 returns `CashPostingKind.LATE_SYNC.value, cand.id, ["LATE_SYNC_UNACK"]` for any posting whose origin shift closed under the lock while device_ts is in-window — reachable by any kassa.sell holder whose sale/cash-op races a close, with no operator approval or custody evidence. T0_CUTOVER_ENFORCEMENT.md:177 states there is 'deliberately no automatic path' to LATE_SYNC and a future recovery workflow 'would verify operator approval'. Worse, the LATE_SYNC_UNACK/TIMESTAMP_OUT_OF_WINDOW/UNRESOLVED_OFF_SHIFT exception rows written by _persist are referenced by NO API route: grep for CashLedgerException across apps/server/app hits only cash_ddl_v1.sql, models/cash.py, posting.py, compare_engine.py and db_fingerprint.py — no endpoint lists, surfaces, or acknowledges them, so entries posted into closed/audited shifts remain invisible to operators.
findings.invariant: A ledger entry attributed to a CLOSED shift must require attestation, or at minimum its anomaly marker must be surfaced to an operator who can acknowledge it.
findings.attack_scenario: A cash op or sale posting races close_shift: the leg lands as LATE_SYNC on the closed cash shift with an OPEN LATE_SYNC_UNACK exception. No Manager screen, report, or endpoint ever shows the exception; the closed shift's reconciliation stays as-is; the anomaly is only discoverable by raw SQL. Money attribution changes retroactively in an audited period with zero operator visibility, contradicting the documented cutover contract.
findings.evidence: posting.py `_resolve_shift`: `if cand.status == ...OPEN...` else `if in_win: return CashPostingKind.LATE_SYNC.value, cand.id, ["LATE_SYNC_UNACK"]`; _persist: `db.add(CashLedgerException(..., state="OPEN", ...))`; git grep CashLedgerException over apps/server/app/api returns nothing.

verdicts.reasoning:
The finding's attack ("any kassa.sell holder posts into a closed/audited shift with no authorization, invisibly changing audited money attribution") is blocked or defused by four concrete mechanisms present at 482b3f38.

1) Deliberate replay into a closed shift is rejected BEFORE the posting service is ever reached. `apps/server/app/services/cash/cutover_guard.py` `reject_closed_shift_replay` (line ~207) raises `CLOSED_SHIFT_CASH_REPLAY_REQUIRES_RECOVERY` when the target shift is closed, and it is invoked from BOTH central custody roots that every physical-cash writer must pass (`require_post_t0_till` line 318 — used by `services/sales.py:189` and `cutover_open_shift_gate`; `resolve_cash_custody` line 389 — used by cashops/customers/purchases/receiving). So a cashier cannot choose a closed shift as a target; the doc claim in T0_CUTOVER_ENFORCEMENT.md §5e ("no automatic path") refers to exactly this replay case, and the code enforces it. Case C in `posting.py:_resolve_shift` is reachable only through the genuine in-flight race: the request passed the guard while the shift was OPEN and `close_shift` won the `CashShift ... with_for_update()` lock first. That race outcome is intentional, adversarially-reviewed design (posting.py module docstring: "sale-vs-close race — adversarial review CRITICAL") and is pinned by tests (`tests/cash/test_posting_service.py:206-207, 441, 496-498` assert ON_SHIFT-or-LATE_SYNC as the two legal race outcomes).

2) No authorization is bypassed. A Case C posting already passed step-1 `_authorize` plus the custody guards while the shift was open — it is a legitimately accepted sale/cash-op whose cash leg must land somewhere, or committed source rows would exist without a ledger leg (the exact silent-loss state `require_ledger_writable` exists to prevent, FRESH_PRODUCTION_LAUNCH.md §6). LATE_SYNC records real money with an explicit anomaly marker; rejecting it would lose custody of real cash.

3) The audited reconciliation does NOT change retroactively. `close_shift` (`services/cash/lifecycle.py`) locks the CashShift FOR UPDATE and snapshots expected = `repo.shift_expected_cash`, which filters `posting_kind == ON_SHIFT` only (`repositories.py:86-95`; same for `shift_movement_total`, and tenant.py's Z-report path). A later LATE_SYNC entry never enters the closed shift's expected/reconciliation record — satisfying the doc's own invariant "never rewrite the closed reconciliation". The finding's core harm ("money attribution changes retroactively in an audited period") is therefore false for the reconciliation; the entry only carries shift_id as flagged attribution metadata.

4) The anomaly is not "only discoverable by raw SQL". `CashLedgerException(state='OPEN')` rows are durable, LATE_SYNC entries have a dedicated partial index (`cash_ddl_v1.sql:493 cle_ix_late_sync`), and operator tooling reads them: `app/services/cash/compare_engine.py exception_counts` (lines 236-252) groups exceptions by kind/state and its report prints LATE_SYNC counts (line 319), exposed via the operator CLIs `app/tools/cash_compare.py` (line 48 prints off_shift/late_sync counts) and `app/tools/cash_preflight.py`; PRODUCTION_CASH_MIGRATION_RUNBOOK.md:133 lists "LATE_SYNC, open exceptions" among preflight alerts. Additionally, FRESH_PRODUCTION_LAUNCH.md §5a explicitly documents the residual scope as accepted, bounded post-launch work: "A full LATE_SYNC approval workflow remains post-launch work; the launch-safe bar — rejected, preserved, visible, no reconciliation rewritten — is met."

Residual truth in the finding, for the record: there is indeed no Manager-facing API route that lists or acknowledges `LATE_SYNC_UNACK` rows (grep confirms no `CashLedgerException` reference under `apps/server/app/api`), and `PostingResult.exceptions` is not logged by callers. But this is a documented, deliberately deferred workflow with operator-CLI visibility, guarded to a rare benign race whose net cash effect is correct and whose audited reconciliation is provably untouched — not the P2 "unauthorized, invisible, retroactive attribution change" the finding alleges. The concrete attack cannot be made real: the attacker cannot target a closed shift (guard), cannot move the reconciliation (ON_SHIFT filter under the same lock), and the marker is durable and counted by existing tooling.
verdicts.protective_constraint_found: reject_closed_shift_replay (cutover_guard.py:207, called from require_post_t0_till:318 and resolve_cash_custody:389) rejects any request targeting a closed shift before source mutation; close_shift/posting serialize on CashShift FOR UPDATE and shift_expected_cash counts ON_SHIFT only (repositories.py:86-95), so LATE_SYNC never alters a closed reconciliation; durable OPEN CashLedgerException + cle_ix_late_sync index surfaced by compare_engine.exception_counts via app/tools/cash_compare.py and cash_preflight alerts.
verdicts.repro_hint: To exercise the only remaining path: run two sessions against Postgres — session A calls close_shift(shift) and holds the transaction after acquiring the CashShift FOR UPDATE; session B submits a cash sale for that shift (guard passes while status is OPEN in B's snapshot before A commits); after A commits, B's posting resolves Case C: assert entry.posting_kind=='LATE_SYNC', reconciliation record unchanged, and one CashLedgerException(kind='LATE_SYNC_UNACK', state='OPEN'). This mirrors tests/cash/test_posting_service.py:441-498.

findings.title: Sale idempotency has no material-match: a reused client_uuid with a DIFFERENT payload is answered ok:true with the first sale, and the client permanently discards the second sale
findings.claim: The idempotency short-circuit `db.query(Sale).filter(Sale.client_uuid == data.client_uuid, Sale.company_id == emp.company_id).first(); if existing: return existing` compares nothing material (items, totals, payment method, cashier). /sync/push reports ok:true with the existing sale's id/receipt_no, and flushOutbox removes the outbox entry on ok:true. Cash movements were hardened against exactly this (shifts.py add_cash_movement material-match + IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED 409, with a comment explaining that answering 'duplicate' for a different operation loses real money); sales were not.
findings.invariant: An idempotent 'duplicate' answer may only be given when the stored record materially matches the submitted one; a key collision with different material fields must be an error, not success.
findings.attack_scenario: A cloned POS image, a localStorage restore, or a client bug reuses an outbox entry's client_uuid for a different basket (or a second cashier replays a uuid already used in the company). The server returns ok:true with the FIRST sale; the client deletes the second, materially different, money-captured sale from the outbox. No dead-letter, no error, no audit row — a silent lost sale of the exact class the cash-op hardening was built to prevent.
findings.evidence: sales.py: `existing = db.query(Sale).filter(Sale.client_uuid == data.client_uuid, Sale.company_id == emp.company_id).first(); if existing: return existing` vs shifts.py: `if _mv0 is not None and _CPV.cash_movement_matches(...): return {"ok": True, "duplicate": True}` else `raise HTTPException(409, _CASHOPS.KEY_REUSED_TEXT, headers=EC.headers(EC.IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED))`.
findings.suggested_repro: TestClient: POST /sync/push sale {client_uuid=U, items=[A]}, then push {client_uuid=U, items=[B], different total}; assert second result is ok:true with the FIRST sale's id and that no second sale/stock movement exists.

verdicts.reasoning:
The full broken path is provable by reading code at 482b3f38, and no protective constraint exists for sales.

1) Server short-circuit compares nothing material. apps/server/app/services/sales.py, _create_sale_once: `existing = db.query(Sale).filter(Sale.client_uuid == data.client_uuid, Sale.company_id == emp.company_id).first(); if existing: return existing`. No comparison of items, totals, payment_method, cashier, or anything else. Sale.client_uuid comes from SyncMixin (apps/server/app/db/base.py) with no unique constraint and no content hash; the only Sale table constraint is UniqueConstraint("company_id","receipt_no") (apps/server/app/models/sales.py:16), irrelevant here.

2) /sync/push reports the collision as success. apps/server/app/api/v1/sync.py push(): the returned existing sale is counted `accepted += 1` and answered `{"ok": True, "receipt_no": sale.receipt_no, "id": str(sale.id)}` — the code comment even states that on a repeated client_uuid the EXISTING sale's id is returned ("Takror `client_uuid` da ham — mavjud sotuv id'si").

3) Client permanently discards on ok:true. packages/shared/src/lib/sync.ts flushOutbox(): `if (r.ok) { outboxRemove(i.client_uuid); ... }`. Dead-letter (deadLetter(...)) runs only on ok:false; ok:true is treated as "qabul qilindi / idempotent dublikat". So a second, materially different, money-captured sale is deleted from the outbox with no error, no dead-letter entry, no server row.

Protective-constraint hunt (all negative for sales, positive for siblings — proving the invariant is an established codebase standard that sales missed):
- Cash ops: apps/server/app/api/v1/shifts.py:146-156 and 171 call _CPV.cash_movement_matches(...) (apps/server/app/services/cash/custody_preview.py:337-345) and raise 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED on a material mismatch.
- Inventory receiving: apps/server/app/models/inventory.py:372-379 has `request_hash` — request CONTENT hash — with a unique index ("ux_lsr_request_client", company_id+client_uuid) and a comment explicitly about the same client_uuid arriving with DIFFERENT content.
- Sales: no sale_matches helper, no request_hash, no 409 path — `git grep` for any material-match in sales.py/sync.py returns nothing.

The precondition (a client_uuid reused for a different basket: cloned localStorage, restore, client bug, or another cashier in the same company since the check is company-scoped, not device-scoped) is a client anomaly, which is why this is P2 rather than P1 — but the server-side invariant violation and the silent-loss path are unconditional once the collision occurs. This is exactly the failure class the cash-op hardening was written to prevent.
verdicts.protective_constraint_found: None for sales. Contrast mechanisms that DO exist elsewhere: shifts.py cash_movement_matches + 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED (cash ops); inventory.py request_hash + ux_lsr_request_client unique index (receiving). Sale has neither a material-match nor a content hash; UniqueConstraint(company_id, receipt_no) does not apply.
verdicts.repro_hint: TestClient, single tenant, open shift: POST /sync/push {"sales":[{"client_uuid":"U","items":[{product A, qty 1}],"payment_method":"cash",...}]} -> ok:true, capture id/receipt_no. Then POST /sync/push {"sales":[{"client_uuid":"U","items":[{product B, qty 3}],"payment_method":"card", different total}]} -> assert results[0].ok is True AND results[0].id == first sale's id; assert Sale count for company == 1 and no stock_movement for product B. (Same via POST /sales, since SaleCreate.client_uuid is accepted on the online path too.)

findings.title: sold_at is client-trusted within a 60-day backdating window, letting any kassa.sell holder inject sales into past days and past (closed) shifts
findings.claim: _clamp_sold_at accepts any sold_at in [now-60d, now+5m]. On /sync/push the sale is then written with sold_at as its business timestamp and bound to whichever historical shift of that cashier covers it. There is no marker distinguishing 'genuinely late-synced' from 'fabricated late' beyond is_offline=True, which the code itself notes is written but never read anywhere ('is_offline bayrog'i bugun HECH QAYERDA o'qilmaydi'); only price diffs and lot shortfalls are audit-logged, not the time skew. The P9 DEVICE_CLOCK_UNRELIABLE check runs only in offline-sale-policy (client advisory, only when force_shift is on and client_time supplied) — it does not constrain /sync/push itself.
findings.invariant: Retroactive writes into closed reporting periods must be bounded tightly and flagged for review; the acceptance window for replayed timestamps should be commensurate with realistic offline durations, not 60 days.
findings.attack_scenario: A cashier crafts a /sync/push (kassa.sell token) with sold_at 45 days ago: the sale lands in that day's revenue and, if the timestamp falls inside one of their old shifts' windows, in that closed shift — silently rewriting historical daily/Z reports long after the owner reviewed them. Combined with honor_price_snapshot the unit_price is also attacker-chosen, and the stock guard is bypassed (offline replay skips the availability check).
findings.evidence: sync.py: `if dt > now + timedelta(minutes=5) or dt < now - timedelta(days=60): return None; return dt`; sales.py: `sale = Sale(..., sold_at=now, is_offline=honor_price_snapshot, ...)` with `now = at or _now()`; honor path takes `it.unit_price` as the written price and `if qty > available ... and not honor_price_snapshot` skips the stock guard.

verdicts.reasoning: See verdict reasoning field.
verdicts.protective_constraint_found: Partial only: (1) force_shift rejects backdated sales whose sold_at falls outside every shift of that cashier (sales.py QA OFF-4) — constrains the timestamp to the attacker's own past shift windows, does not prevent the attack; (2) for CASH legs with cash dual-write enabled, posting.py::_resolve_shift books the out-of-window amount OFF_SHIFT with an OPEN TIMESTAMP_OUT_OF_WINDOW / UNRESOLVED_OFF_SHIFT CashLedgerException — a detective flag, but ops-tool-visible only (compare_engine), absent for card/QR/credit and for cash-disabled deployments. No mechanism bounds the 60-day window or flags the Sale itself.
verdicts.repro_hint: With a kassa.sell token whose cashier has a closed shift ~45 days old: POST /api/v1/sync/push {"sales":[{"client_uuid":"<new uuid4>","sold_at":"<inside that shift's window>","payment_method":"card","items":[{"product_id":"<pid>","qty":1,"unit_price":999999}]}]} -> expect 200 ok:true; then verify Sale.shift_id equals the closed shift's id, sold_at is the backdated value, and the daily sales report for that past day changed, with no audit row or exception referencing the time skew (audit only logs offline_price_snapshot diffs / sale_lot_shortfall).

findings.title: Permanently failing 409 records retry forever with no backoff, cap, or escalation — the outbox re-runs the full sale transaction every 30 seconds indefinitely
findings.claim: All 409s are transient by contract (sync.py: `_transient = e.status_code >= 500 or e.status_code == 409`), including LOT_INVARIANT_BROKEN, which sales.py raises as 409 precisely so the record is never dead-lettered.
