The only guard is packages/shared/src/screens/Shift.tsx line 246 (`outboxAll().length > 0` blocks close), whose own comment (lines 243-245) admits it is "faqat ... UX qatlami" — a per-device localStorage check, invisible to the same cashier's session on another terminal. (4) No recovery path exists at this SHA for this rejection: T0_CUTOVER_ENFORCEMENT.md line 177 and the reject_closed_shift_replay docstring both say the LATE_SYNC recovery flow "alohida quriladi" (built later). posting.py::_resolve_shift Case C (line 339) can mint LATE_SYNC legs, but only for a sale already in flight during a concurrent close — a replay arriving after close commit is 400'd before any posting. Decisive evidence: apps/server/tests/test_offline_shift_policy_pg.py::test_post_t0_yopilgan_smenaga_naqd_replay_RAD_ETILADI executes the exact scenario (sale accepted while open, shift closed, same-window replay → 400 CLOSED_SHIFT_CASH_REPLAY_REQUIRES_RECOVERY, zero sales/ledger rows written) and its module docstring states the P9 gate "to'sa OLMAYDI" this and it stands as an open risk deferred to the owner. Two precision corrections to the finding, neither of which saves it: (a) a manager cannot close another cashier's shift via POST /shifts/{id}/close (404 on cashier_id mismatch) — the feasible vector is the SAME cashier closing from a second device/session whose local outbox is empty, or any use of the cashier's own token; (b) the offline_sale_policy route is not blind post-T0 — it returns BLOCKED for the deterministic cases (no shift → TILL_REQUIRED_AFTER_CUTOVER; till-less legacy shift), so the residual hole is precisely the temporal one the finding names: ALLOWED issued while the shift is open is not a durable guarantee, and the "NEGA OCHIQ SMENA YETARLI" comment block (shifts.py ~350-360) states a closed-later shift still accepts the replay, which is true pre-T0 but false for post-T0 cash. Note for the report: this is a documented, deliberately accepted fail-closed trade-off (no silent cash writes into a reconciled shift, no auto-duplication from dead-letter), not an unnoticed bug — but the invariant as stated (honestly captured cash must eventually be recordable) is genuinely violated: the original transaction can never be admitted server-side, the closed shift's Z-report keeps a phantom overage, and the sole evidence lives in clearable client localStorage.
verdicts.protective_constraint_found: Partial only: (1) client-side close block Shift.tsx:246 — per-device, bypassed by cross-device close; (2) offline_sale_policy BLOCKs the deterministic post-T0 rejection cases and close_shift clears the cached ALLOWED (Shift.tsx:256); (3) close_shift ownership check limits the closer to the shift's own cashier; (4) posting.py Case C LATE_SYNC covers only the concurrent sale-vs-close race, not post-close replays. None prevents the described loss.
verdicts.repro_hint: Already reproduced in-repo: apps/server/tests/test_offline_shift_policy_pg.py::test_post_t0_yopilgan_smenaga_naqd_replay_RAD_ETILADI (requires real Postgres with cash schema; SQLite skips the guard entirely). For the cross-device variant: same cashier token, open till-bound shift post-T0, sell via /sync/push payload held back; POST /shifts/{id}/close from a second session (server accepts — no pending check); then push the held replay with sold_at inside the window → 400 CLOSED_SHIFT_CASH_REPLAY_REQUIRES_RECOVERY, retry absent/false, no Sale/ledger row.

findings.title: Malformed cutover_at silently disables ALL post-T0 cash enforcement (fail-open config parse)
findings.claim: cutover_at parses Setting(key='cash').value['cutover_at'] with fromisoformat and returns None on any parse failure. None means 'no cutover' throughout: enforcement_active → False, cutover_reached → False. A corrupted or mistyped value (e.g. an operator edit through any settings write path, or a serialization change) therefore reverts the whole tenant to pre-T0 legacy custody — no TILL requirement, no closed-shift replay rejection — with zero error, zero log line.
findings.invariant: Project rule (fail-open-defaults memory + cutover_guard's own §6 doctrine): an unreadable/invalid security-relevant setting must never grant permission; a tenant that once crossed T0 must not silently fall back to legacy behavior.
findings.attack_scenario: Post-T0 tenant. cutover_at value becomes non-ISO (typo via a raw settings update, defective client, or migration re-encode). From the next request on, every guard in cutover_guard.py returns pre-T0 behavior: cash sales/ops with till_id NULL are accepted again, closed-shift replays are accepted (finding 1's P0 channel reopens), while readiness/compare tooling still believes T0 was set. Nothing alerts anyone.
findings.evidence: cutover.py:24-36: bare `except (ValueError, TypeError): return None` with no logging; enforcement_active (cutover_guard.py) treats None as 'legacy rejim (butun tenant)'. Contrast with cutover_guard._fail which logs every refusal — parse failure of the very switch that arms those refusals is silent.

verdicts.protective_constraint_found: Settings-key whitelist in apps/server/app/api/v1/settings.py: put_setting -> _validate_value accepts only {tax, payments, security, features, store_info, receipt} and ends with `raise HTTPException(400, f"Noma'lum sozlama kaliti: {key}")`, so key='cash' is unwritable through the settings API (plan/suspended additionally 403). The sole application writer of Setting(key='cash'), tenant.mark_ledger_native (apps/server/app/services/cash/tenant.py), writes `datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()` — always fromisoformat-parseable — and is insert-only/idempotent: it returns an existing row untouched, so it can never re-encode or overwrite cutover_at. Every ops/migration tool at the SHA (cash_t0_probe.py, cash_runtime_readiness.py, cash_till_plan.py, migration CLI) explicitly never sets cutover_at.
verdicts.reasoning: The code pattern is real: cutover.py lines 33-36 swallow ValueError/TypeError and return None without logging, and cutover_guard.enforcement_active (line 201) treats None as legacy mode. But the finding's attack requires a malformed value to actually reach Setting(key='cash').value['cutover_at'], and no in-application channel can produce one: (1) PUT /settings rejects key='cash' outright via the key whitelist (no "settings write path" exists for it); (2) the only writer, mark_ledger_native, emits a guaranteed-valid isoformat string and never mutates an existing row; (3) catalog_import_v2's cutover_at lives under key='catalog' and is verified independent; receipt settings write only receipt keys; (4) no T0-setting tool or endpoint exists at this SHA for legacy tenants — corrupting the value requires a raw SQL edit on production, outside the application boundary, and that same operator could equally DELETE the row, which no parse hardening would defend. The finding's aggravating claim that "readiness/compare tooling still believes T0 was set" is factually wrong: runtime_readiness.py:226 and cash_t0_probe.py:46 call the same _cut.cutover_at parser, so a corrupted value shows as cutover_at=UNSET / enforcement=False in the ceremony's own verify probes (cash_runtime_readiness.py:136) — visible, not masked. Also, fresh ledger-native tenants (the only ones with cutover_at at this SHA) keep require_ledger_writable protection keyed off ledger_native:True in the same JSON at both guard roots, so ledger legs would still be written. Residual note: adding a warning log on parse failure is cheap defense-in-depth worth doing, but as a P2 attack finding it fails — the fail-open branch is unreachable through any concrete write path.
verdicts.repro_hint: Only reachable via out-of-band raw SQL: UPDATE settings SET value = jsonb_set(value,'{cutover_at}','"not-a-date"') WHERE key='cash'; then observe cash sale with till_id NULL accepted post-T0. No API/tool path produces this state; cash_t0_probe would immediately display cutover_at=UNSET.

findings.title: Legacy shift lifecycle endpoints have no permission gate: any authenticated employee can open a shift, seize a TILL, and write cash movements
findings.claim: POST /shifts/open (shifts.py:438), POST /shifts/{shift_id}/cash (shifts.py:49) and POST /shifts/{shift_id}/close (shifts.py:528) use only `Depends(get_current_employee)` (authentication + suspended check, core/deps.py:12-45) with no `require(...)` permission. Every other money-path in this area is permission-gated (POST /sales and /sync/push and GET /shifts/offline-sale-policy require kassa.sell; POST /cash/ops requires hisobot.view). So an active employee whose role has zero permissions (e.g. a stock clerk or report-only account) can: (a) open a legacy Shift, and post-T0 pass `till_id` of any TILL in their branch (validated only for tenant/branch, shifts.py:465-480), which then blocks the real cashier because open_shift rejects a second open shift on that TILL (shifts.py:493-497 'Bu kassa (TILL) band') and on_shift_open also occupies cash.shift via sh_one_open_per_account; (b) write payin/payout/expense/collection CashMovements plus real cash-ledger legs into that shift via add_cash_movement (payin is unbounded; outflows only capped by till formula). Because close_shift and add_cash_movement both enforce `s.cashier_id == emp.id` (shifts.py:59, 541) and the route list contains no manager force-close for legacy shifts (only cash-native lifecycle.reopen/assign on cash.shifts), nobody else can close the rogue shift via the API; if the employee is then deactivated their token is 401 and the TILL stays locked until DB surgery.
findings.invariant: Cash-custody actions (opening a shift on a physical till, recording cash movements) must be restricted to employees holding the cashier permission, and a seized till must be releasable by a manager/owner through the API.
findings.attack_scenario: Tenant with cutover reached (post-T0). Employee E has an active account with a permissionless role. E calls POST /shifts/open {till_id: <branch's TILL>} -> 200, shift S opened, legacy Shift.till_id set and cash.shift opened on the TILL. Real cashier C now gets 400 'Bu kassa (TILL) band' from /shifts/open; post-T0 cash sales requiring exact TILL custody are blocked on that drawer. E can additionally POST /shifts/{S}/cash {type:'payin', amount:900000} repeatedly, polluting cash reports and the append-only ledger. Only E can close S; firing E (status!=active) makes the shift permanently unclosable through the API.
findings.evidence: shifts.py:438 `def open_shift(data: OpenShift, emp: Employee = Depends(get_current_employee), ...)`; shifts.py:50-53 `def add_cash_movement(..., emp: Employee = Depends(get_current_employee), ...)`; shifts.py:540-541 close_shift: `if not s or s.cashier_id != emp.id: raise HTTPException(404, ...)`. Route inventory for the shifts router (git grep @router shifts.py) shows no other close/force-close/delete endpoint for legacy shifts. Contrast: sales.py:55 `Depends(require("kassa.sell"))`, shifts.py:381 offline_sale_policy `Depends(require("kassa.sell"))`.
findings.suggested_repro: SQLite TestClient: create employee with a role that has no permissions; POST /shifts/open -> expect 200 (should be 403); POST /shifts/{id}/cash {type:'payin',amount:100} -> 200. The post-T0 TILL-lock variant (cash schema + sh_one_open_per_account) needs PostgreSQL.

verdicts.protective_constraint_found: Partial only, and not for the core claim: employees.py `_has_open_shift` (lines 103-109, used at 477/516) blocks deactivating/deleting an employee with an open shift, preventing the "fired employee -> permanently unclosable shift" tail; and PATCH /employees/{id} credential reset (xodimlar.edit) provides an API-level recovery path (reset PIN, log in as the employee, close the shift). No mechanism restricts open_shift/add_cash_movement/close_shift to cashier-permission holders.
verdicts.repro_hint: SQLite TestClient: create role with zero permissions, active employee E on it; POST /shifts/open as E -> observe 200 (expected 403); POST /shifts/{id}/cash {"type":"payin","amount":100} -> 200. Also assert PATCH /employees/{E} {"status":"inactive"} -> 409/400 due to _has_open_shift, showing the rogue shift also blocks offboarding. Post-T0 till seizure (409 for the real cashier via shifts.py:493-497 and sh_one_open_per_account) needs PostgreSQL with cash schema and cutover reached.

verdicts.reasoning: duplicate-field-guard
verdicts.protective_constraint_found: Partial only: (a) employees.py `_has_open_shift` blocks deactivating an employee with an open shift, so the "fired employee => permanently unclosable shift" branch cannot occur via the API — but this inverts into "rogue shift-holder cannot be deactivated"; (b) recovery without DB surgery exists via owner resetting the rogue employee's credentials and closing the shift while logged in as them; (c) router-level subscription_gate exists but is subscription-status, not permission, enforcement. No constraint prevents the permissionless open/seize/payin path itself.
verdicts.repro_hint: SQLite TestClient at 482b3f38: seed company with a role having zero permissions, active employee E, one branch. As E: POST /api/v1/shifts/open {} -> expect 200 (defect; should be 403 without kassa.sell); POST /api/v1/shifts/{id}/cash {"type":"payin","amount":100} -> 200 and a CashMovement row with employee_id=E. Then as owner: PATCH deactivate E -> expect the _has_open_shift rejection (confirms no one else can ever close it while E holds it). The post-T0 TILL-block variant (shifts.py:493-497 rejecting the real cashier) needs PostgreSQL with cash schema enabled and cutover reached.

findings.title: Inter-branch transfer idempotency dedup is global (not company-scoped) and ignores material fields, silently dropping a real transfer as 'duplicate'
findings.claim: The dedup SELECT in _transfer_once (cashops.py:288-293) filters only `StockMovement.client_uuid == data.client_uuid AND type == transfer_out` — StockMovement has no company_id and the query does not join Branch to scope by tenant, and it does not compare material fields (items, branches, qty). Any pre-existing transfer_out row anywhere in the database with the same client_uuid — another tenant's, or the same tenant's earlier *different* transfer — makes the endpoint return {ok:true, duplicate:true} without moving any stock. The backing unique index ux_stockmov_client_prod_type is (client_uuid, product_id, type) with no company column (initdb.py:800-802), and after an IntegrityError the retry loop (transfer, cashops.py:265-276) re-runs the same unscoped SELECT, so the IE-recovery path misreports the same way. This is strictly weaker than the cash-movement paths, which re-verify company scope AND material match before saying 'duplicate' (shifts.py:145-149, cashops.py:180-195).
findings.invariant: Idempotency keys must be scoped to the company, and a request may only be answered 'duplicate' when the stored operation materially matches the retried one (mapper note and the sale/cash paths both implement this).
findings.attack_scenario: Smallest concrete case (same tenant, no collision luck needed): Manager client sends transfer T1 {uuid U, product P, qty 5, A->B}; commit succeeds but the response is lost. The operator edits the list and resubmits with the SAME uuid U but different content {product Q, qty 50, A->C} (or a buggy client reuses U). The server answers ok:true duplicate:true and moves nothing — the 50 units of Q are never transferred while the client marks the operation synced. Cross-tenant variant: if a transfer_out row with uuid U exists in tenant X, tenant Y's legitimate transfer with U is silently swallowed (v4 collision, negligible probability but a scope violation of the stated invariant).
findings.evidence: cashops.py:288-293: `ex = db.query(StockMovement).filter(StockMovement.client_uuid == data.client_uuid, StockMovement.type == MovementType.transfer_out).first(); if ex: return {"ok": True, "duplicate": True}` — no Branch/company join, no item comparison. initdb.py: `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ... ux_stockmov_client_prod_type ON stock_movements (client_uuid, product_id, type) WHERE client_uuid IS NOT NULL` (global).
findings.suggested_repro: TestClient: POST /inventory/transfer with uuid U (product P). Then POST again with uuid U but a different product/qty/branches. Second call returns duplicate:true and destination inventory for the new product is unchanged.

verdicts.reasoning: Every element of the claim is provable by reading the code at 482b3f38. (1) The dedup in _transfer_once (apps/server/app/api/v1/cashops.py) executes BEFORE the branch FOR UPDATE / company-ownership check and filters only StockMovement.client_uuid == data.client_uuid AND type == transfer_out, then returns {ok:true, duplicate:true}. (2) StockMovement (apps/server/app/models/inventory.py:519) has no company_id and the query joins nothing, so the match is global across tenants; a colliding uuid from another tenant short-circuits the request before the caller's branches are even validated. (3) The backing index ux_stockmov_client_prod_type (apps/server/app/initdb.py:800-802) is (client_uuid, product_id, type), no company column; worse, the dedup SELECT omits even product_id, so a reused uuid carrying a DIFFERENT product/qty/branches is answered duplicate:true and nothing moves — the DB index alone would have allowed that insert. (4) The IE-retry wrapper (transfer) just re-runs the same unscoped SELECT. (5) The invariant is the codebase's own: the writeoff dedup comment (apps/server/app/api/v1/inventory.py:205-209) explicitly names the missing company_id as a silent-swallow hazard and scopes by product_id, and both cash paths (shifts.py IE handler; cashops.py cash-op IE handler) do a company-scoped lookup plus cash_movement_matches material comparison, raising 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED on mismatch. The transfer path is strictly weaker than its siblings, exactly as claimed. I hunted for a protective server mechanism and found none — no trigger, no scoped index, no material check, no gate. The only mitigation is client-side: the sole first-party caller (apps/mobile/lib/screens/transfer_screen.dart via DraftUuid.forDraft, apps/mobile/lib/api.dart:1085) content-fingerprints the body and mints a new uuid whenever the draft changes, and freezes the draft after an unknown outcome. That makes the same-uuid-different-content scenario unreachable through the shipped PWA and leaves cross-tenant swallow at v4-collision probability — so real-world exploitation needs a buggy or third-party client — but it is not a server-side constraint, does not bind other API consumers, and the P2 severity (defense-in-depth/invariant violation, not an open exploit) is consistent with that.
verdicts.protective_constraint_found: Client-side only: DraftUuid.forDraft (apps/mobile/lib/api.dart:1085) regenerates client_uuid whenever the request body fingerprint changes, and transfer_screen.dart freezes the draft after an unknown outcome until explicit discard — so the first-party PWA cannot resubmit a different transfer under an old uuid. No server-side protection exists: no company scoping, no material-field comparison, no scoped unique index, no trigger.
verdicts.repro_hint: TestClient (SQLite fine, needs_pg=false): seed one company with branches A, B, C and untracked products P, Q with stock. POST /inventory/transfer {client_uuid: U, from: A, to: B, items:[{P, 5}]} -> ok. POST /inventory/transfer {client_uuid: U, from: A, to: C, items:[{Q, 50}]} -> expect {ok:true, duplicate:true}; assert Inventory(Q, C).qty unchanged and no transfer_out row for Q exists. Cross-tenant variant: insert a transfer_out StockMovement with client_uuid U under tenant X directly, then POST as tenant Y's employee with U -> duplicate:true despite tenant Y having no such movement.

findings.title: POST /cash/ops: a report-view permission authorizes cash-ledger writes into another cashier's open shift
findings.claim: cash_op is gated by `require("hisobot.view")` (cashops.py:70) — a read/report permission — yet it writes CashMovement rows and ledger legs. The target shift is resolved server-side as the newest open shift in the caller's branch regardless of who owns it (custody_preview.cash_op_shift, custody_preview.py:247-261; falls back to the company-wide newest open shift when the employee has no branch binding and actor_branch's last-resort fallback fails), so the caller writes into a shift whose cashier_id is someone else. That is intended for the owner's mobile app, but the chosen gate means any employee granted report viewing (a common grant for supervisors/accountants) can inject unlimited `payin` and up-to-till `expense`/`collection` into another cashier's shift, shifting that cashier's frozen expected_cash and Z-report difference without any cashier-level permission or the shift owner's involvement.
findings.invariant: Write operations against a cashier's cash custody should require a write-class permission (and arguably owner/manager role), not a report-view permission; permission semantics should distinguish reads from money writes.
findings.attack_scenario: Employee R holds only hisobot.view (given so they can see reports). Cashier C has the branch's open shift with a balanced till. R calls POST /cash/ops {type:'expense', amount:<till balance>, reason:'x'} -> 200, recorded in C's shift with employee_id=R. At close, C's expected_cash drops by that amount; if the physical money was not actually removed, C shows a fake overage — or R uses the record to cover a real removal. C never authorized or saw the operation at the time.
findings.evidence: cashops.py:70 `def cash_op(data: CashOpIn, emp: Employee = Depends(require("hisobot.view")), ...)`; custody_preview.py:247-261 cash_op_shift returns the latest open shift in the actor branch (`Shift.status == open`, ordered by opened_at desc) with no cashier_id constraint; cashops.py:150-152 `_mv = CashMovement(shift_id=shift.id, ..., employee_id=emp.id, ...)`.
findings.suggested_repro: TestClient: employee with only hisobot.view; another employee opens a shift with cash sales; the first calls POST /cash/ops expense for the full till amount -> 200; GET /shifts/{id}/summary as the cashier shows reduced expected.

verdicts.reasoning: See main reasoning field.
verdicts.protective_constraint_found: None on this path. The only ownership constraint (`Shift.cashier_id == emp.id`) lives in the sibling route POST /shifts/{shift_id}/cash (apps/server/app/api/v1/shifts.py:59) and in custody_preview.actor_open_shift — neither is used by POST /cash/ops. Bounding-only mitigations: expense/collection capped at current till balance (cashops.py till check); movement is attributed to the caller (employee_id=emp.id) and visible in GET /cash/ops — detection after the fact, not authorization.
verdicts.repro_hint: TestClient (SQLite is enough since custody ledger is a no-op there): seed a shop; create employee R with role "menejer" (has hisobot.view by default, no kassa.* perms); create cashier C and open a shift as C (POST /shifts/open) with opening_cash>0; as R call POST /api/v1/cash/ops {"type":"expense","amount":<till>,"client_uuid":...} -> expect 200 with shift_id == C's shift; then close the shift as C and assert expected_cash dropped by the amount (and that R gets 404 from POST /shifts/{id}/cash on the same shift, proving the sibling route's ownership check that /cash/ops lacks). Also assert R with type "payin", amount 1e9 -> 200 (unbounded expected_cash inflation).

findings.title: Another cashier's queued sales permanently block shift close and never flush
findings.claim: confirmClose gates shift close on the UNFILTERED outbox (`if (outboxAll().length > 0) { setErr(t("shift.syncFirst")); return; }`), but flushOutbox only sends records whose owner_id matches the logged-in cashier and usePendingCount hides other owners' records from the badge. A record owned by a cashier who never logs back into that device can never be flushed there, so every other cashier on the device is told 'finish sync first' forever and cannot close their shift; the stranded sale itself never reaches the server.
findings.invariant: A cashier must always be able to close their own shift once THEIR queue is drained; every captured offline sale must eventually be pushed or surfaced to someone who can act on it.
findings.attack_scenario: Cashier A sells offline (record queued with owner_id=A), logs out, quits/is reassigned. Cashier B logs in on the same POS: syncTick flushes nothing of A's (owner filter, sync.ts:160), pending badge shows 0 (filter at sync.ts:41), yet Shift.tsx confirmClose sees outboxAll().length==1 and refuses to close B's shift with shift.syncFirst — permanently, with no visible cause and no way to clear it from the UI. A's captured cash sale also never reaches the server (stock/cash/report loss until forensics on localStorage).
findings.evidence: Shift.tsx confirmClose: `if (outboxAll().length > 0) { setErr(t("shift.syncFirst")); return; }` (unfiltered). sync.ts:160 flush filter: `outboxAll().filter((i) => !i.owner_id || !me || i.owner_id === me)`. sync.ts:41 pending count uses the same owner filter, so the blocking record is invisible in the UI.
findings.suggested_repro: In pos-offline tests: queue one outbox record with owner_id='A', log in as employee 'B' with an open shift, run flushOutbox (record stays), then invoke the close handler — it errors with shift.syncFirst and never proceeds while the pending badge shows 0.

verdicts.reasoning: The broken path is fully provable by reading the SHA. (1) Gate: packages/shared/src/screens/Shift.tsx:246 in confirmClose checks the UNFILTERED device queue: `if (outboxAll().length > 0) { setErr(t("shift.syncFirst")); return; }` — the only client call site of POST /shifts/{id}/close in the repo (Shift.tsx:249; nothing in apps/mobile or Manager). (2) Flush: packages/shared/src/lib/sync.ts:160 filters `outboxAll().filter((i) => !i.owner_id || !me || i.owner_id === me)`; every record is captured with owner_id (submitSale), so with cashier B logged in, A's record is never sent and never removed (outboxRemove is called only inside flushOutbox). The `!me` branch cannot rescue it: no employee means no token, /sync/push gets 401, the chunk throws, nothing is removed. (3) Invisibility: usePendingCount (sync.ts:41) applies the identical owner filter (deliberate per the QA OFF-6 comment), so B sees pending=0 while close is refused. (4) No escape hatch: useAuth.logout (packages/shared/src/store/auth.ts) never touches the outbox; there is no TTL, no foreign-record UI, no reassignment; even an owner login on that device is owner-filtered out. The developer comment above the gate calls it "faqat UX qatlami", assuming the inspected queue equals the drainable queue — false since QA OFF-6. Only partial mitigation found: fleet.ts:63 heartbeat reports unfiltered pending_ops to server telemetry, which surfaces a stuck nonzero count to backoffice but neither flushes the sale nor unblocks the close, so both stated invariants (B can close a drained shift; captured sale reaches server or an actor) remain violated. Severity caveat: it is per-device recoverable if cashier A ever logs back into that device, and A's stranded sale survives in localStorage (not silently deleted); but under the finding's stated scenario (A never returns) the block is permanent from the UI.
verdicts.protective_constraint_found: None that refutes it. Closest candidates, all insufficient: (a) fleet heartbeat (packages/shared/src/lib/fleet.ts:63) sends the unfiltered pending_ops count to the server, making the stuck record visible as a number in backoffice telemetry only; (b) the record is retained (not lost) in namespaced localStorage and would flush if cashier A logged back into that same device; (c) dead-letter UI (failedSales/clearFailed) does not apply — the record is in the outbox, not the failed list. Logout does not flush, reassign, or clear outbox records; outboxRemove is reachable only through the owner-filtered flushOutbox.
verdicts.repro_hint: In packages/shared pos-offline vitest: seed localStorage outbox (key savdoos_outbox@<ns> via outboxAdd) with one record {client_uuid, payload, created_at, owner_id:'A'}; set useAuth state to employee B with kassa.sell and an open shift; run flushOutbox() against a mock /sync/push and assert no request contains A's record and outboxAll().length===1; assert usePendingCount getSnapshot ((outboxAll filtered by owner B).length) === 0; then invoke Shift.tsx confirmClose (render Shift with an open shift) and assert err === t('shift.syncFirst') and no POST to /shifts/{id}/close was made.

verdicts.reasoning: The set-mismatch is provable by reading three code sites at SHA 482b3f38. Gate: packages/shared/src/screens/Shift.tsx:246 in confirmClose checks the UNFILTERED queue — `if (outboxAll().length > 0) { setErr(t("shift.syncFirst")); return; }` — and early-returns on every attempt. Drain: packages/shared/src/lib/sync.ts flushOutbox sends only `outboxAll().filter((i) => !i.owner_id || !me || i.owner_id === me)`, so with cashier B logged in, A's record (owner_id='A') is never pushed. Visibility: usePendingCount (sync.ts, "QA OFF-6" comment) applies the identical owner filter, so the badge shows 0 while the blocking record exists. outboxRemove has exactly two call sites, both inside flushOutbox and both requiring the record to first be sent to the server (accept, or dead-letter after a per-record rejection); there is no other consumer and no UI to view or clear the outbox (clearFailed clears only the separate dead-letter key). Refutation attempts all fail: (1) logout (store/auth.ts) neither flushes nor gates on pending records, and AutoLogout.tsx logs A out automatically on inactivity, so the precondition arises without any deliberate act; (2) with nobody logged in the `!me` branch would include A's record, but /sync/push is authenticated — the tokenless request fails wholesale, catch does `break`, record stays; (3) the server can never rescue the sale because the owner filter exists precisely so sales leave only under their owner's token — if A never logs into that device again, the captured cash sale never reaches the server (stock/cash/report loss, recoverable only by localStorage forensics or A's return). Net effect: every other cashier on the device gets shift.syncFirst forever with a pending badge of 0 and no actionable path, violating both stated invariants. Only caveat vs. the finding's wording: the block is not cryptographically permanent — A logging in once on that device with network drains it — but in the stated scenario (A reassigned/quit) it is permanent in practice.
verdicts.protective_constraint_found: None. Logout does not flush or gate on pending outbox; AutoLogout can create the state unattended; no UI exists to surface or clear another owner's outbox records; outboxRemove is reachable only via a successful/answered push under the owner's own session; the tokenless `!me` flush path fails wholesale on the authenticated /sync/push route.
verdicts.repro_hint: In pos-offline vitest: seed localStorage outbox (namespaced key savdoos_outbox@<serverTag>) with one record {client_uuid, payload, created_at, owner_id:'A'}; set useAuth state to employee B with token; run flushOutbox against a mocked /sync/push that records calls — assert zero sales sent and record still present; assert usePendingCount snapshot returns 0; then render Shift close flow (or call confirmClose with an open shift) — assert setErr receives t('shift.syncFirst') and no POST to /shifts/{id}/close occurs.

findings.title: Dead-letter list capped at 200: overflow silently discards oldest money-captured rejected sales
findings.claim: deadLetter appends the rejected sale then writes `failed.slice(-200)`, silently dropping the oldest entries once more than 200 rejections accumulate. The dead-letter record (full payload) is the ONLY remaining trace of a sale that took money but was refused by the server, and the whole mechanism's stated contract is 'never silently lose'. deadLetter still returns true, so the caller also removes the sale from the outbox — the transaction record then exists nowhere.
findings.invariant: A server-rejected offline sale must remain inspectable until an operator explicitly clears it (the two-step clear in POSKassa exists precisely for this).
findings.attack_scenario: force_shift is enabled (or a catalog/validation change breaks queued payloads) while a store has a long outage backlog: flushOutbox replays 500 queued sales, all get permanent 400s, each is deadLetter()ed and outboxRemove()d. After the 201st rejection, entry 1 is silently evicted by slice(-200); by the end, 300 money-captured sales have no payload, no amount, no error text left anywhere — reconciliation is impossible and the cashier's 'N rad etildi' counter under-reports.
findings.evidence: sync.ts deadLetter: `failed.push({ ...item, error, code: code ?? null }); localStorage.setItem(FAILED_KEY_FN(), JSON.stringify(failed.slice(-200))); ... return true;` — true is returned even when the write evicted older entries, and flushOutbox then runs `outboxRemove(i.client_uuid)`.
findings.suggested_repro: Unit test: seed 200 entries in savdoos_outbox_failed@<tag>, call deadLetter once more, assert the first entry is gone while the function returned true.

verdicts.reasoning: The defect is provable by reading packages/shared/src/lib/sync.ts at 482b3f38. deadLetter() does `failed.push(...)` then `localStorage.setItem(FAILED_KEY_FN(), JSON.stringify(failed.slice(-200)))` and returns true unconditionally on a successful write — there is no length check, no overflow branch, no warning path. In flushOutbox the permanent-rejection branch is `else if (deadLetter(i, ...)) outboxRemove(i.client_uuid)`, so on the 201st cumulative rejection the oldest dead-letter entry is silently evicted while the newest sale is also removed from the outbox; the evicted sale (already outboxRemove'd when it was dead-lettered earlier) then exists nowhere on the client. I hunted for protective constraints and found none: (a) offline.ts outboxAdd has no cap, so a 500-sale backlog is representable; (b) the print journal (printing.ts LocalPrintJob, itself capped KEEP_JOBS=300) stores only doc ids/print status, never amounts or payloads, and only for sales where printing was attempted — it is not a reconciliation trace; (c) fleet.ts reports failed_ops = failedSales().length, i.e. the already-capped count, so telemetry under-reports identically; (d) clearFailed/POSKassa's two-step confirm protect against accidental manual clearing only, and the POSKassa comment explicitly states these records are the sole evidence ("yagona dalil") of money-taken-but-unrecorded sales — the exact invariant the cap violates. One material caveat on the attack narrative: the cited force_shift scenario is substantially pre-empted at this same SHA by the P9 gate (offlineSaleAllowed: fail-closed server confirmation with 8h TTL, and server-side historical-shift replay), so a single-outage 500-sale mass rejection via force_shift is unlikely. But permanent per-record rejections (ok:false without retry) from other validation causes still dead-letter, the list persists until explicit operator clear, and accumulation past 200 over time triggers unconditional silent eviction. The mechanism defect stands regardless of which rejection cause fills the list.
verdicts.protective_constraint_found: None for the cap itself. Partial mitigations only: (1) P9 offlineSaleAllowed gate (sync.ts) blocks the force_shift mass-rejection path before money is taken, reducing how fast the list fills; (2) QA OFF-3 false-return path protects against localStorage quota failure, not eviction; (3) flushing mutex prevents duplicate dead-letters. Nothing prevents or signals eviction at entry 201+.
verdicts.repro_hint: Unit test (vitest, jsdom): set localStorage key `savdoos_outbox_failed@<serverTag>` to a JSON array of 200 FailedSale entries with distinct client_uuids; invoke the flushOutbox permanent-rejection path (mock post to return results:[{client_uuid, ok:false}] for a 201st queued sale); assert failedSales().length === 200, the first seeded client_uuid is absent, and outboxAll() no longer contains the 201st sale.

verdicts.reasoning: The broken path is provable by reading code at 482b3f38. (1) packages/shared/src/lib/sync.ts deadLetter (lines 63-71): `failed.push({...item, error, code}); localStorage.setItem(FAILED_KEY_FN(), JSON.stringify(failed.slice(-200))); return true;` — the write succeeds and returns true even when slice(-200) just evicted the oldest entry; false is returned only when setItem throws (quota). (2) flushOutbox (sync.ts:191): `else if (deadLetter(i, ...)) outboxRemove(i.client_uuid)` — on true the sale leaves the outbox, so after the 201st permanent rejection the evicted sale's payload, amount and error text exist nowhere: the server did db.rollback() on the reject (apps/server/app/api/v1/sync.py push handler) and logs nothing per-record. (3) No compensating trace: fleet.ts:64 heartbeat sends only failedSales().length (read from the already-capped list, so ≤200 and under-reporting); useFailedCount/POSKassa's 'N rad etildi' badge reads the same capped list; the print journal in printing.ts is a separate print-jobs log with its own HARD_CAP_JOBS cap, bound to server ids only for ACCEPTED sales, not a record of rejected ones. (4) The >200 scenario is within the code's own design envelope: outboxAdd (offline.ts:92) is uncapped, sync.ts added PUSH_CHUNK=1000 and comments about 500-sale reconnects, and the server marks every non-409/non-5xx HTTPException and every pydantic ValidationError as permanent (retry:false) per record — so one systemic 400 cause rejects a whole backlog in a single flush, record by record. (5) The violated invariant is the code's own stated contract, not the finder's invention: sync.ts comments say dead-letter exists so a rejected offline sale 'jimgina yo'qolmasin' (never silently lost) and the QA OFF-3 boolean was added precisely to close the silent-lost-sale hole — but that boolean only protects the newest entry; slice(-200) silently destroys the oldest, and the caller cannot distinguish 'recorded' from 'recorded by evicting another money-captured sale'. The natural fix the caller already handles exists (return false when at cap, leaving overflow in the outbox); it is simply not implemented. Only the operational frequency of >200 permanent rejects is deployment-dependent; the defect itself is unconditional in code.
verdicts.protective_constraint_found: None. Checked: server-side sync.py push rolls back rejected sales and keeps no per-record log; fleet.ts heartbeat carries only the capped list's length; printing.ts journal is print-jobs only, itself capped (HARD_CAP_JOBS) and bound to doc ids only on ok:true; outbox has no size cap that would prevent a 200+ backlog; the flushing mutex prevents double-deadLetter but does nothing against eviction.
verdicts.repro_hint: Unit test (vitest, jsdom localStorage): seed `savdoos_outbox_failed@<ns>` with 200 FailedSale entries (uuid-1..uuid-200), call the module's deadLetter via flushOutbox path or export-for-test with a 201st item; assert the returned value is true, JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(key)).length === 200, entry uuid-1 is absent, and uuid-201 is present — proving true was returned while uuid-1's only trace was destroyed.

findings.title: Changing the server URL silently strands the unsent sale queue (no warning, weak URL normalization)
findings.claim: All queue keys (outbox, dead-letter, policy) are namespaced by a hash of the raw `savdoos_api_url` string. Namespacing per server is intentional, but (a) LoginPin.saveCfg lets the URL be changed while the current namespace still holds unsent sales, with no check or warning (it explicitly clears the roster but never looks at outboxAll()), and (b) normalization is only `trim().replace(/\/+$/, "")` — a case change, http↔https, or an added `:443` produces a different hash for the SAME server. After the change the pending badge drops to 0, flushOutbox reads the new (empty) namespace, and the queued money-captured sales are never pushed or shown again.
findings.invariant: Unsent captured sales must never become unreachable by a configuration edit without the operator being told.
findings.attack_scenario: A POS has 12 offline cash sales queued. During troubleshooting someone opens the login config and re-enters the server address as 'HTTPS://savdoos-production.up.railway.app' (or the same URL after a temporary switch to staging and back with different casing). serverTag changes, savdoos_outbox@<old> is orphaned forever: badge shows 0, sync loop pushes nothing, shift close is no longer blocked (outboxAll() reads the new namespace) — 12 sales silently vanish from every UI while cash sits in the drawer unaccounted on the server.
findings.evidence: offline.ts serverTag hashes `localStorage.getItem("savdoos_api_url") || "default"` verbatim; api.ts setServerUrl stores `url.trim().replace(/\/+$/, "")` (no case/protocol canonicalization); LoginPin.tsx saveCfg: on change it only calls `clearRoster(); setServerUrl(server); setCompanyCode(company);` — no outbox/pending inspection, unlike Shift.tsx confirmClose which does guard on outboxAll().
findings.suggested_repro: Queue one sale, change savdoos_api_url casing via the login config screen, observe usePendingCount()===0 and flushOutbox() sending nothing; restore the exact original string and the sale reappears.

verdicts.reasoning: See above.
verdicts.protective_constraint_found: None. Searched at the SHA for: any outbox/pending inspection in LoginPin.saveCfg (absent); any confirmation dialog or password gate on the login-screen config panel (absent — gear button toggles the form, Save calls saveCfg directly); any cross-namespace localStorage scan or orphan-queue recovery (`savdoos_outbox@`, `localStorage.key` — zero hits); any URL canonicalization beyond trim + trailing-slash strip (absent in api.ts setServerUrl and in offline.ts serverTag, which hashes the raw stored string). The Shift.tsx:246 outbox guard and migrateLegacyKeys both operate only on the current namespace and therefore do not protect against this.
verdicts.repro_hint: Static proof suffices, but for a demo: with one sale in the outbox, on the login screen open the gear config, re-enter the server URL with any case change (e.g. HTTPS:// scheme), Save; observe usePendingCount()===0, flushOutbox() sends nothing, Shift close no longer blocked; re-enter the exact original string and the sale reappears.

verdicts.reasoning:
Every link of the claimed chain is present at 482b3f38, and no countervailing mechanism exists.

1) Namespacing on the raw string. packages/shared/src/lib/offline.ts `serverTag()` hashes `localStorage.getItem("savdoos_api_url") || "default"` verbatim (case-sensitive `h*31+charCode` hash); `nsKey(base)` is recomputed at every call. packages/shared/src/lib/api.ts `setServerUrl` stores only `url.trim().replace(/\/+$/, "")` — no lowercasing, no protocol/port canonicalization — so 'HTTPS://host', 'https://host', and 'https://host:443' are three distinct namespaces for one server.

2) The config edit has no guard. packages/shared/src/screens/LoginPin.tsx `saveCfg()` compares the server string only to decide `clearRoster()`, then unconditionally calls `setServerUrl(server); setCompanyCode(company)`. It never calls `outboxAll()`, shows no warning, and migrates nothing. The gear button rendering this config panel is on the unauthenticated login screen, and the logout buttons (apps/pos/src/components/Sidebar.tsx, NavDrawer.tsx) plus AutoLogout have no pending-outbox guard — so the screen is reachable with sales queued.

3) After the tag changes, every reader silently sees an empty queue: `flushOutbox()` (packages/shared/src/lib/sync.ts:160) reads `outboxAll()` = `cacheGet(CACHE.outbox)` = current namespace; `usePendingCount()` (sync.ts:41) same; the shift-close guard `if (outboxAll().length > 0)` (packages/shared/src/screens/Shift.tsx:246) same, so shift close is no longer blocked; even fleet telemetry `pending_ops` (packages/shared/src/lib/fleet.ts:63) reports 0. A repo-wide grep at this SHA finds no `Object.keys(localStorage)`/`localStorage.key(` scan and no cross-tag migration; `migrateLegacyKeys()` in offline.ts only moves the pre-namespacing GLOBAL keys into the current tag once — it never moves data between tags. The dead-letter list (`savdoos_outbox_failed@tag`, sync.ts) is stranded identically.

4) Bonus path proving it needs no typo at all: on a fresh install `savdoos_api_url` is null, so serverTag hashes the literal string "default" while `getServerUrl()` returns DEFAULT_ORIGIN. Offline sales queue under `savdoos_outbox@hash("default")`. Opening the config panel (input pre-filled with `getServerUrl()`) and pressing Save writes the URL to localStorage — `saveCfg`'s change check only gates `clearRoster`, `setServerUrl` runs regardless — and the tag flips from hash("default") to hash(url) with zero visible change to the operator. The queue is orphaned by pressing Save on unchanged settings.

The per-server namespacing itself is intentional and well-motivated (comment in offline.ts: production checks must not be pushed to staging), so the cross-server stranding is a design trade-off — but the stated invariant (operator must be told before captured sales become unreachable) is violated: severity holds for (a) no warning/no migration on any change, and (b) trivially-different spellings of the SAME server splitting the namespace. The data is recoverable only by restoring the byte-exact prior string, which nothing in the UI reveals.
verdicts.protective_constraint_found: None. No warning, no outbox check in LoginPin.saveCfg, no cross-namespace scan or migration anywhere in the client (migrateLegacyKeys handles only the one-time global→namespaced move), no server-side knowledge of client-queued sales, and the Shift.tsx close guard itself reads the new empty namespace.
verdicts.repro_hint: Offline-queue one sale (kill network, cash sale), note usePendingCount()===1. Open the login-screen gear and press Save with the server string re-typed in different casing (or, on a fresh install where localStorage savdoos_api_url is unset, press Save without editing anything). Observe pending badge 0, flushOutbox() POSTs nothing after network returns, and Shift close is no longer blocked. Set localStorage savdoos_api_url back to the byte-exact prior value (or remove the key in the fresh-install case) — the sale reappears and syncs.

findings.title: Status-only retry triage makes deterministic 409s loop forever, invisibly, and wedge shift close
findings.claim: sync.py classifies every 409 as retryable (`_transient = e.status_code >= 500 or e.status_code == 409`; the comment admits 'retry qarori hamon FAQAT HTTP holatiga tayanadi'), but sales.py raises 409 for conditions that can be permanent for a given record: till-vs-shift mismatch (sales.py:157) and LOT_INVARIANT_BROKEN (sales.py:726, whose own comment says the operator must 'contact support'). Such a record is retried every 30 s forever, is never dead-lettered (so the cashier never sees it in 'N rad etildi'), there is no retry counter, aging, or escalation in flushOutbox, and via Shift.tsx confirmClose the stuck record permanently blocks closing the shift on that device.
findings.invariant: Every queued sale must terminate in exactly one of: accepted, or surfaced to an operator as failed. 'Retried silently forever' is neither.
findings.attack_scenario: Cashier opens shift on till A (identity saved), device clock is >5 min ahead and force_shift is OFF (offline-sale-policy skips the clock check when `required` is false, shifts.py offline_sale_policy), sale queued offline. On flush, _clamp_sold_at returns None, so _create_sale_once takes the current-shift branch; the cashier has meanwhile been moved to a shift on till B — payload till_id=A vs resolved till B raises 409 at sales.py:157 on EVERY replay. The record loops eternally: badge stuck at 1, dead-letter empty, shift close refused with shift.syncFirst, and the sale is never recorded.
findings.evidence: sync.py: `_transient = e.status_code >= 500 or e.status_code == 409` -> `retry: _transient`. sync.ts:188: retry branch is a no-op keep, with no attempt count or max-age. sales.py:157 `raise HTTPException(409, "Yuborilgan TILL ochiq smena kassasiga mos emas...")` and sales.py:724-728 deliberately keep LOT_INVARIANT_BROKEN as 409 so it stays in the queue — with no client-side surfacing of a record that has failed N times.
findings.suggested_repro: TestClient: queue a sale whose till_id differs from the resolvable till, call /sync/push repeatedly — every response is ok:false,retry:true; on the client the record never leaves outbox and close is blocked.

verdicts.reasoning:
Every link of the claimed broken path is verbatim in the code at 482b3f38; no protective mechanism exists anywhere on it.

1) Status-only triage: apps/server/app/api/v1/sync.py push() has `_transient = e.status_code >= 500 or e.status_code == 409` and returns `"retry": _transient`. The adjacent comment explicitly admits the stable `code` field is informational only: "retry qarori hamon FAQAT HTTP holatiga tayanadi". So EVERY 409 is marked retryable regardless of cause.

2) Deterministic 409 producers exist: (a) apps/server/app/services/sales.py:157 raises 409 "Yuborilgan TILL ochiq smena kassasiga mos emas" whenever the payload's frozen till_id differs from the resolved shift till — deterministic for a queued record while the conflicting open shift persists. The client knowingly freezes till_id into the outbox: packages/shared/src/screens/POSKassa.tsx:644-647 comment says "zid bo'lsa server 409 qaytaradi (jimgina tuzatish YO'Q). Offline navbatda ham saqlanadi". (b) sales.py:724-728 deliberately keeps LOT_INVARIANT_BROKEN as 409 ("409 QOLADI: /sync/push uni tranzient deb biladi — pul olingan offline chek outbox'dan TUSHIB QOLMAYDI") while its user message says to contact support — an admitted permanent-until-human-intervention condition routed into the eternal-retry lane.

3) No client-side termination: packages/shared/src/lib/sync.ts flushOutbox retry branch is literally a no-op comment (`else if (r.retry) { /* ... outbox'da SAQLAYMIZ ... */ }`); OutboxSale (packages/shared/src/lib/offline.ts) has no attempt/age field; there is no max-retries, max-age, or promotion to dead-letter, so the retry:true error text/code is never shown — the record only inflates the generic pending badge (usePendingCount), indistinguishable from a normal unsynced sale, while useFailedCount ("N rad etildi") stays 0.

4) Wedged close: packages/shared/src/screens/Shift.tsx:246 confirmClose hard-returns with t("shift.syncFirst") while `outboxAll().length > 0` (unfiltered), so the stuck record blocks shift close on that device forever. close_shift is owner-only (shifts.py comment: cashier_id != emp.id -> 404), so escape requires the same cashier on another device — an operational workaround, not a code mechanism.

5) Attack preconditions verified: shifts.py offline_sale_policy runs the device-clock check only `if required and client_time is not None`, i.e. with force_shift OFF a >5-min-ahead clock still gets ALLOWED; sync.py _clamp_sold_at then returns None (future >5 min), sending the replay into the current-shift branch (sales.py:92-107, `at is None` path) instead of the historical opened_at<=sold_at match that would otherwise bind the sale to its original till. A stale persisted ShiftIdentity (packages/shared/src/store/shift.ts, never reconciled with /shifts/current — sync.ts's own comment admits "u hech qachon /shifts/current bilan solishtirilmaydi") plus a shift moved to another till via a second device produces the same permanent mismatch even without clock skew.

Softening (does not refute): the record IS weakly surfaced via the pending count, so "invisibly" is slightly overstated; the till-mismatch loop self-heals if the conflicting shift is closed elsewhere; and the LOT_INVARIANT_BROKEN routing is a deliberate lesser-evil choice (dead-lettering a money-taken sale was the prior LOST-SALE bug). But the stated invariant — every queued sale terminates in accepted or operator-visible failure — is violated by construction: a deterministic-409 record retries every 30 s with no counter, no reason shown, no escalation, and blocks shift close on the device.
verdicts.protective_constraint_found: None. Searched for: per-error-code retry triage (the `code` field exists in the push result but the comment states it is NOT used for the retry decision), retry counter or max-age on OutboxSale (absent in offline.ts), dead-letter promotion after N attempts (absent in sync.ts flushOutbox), client reconciliation of stale shift identity against /shifts/current (explicitly absent per sync.ts comment), server-side normalization of conflicting client till_id (explicitly rejected by design — 409, "jimgina tuzatish YO'Q"). The only mitigations are the generic pending badge (no error, no age) and cross-device manual shift close.
verdicts.repro_hint: TestClient, Postgres with cash_enabled: cashier opens shift on till A, sale payload {client_uuid, till_id: A, payment cash, sold_at: now+10min (gets clamped to None)}; close shift A directly in DB (or via a second session) and open a shift for the same cashier on till B; POST /api/v1/sync/push with the payload repeatedly — assert every response result is {ok:false, retry:true} with the till-mismatch detail (sales.py:157), the sale is never created and never marked permanent. Client-side: with that record in outbox, Shift.tsx confirmClose returns shift.syncFirst without calling /shifts/{id}/close. For the LOT case: monkeypatch stock_invariant.assert_ok to raise, push once — same {ok:false, retry:true, code:LOT_INVARIANT_BROKEN} loop.

verdicts.reasoning: SPLIT VERDICT. The static mechanics are all confirmed: apps/server/app/api/v1/sync.py push() marks every 409 retryable (`_transient = e.status_code >= 500 or e.status_code == 409`), packages/shared/src/lib/sync.ts:188's retry branch is a no-op keep with no attempt counter, max-age, or reason surfacing (r.error/r.code are discarded; only a bare pending count via usePendingCount is visible), and packages/shared/src/screens/Shift.tsx:246 hard-refuses close while outboxAll() (unfiltered by owner) is non-empty — despite its own comment claiming it merely warns. HOWEVER, the headline attack scenario (till-mismatch 409 at services/sales.py:157 looping forever) is REFUTED by runtime analysis: sync.py _clamp_sold_at compares the fixed sold_at to the server's CURRENT clock on each replay, so with clock skew S the future-clamp (`dt > now + 5min`) stops firing after S-5 minutes of wall time; from then on at=sold_at and create_sale takes the historical-shift branch (sales.py:95-100, `Shift.opened_at <= now AND (closed_at IS NULL OR closed_at >= now)` for honor_price_snapshot replays), which finds original shift A whose till matches the payload -> accepted. If shift A is not found historically, shift=None with force_shift off validates and USES the declared till (`if _till_id is None and shift is None: _till_id = _acc.id`) -> accepted. Independently, any 30-second flush tick while the cashier has no open conflicting shift resolves the record via the same shift-less path. So that loop is bounded (~clock skew, or until the conflicting shift closes) and the shift-close wedge self-heals; the only unbounded variant requires sold_at >60 days old AND a mismatching open shift at every single flush, which is not concretely constructible. WHAT SURVIVES: the finding's second leg, LOT_INVARIANT_BROKEN at sales.py:724-728, is deliberately kept 409 and fires on a persistent lot/Inventory inconsistency that only manual data repair clears (the message itself says contact support). Such a record genuinely retries every 30 s forever, invisibly (no dead-letter, no reason shown), and hard-blocks shift close on that device — violating the stated invariant. This cannot be shown occurring from code alone (needs a seeded invariant breach) and the comments show it is a known, documented tradeoff (keep money-taken offline checks in the queue) rather than an oversight, so it is PLAUSIBLE, not CONFIRMED_STATIC, and severity should be re-scored below P1 (missing operator surfacing/escalation for a retrying record, not a routine deterministic wedge).
verdicts.protective_constraint_found: _clamp_sold_at is evaluated against the server's advancing clock on every replay: sold_at stops being '>5 min in the future' after (skew-5min) wall minutes, after which the replay takes the historical-shift branch (sales.py:95-100) that binds the sale to the original shift A whose till_id matches the frozen payload; and when no shift matches (or none is open at a flush tick), the shift-less path with force_shift off validates and adopts the declared client till_id (`if _till_id is None and shift is None: _till_id = _acc.id`), accepting the sale. Both paths terminate the claimed eternal 409 loop for the till-mismatch scenario.
verdicts.repro_hint: For the surviving leg: on a lot-tracked Postgres tenant, create an offline-style sale payload (client_uuid, honor path via /sync/push) for a tracked product, then corrupt the invariant before flush (e.g. UPDATE inventory SET qty = qty + 1 for that product so services/stock_invariant.assert_ok fails). Call POST /sync/push repeatedly: every response is ok:false, retry:true, code:LOT_INVARIANT_BROKEN. Assert (a) the record would never be dead-lettered by the client triage (retry stays true on every call), (b) no field in the response or client state records attempt count/first-failure age, and (c) Shift.tsx confirmClose refuses with shift.syncFirst while the record sits in outbox. Contrast: replay the till-mismatch scenario (payload till A, open shift on till B, sold_at 10 min ahead) and observe the 409 turns into ok:true once server time passes sold_at-5min or the till-B shift closes — proving that loop is bounded.

findings.title: Offline-sale policy invalidation is device-local: shift closed from another device leaves ALLOWED cached up to 8h
findings.claim: The P9 gate's safety argument (sync.ts comment: the shift 'is only closed by its owner and that needs internet') assumes one device per cashier. clearOfflinePolicy() runs only on the device that performs the close (Shift.tsx confirmClose) or logout; an offline device belonging to the same cashier keeps its cached {mode:ALLOWED, owner_id:me} for up to OFFLINE_POLICY_TTL_MS = 8h. Offline cash sales finished there after the shift was closed elsewhere carry sold_at > closed_at, so replay finds no historical shift and, with force_shift on, gets the permanent 400 OPEN_SHIFT_REQUIRED — exactly the money-captured-then-dead-lettered outcome P9 was built to prevent.
findings.invariant: offlineSaleAllowed()==true must imply the eventual /sync/push replay will be accepted (the P9 commit is titled 'Refuse an offline sale the server is certain to reject').
findings.attack_scenario: Cashier's POS at till 1 goes offline at 10:00 with a fresh ALLOWED policy. At 10:30 the same cashier (or someone with their login) closes the shift from a second, online device. Until 18:00 the offline POS keeps completing cash sales (gate passes: mode ALLOWED, owner matches, TTL fresh). On reconnect every one of those sales is 400 OPEN_SHIFT_REQUIRED -> dead-letter; money is in the drawer, server has no sale/stock/cash record.
findings.evidence: sync.ts offlineSaleAllowed checks only cached mode/owner/TTL; Shift.tsx confirmClose calls clearOfflinePolicy() locally after a successful POST /shifts/{id}/close; nothing propagates the close to other devices, and shifts.py close_shift permits the owner from any device.
findings.suggested_repro: Two-client test: device1 caches ALLOWED then goes offline; device2 (same employee) closes the shift; device1 finishes a cash sale (gate passes), reconnects, /sync/push returns ok:false code=OPEN_SHIFT_REQUIRED.

verdicts.reasoning:
Every step of the claimed path is real at 482b3f38, and no protective constraint interrupts it.

1) Gate is purely device-local. packages/shared/src/lib/sync.ts::offlineSaleAllowed checks only the cached policy: mode==ALLOWED, owner_id===me, and now-at <= OFFLINE_POLICY_TTL_MS (8h). refreshOfflinePolicy is the only writer and runs from syncTick, which requires the network; an offline device keeps the stale ALLOWED for the full 8h. POSKassa.tsx (~line 612) uses exactly this gate for offline finish.

2) Invalidation is local-only. clearOfflinePolicy() has exactly three call sites (git grep): sync.ts (definition), Shift.tsx:256 inside confirmClose (after that device's own successful POST /shifts/{id}/close), and store/auth.ts:116 (logout). Nothing propagates a close to other devices — and cannot, since the target device is offline by hypothesis.

3) Nothing prevents the same cashier closing from another device. apps/server/app/api/v1/shifts.py::close_shift (line 528) checks only s.cashier_id == emp.id and status==open under FOR UPDATE. Auth is stateless JWT (app/core/security.py::create_access_token, no session table or token_version), so concurrent logins on two devices are valid; device pairing is deferred per project memory. Shift.tsx confirmClose does warn if outboxAll().length > 0, but that reads the CLOSING device's localStorage outbox — the second device has none, so the warning never fires; its own comment concedes "server yopilgan smenaga replay'ni baribir RAD etadi".

4) Replay is deterministically rejected. apps/server/app/services/sales.py::create_sale (honor_price_snapshot, at!=None) looks up the shift historically: opened_at <= sold_at AND (closed_at IS NULL OR closed_at >= sold_at). A sale with sold_at after closed_at matches nothing; with force_shift on it raises HTTPException(400, headers OPEN_SHIFT_REQUIRED). apps/server/app/api/v1/sync.py::push marks 400 as ok:false, retry:false (only 409/5xx/OperationalError are transient), and sync.ts flushOutbox dead-letters non-retry rejects. Test test_7b in apps/server/tests/test_offline_shift_policy.py asserts exactly this (ok:false, code OPEN_SHIFT_REQUIRED) when no shift covers sold_at. Retrying later cannot help: any newly opened shift has opened_at > sold_at, so the historical lookup still finds nothing — the money-captured/no-server-record outcome is permanent (dead-letter is only a local evidence list; sync.ts exposes no requeue, only clearFailed).

5) The stated safety argument itself contains the hole: both sync.ts ("Smenani esa FAQAT egasi yopadi va buning uchun internet kerak") and shifts.py (~line 350) argue that only the owner can close and that requires internet — implicitly assuming the owner is at the offline device. A second device (another activated POS till, or the Phase 5G PWA) with the same login breaks the assumption without violating any server check. In post-T0 cash-enforced (PG) stores the situation is strictly worse: per the test-7 docstring, even a sold_at inside the closed shift's window is rejected with CLOSED_SHIFT_CASH_REPLAY_REQUIRES_RECOVERY.

Severity P2 is fair: it needs the cashier (or someone with their PIN) to close the shift from a second online device during the outage window, which is operator misuse-adjacent but entirely unprevented by code, and the consequence is exactly the P9-class loss (cash in drawer, no sale/stock/ledger record on server).
verdicts.protective_constraint_found: None. Searched for: single-session/token invalidation (stateless JWT, app/core/security.py — none), device binding on close_shift (only cashier_id check, apps/server/app/api/v1/shifts.py:541-543), server-side grace for sold_at shortly after closed_at (none — strict closed_at >= sold_at in services/sales.py), cross-device policy invalidation (clearOfflinePolicy call sites are all local: Shift.tsx:256, store/auth.ts:116), pending-outbox guard at close (Shift.tsx checks only the closing device's own localStorage outbox), retry semantics (sync.py marks 400 permanent, retry:false). The only mitigations are the 8h TTL bound and the local dead-letter evidence trail — neither prevents the loss.
verdicts.repro_hint: Two-client test against PG or SQLite with security.force_shift=true: employee E opens shift (client A headers), simulate device A caching policy (GET /shifts/offline-sale-policy -> ALLOWED); close the shift via client B (same employee token, POST /shifts/{id}/close — succeeds, only ownership is checked); then POST /sync/push as A with a cash sale whose sold_at is after closed_at (within 60d/+5m clamp of sync.py::_clamp_sold_at). Expect results[0] == {ok:false, retry:false-ish, code:"OPEN_SHIFT_REQUIRED"} — mirrors test_7b_smena_umuman_bolmaganda_replay_RAD in apps/server/tests/test_offline_shift_policy.py but with the shift closed cross-device while ALLOWED was cached.

findings.title: offlineCard preference alone counts as 'money captured', voiding the P9 gate for card sales
findings.claim: finish() computes `moneyCaptured = active.some((c) => (c === "qr" && qrDoneRef.current) || (c === "card" && prefs.offlineCard))` and then `offlineOk = offlineSaleAllowed() || moneyCaptured`. For QR, qrDoneRef proves the money actually moved; for card, the mere store PREFERENCE offline_card=true is treated as proof of capture. So in a force_shift store with offlineCard enabled, the P9 gate never applies to card sales: a cashier with no open shift can complete offline card checkouts that the server is certain to reject (400 OPEN_SHIFT_REQUIRED -> dead-letter), even in the flow where the external terminal has not yet been charged and the gate could still have blocked before money moved.
findings.invariant: The money-captured escape hatch should fire only when payment has demonstrably occurred, not when a payment method is merely configured to work offline.
findings.attack_scenario: Store: force_shift on, prefs.offlineCard on. Cashier without an open shift, device offline (or policy BLOCKED/expired): taps card payment and finishes BEFORE running the external terminal. allowOffline is true via moneyCaptured, the sale is queued, the customer is charged (or not) outside any record, and replay dead-letters with OPEN_SHIFT_REQUIRED — the exact pre-P9 failure mode, still open for the card method.
findings.evidence: POSKassa.tsx finish(): `const moneyCaptured = active.some((c) => (c === "qr" && qrDoneRef.current) || (c === "card" && prefs.offlineCard)); const offlineOk = offlineSaleAllowed() || moneyCaptured;` — the card leg has no per-sale confirmation analogous to qrDoneRef; the adjacent comment acknowledges the trade-off but conflates the pref with capture.
findings.suggested_repro: Vitest (tests/pos-offline-shift.test.tsx style): policy BLOCKED, prefs.offlineCard=true, pay by card offline — finish() queues the sale instead of showing errOfflineShift.

verdicts.reasoning: See verdict reasoning.
verdicts.protective_constraint_found: None. Finish button gate (POSKassa.tsx:1321) checks only busy/payOk/xpayWait; no per-sale card capture signal exists; settings.py accepts offline_card without cross-validating force_shift; server-side force_shift enforcement (services/sales.py:108-119) fires only at replay, i.e. after the customer has left - it produces the dead-letter, it does not prevent the capture-less checkout. The only "defense" is the in-code comment documenting the trade-off, which is rationale, not a mechanism.
verdicts.repro_hint: Vitest in packages/shared (style of the P9 gate tests): mock prefs with offlineCard=true, seed the offline-policy cache with {mode:"BLOCKED", reason:"OPEN_SHIFT_REQUIRED", at:Date.now(), owner_id:<me>} (or leave it absent), mock post("/sales") to reject with a network error, select card as the sole payment method, call finish(). Expected-fail assertion: errOfflineShift is shown and nothing is queued. Actual: submitSale is called with allowOffline=true and the sale lands in the outbox; a subsequent mocked /sync/push 400 OPEN_SHIFT_REQUIRED moves it to failedSales. Contrast test: offlineCard=false with same state correctly shows t("pos.errNeedNet").

findings.title: _clamp_sold_at drops the timestamp, silently rebinding a replayed sale to the CURRENT shift
findings.claim: _clamp_sold_at returns None when sold_at is >5 min in the future or >60 days old; sync.push then calls create_sale(at=None, honor_price_snapshot=True). The historical-shift branch in _create_sale_once requires `honor_price_snapshot and at is not None`, so the sale falls into the online branch: it is stamped at flush time and attached to whatever shift is CURRENTLY open — inflating that shift's expected cash and today's reports with money physically taken during another shift/day — or, if no shift is open under force_shift, it gets the permanent 400 and dead-letters. The client half never learns its timestamp was discarded (push result is a plain ok:true).
findings.invariant: An offline sale must be accounted in the shift/day it physically happened, or be explicitly rejected — never silently re-dated.
findings.attack_scenario: POS clock is 10 min ahead (force_shift OFF, so offline_sale_policy skips the DEVICE_CLOCK_UNRELIABLE check entirely — shifts.py: `if required and client_time is not None`). Evening offline cash sales are queued with future sold_at. Next morning, new shift open, network returns: every replay clamps to None and books into the NEW shift at the new day — yesterday's Z-report is short, today's shift shows phantom surplus cash, and no result field warns anyone.
findings.evidence: sync.py _clamp_sold_at: `if dt > now + timedelta(minutes=5) or dt < now - timedelta(days=60): return None`. sales.py: `if honor_price_snapshot and at is not None:` historical lookup, else `Shift.status == open` current-shift lookup. shifts.py offline_sale_policy runs the clock check only when force_shift is required.
findings.suggested_repro: TestClient: open shift, push a sale with sold_at = now+10min — 200 ok:true, Sale.sold_at ≈ server now and shift_id = current shift, with no indicator in the push result.

verdicts.reasoning: See above.
verdicts.protective_constraint_found: Only a partial, advisory one: GET /shifts/offline-sale-policy (apps/server/app/api/v1/shifts.py) returns BLOCKED/DEVICE_CLOCK_UNRELIABLE for a clock >5 min ahead — but only when force_shift is ON and the client volunteers client_time, it is enforced client-side at queue time (not at /sync/push replay), and test_5e proves it is skipped entirely with force_shift OFF. Nothing at replay time preserves or flags the discarded timestamp; ledger device_occurred_at is set to server-now (sales.py:697).
verdicts.repro_hint: TestClient, force_shift OFF: open shift A, push {sold_at: now+10min, cash} -> 200, ok:true, no warning; assert Sale.sold_at ≈ server now and shift_id == A (silent re-dating, same-shift variant). Cross-shift variant: push a sale whose sold_at is 61+ days old (or now+13h simulating a day-ahead clock with overnight replay): assert it books into the currently open shift with today's sold_at, inflating today's expected cash. Note: do NOT test with sold_at = yesterday+10min replayed today — the clamp passes that through (historical branch works), which is why the finding's own scenario fails.

notes: PG-path guard verifies all four questioned properties: uniqueness (indisunique), validity (indisvalid AND indisready — an INVALID leftover from failed CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY yields IX_INVALID -> BAD -> 409, it cannot satisfy the guard), key column set AND order (array_agg(attname ORDER BY k.ord) compared as an ordered tuple, required_schema.py:1043-1047), and predicate (structural, not textual).

Predicate comparison on PG is not naive string equality: check_canon parses with Postgres operator precedence; extra/negated conjuncts, moved NOT, different literals, truncating varchar(n) casts, quoted type names and 2-vs-2.0 all change the tree; unknown syntax raises CanonError -> IX_DEF_UNREADABLE -> UNVERIFIABLE (refused, never mis-passed). I could not construct a semantically different predicate that canonicalizes equal on the PG path.

Case/quoting: unquoted identifiers are lowercased consistently with PG folding; quoted identifiers and string-literal case are preserved, so 'ORIGINAL' vs 'original' and "Copy" vs copy correctly mismatch. Both catalog queries scope to nspname='public' and key results by (name, table), so a same-named index on another table or schema cannot satisfy the guard.

UNVERIFIABLE is never cached (the self-reinforcing-outage regression is genuinely fixed, verified in code and tests); OK and BAD are cached 10s per (bind,index,table); the 10s stale-OK window after an operator breaks an index is an explicitly documented, owner-accepted risk (index_guard.py TTL comment).

All three wired sites call require_index before any lock, flush or write (doc_seq.py:146, lifecycle.py:331 in enrol, payments.py:71 in record_payment), and none sits under an except-HTTPException swallow; cutover_guard.dry_run's swallow wraps only read-only custody guards, and sync.py treats the 409 as transient (retry:true), so a guard refusal does not dead-letter a paid offline receipt.

record_payment ordering is sound: guard -> FOR NO KEY UPDATE lock on the subscription row -> idempotency SELECT under the lock -> renewal_base -> flush; duplicate hit releases the lock only when the service owns the transaction. enrol's IntegrityError fallback maps the losing racer to the same 409 as the pre-check.

The 6 REQUIRED_INDEXES writers left unwired (ux_print_jobs_original, ux_products_external_identity, ux_import_jobs_snapshot, ux_lot_intake_key, ux_lsr_request_client, ux_recv_corr_client) are a documented owner decision (docs/PURCHASE_SETTLEMENT_PHASE1.md §11.2/§11.3 OPTION A, after a 7-index wiring collapsed the cash suite); /lots/enable reads rs.missing(), which via soft_missing does include unique_index_problems and index_definition_problems, so lot activation is blocked on broken-shape indexes as claimed. One bookkeeping gap: ux_movements_cutover_key is listed unwired in §11.2 but never dispositioned in §11.3 — in code it is defended in depth anyway (company-row FOR NO KEY UPDATE with lock_timeout, job-level AlreadyApplied/StaleSnapshot scan under the lock, and the ux_import_jobs_snapshot claim at apply.py flush), so a broken cutover index alone does not enable double reconciliation.

Boot behavior matches the stated contract: _fatal treats a present-but-invalid/non-unique index as present (boot proceeds, name-missing stays fatal on PG via rs.enforced), and _verify_required_schema prints soft problems without raising — intentional per §11.2, compensated at the wired sites.
