notes: SHA input validation is sound at BOTH SHAs: reverse charset match `*[!0-9a-f]* | ""` plus exact length-40 check (38f1d750 lines 116-121); rejected values are never echoed to the public log; the GraphQL payload is written to a file with escaped variables and constant IDs, so the earlier 8-char-prefix heredoc injection is closed (was fixed before e60c213a, per the map — confirmed).

Step-level `if:` expressions without a status function carry GitHub's implicit success(): a failed 'CI HAQIQATAN yashilmi' step skips the Railway mutation step even though its `if:` only mentions steps.fresh.outputs.stale — no failed-check-then-deploy path.

Fork PR whose head branch is literally named 'main' does trigger the deploy workflow (workflow_run branches:[main] matches the PR run's head_branch), but it cannot deploy: at 38f1d750 the freshness step marks the fork SHA stale (green skip); at e60c213a the CI check finds no push-event run for the fork SHA and fails red. Noise only, no bypass.
The automatic workflow_run path excludes ci-proof/** at both SHAs via the trigger's `branches: [main]` filter (ci-proof CI runs have head_branch=ci-proof/...); the B4 bypass was dispatch-only.

Job-level gate booleans are correct string comparisons: unset STAGING_DEPLOY_ENABLED yields '' == 'true' -> false, so the workflow ships fully inert at both SHAs; `workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'` correctly excludes failure/cancelled/skipped conclusions of the triggering CI run.

Hollow CI success is not possible: ci.yml (byte-identical at both SHAs) has no job-level `if:`, no continue-on-error, and no path filters — every job (backend, backend-pg18, prod-install-boundary, frontend, unit, e2e, mobile, mobile-e2e) runs on every main push, so run conclusion 'success' implies all jobs passed; verify_pytest_run.py additionally proves tests executed.

In-progress/queued CI is fail-closed on both SHAs: at e60c213a a running run's conclusion is None -> counted in `bad` -> hard fail; at 38f1d750 there is an explicit `status != 'completed'` pending check (line 211).
38f1d750 re-filters `r.get('head_sha') == sha` locally instead of trusting the API's head_sha query filter (line 194) — API-filter drift defended.

Every code path of the 38f1d750 freshness step either writes a stale output or exits 1 (gh api failure aborts via set -Eeuo pipefail), closing the empty-output-passes-comparison hole; dispatch with SHA != main tip is a hard fail, delegating rollback to Railway's own deploymentRollback per the runbook.

staging-backup.yml p8.1 change (`vars.STAGING_BACKUP_ENABLED == 'true' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'`, lines 71-74) is a deliberate, documented B3 fix: the scheduled path stays gated, manual validation runs execute, and _db-backup-core fails closed without the connection-string secret; residual effect (any write-access actor can dispatch a staging dump anytime) is accepted by design and the artifact is GPG-encrypted before upload.

_db-backup-core.yml, db-backup.yml, restore-rehearsal.yml, ci.yml and uptime.yml are byte-identical between e60c213a and 38f1d750 (git diff empty) — the mapper's claim verified; the P8.1 commit touched only staging-deploy.yml, staging-backup.yml, RELEASE_SAFETY_RUNBOOK.md and two test files.

Dimension 'incorrect boolean conditions' beyond the reported findings: nothing found — no needs.X.result comparisons exist (single-job workflow), and no bare-boolean vs string confusion in any `if:` at either SHA.

continue-on-error masking a gate: VERIFIED ABSENT — no `continue-on-error` anywhere under .github/workflows at 38f1d750; the only `|| true` uses are ci.yml flutter precache/log-tail, uptime.yml body-read, and restore-rehearsal.yml cleanup/diff steps; the two `set +e` blocks in restore-rehearsal.yml (lines 260, 508) are bounded and re-check rc, failing hard on rc not in {0,2}.

Two workflow_dispatch runs racing: safe — the `staging-deploy` concurrency group serializes them, and each run re-reads main tip at execution time; a dispatch whose SHA is no longer tip HARD-FAILS at 38f1d750 (lines 155-158), so the second dispatch cannot re-deploy a superseded SHA (at e60c213a dispatch skipped the freshness step entirely — that is fixed B4, exists-on-main only, already in the known-defect list).

Stale queued workflow_run deploying an OLD SHA over a newer deployment: prevented in the common case — freshness is a per-run fact-check against live main tip evaluated when the run finally executes, not at queue time, so late-finishing CI of an older commit yields stale=true/skip (residual gaps are findings 1 and 3, not the base case).
Re-run of an old green/red CI run on main firing workflow_run: cannot deploy an old SHA — same freshness fact-check applies to the workflow_run path at both SHAs.

ci-proof/** green SHA authorizing a manual deploy (B4): VERIFIED FIXED at 38f1d750 — freshness step now runs on both paths (empty-output-satisfies-condition hole closed because `stale` is always written or the job fails), and the CI check filters head_branch=='main', event=='push', status=='completed', plus client-side head_sha re-verification and --paginate; exists-on-main only.
SHA injection into the GraphQL heredoc: reverse charset match `*[!0-9a-f]*` + exact length 40 present at BOTH SHAs (staging-deploy.yml lines ~116-121); rejected value is not echoed.

Backup/rehearsal cron overlap: db-backup 22:30 daily, staging-backup 21:30 daily, restore-rehearsal Sun 03:00, uptime */15 — all prod-touching jobs are read-only (pg_dump/probe) and restore targets an ephemeral service container; no concurrency group needed among them.

restore-rehearsal artifact-vs-fresh mode selection: the two modes are separate jobs gated by mutually exclusive `if:` on backup_run_id emptiness (lines 67, 331) — no silent fallback path from stored-artifact failure to fresh dump, as designed.

Encryption at rest verified real, not just a YAML substring: scripts/encrypt_evidence.sh fails closed on missing gpg or empty BACKUP_PASSPHRASE, encrypts AES256, then decrypts and compares sha256 bit-for-bit BEFORE deleting plaintext, rejects malformed checksums (empty/non-hex) that would have made before==after vacuously true, and exits non-zero if zero files were encrypted; identical blob at e60c213a and 38f1d750.

Passphrase never reaches argv or logs: passed step-env -> BACKUP_PASSPHRASE env -> `printf '%s' | gpg --passphrase-fd 0` (shell builtin, not in process list); no `set -x` anywhere in the backup path (git grep confirms); GitHub secret masking additionally covers the raw values.

Plaintext never uploaded: _db-backup-core.yml upload step has no `if: always()` (runs only after successful encrypt), path globs take only *.gpg/*.meta.json/*.sha256, `if-no-files-found: error`; fingerprint row counts/ledger sums are encrypted before upload at BOTH SHAs (core byte-identical, so this P8-era fix is not a P8.1-only claim); row-count printing to the log was removed (only table count + 12-hex fingerprint digest is printed).

Injection via workflow inputs: no untrusted interpolation found — _db-backup-core.yml inputs reach `run:` blocks only through `env:` indirection; the only inline interpolations are numeric/trusted (`${{ github.run_id }}`, `${{ steps.ret.outputs.* }}` computed internally); both dispatch triggers declare `workflow_dispatch: {}` (no inputs); .github/actions/pg-client interpolates `${{ inputs.major }}` into shell but is reachable only via in-repo callers who already control the workflow file, so no privilege boundary is crossed (fork PRs get no secrets).

B3 fix verified at execution-semantics level: `github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'` in the job-level `if:` of the workflow-call job evaluates in the caller run's context, so a manual staging-backup dispatch now executes and, with STAGING_DATABASE_URL absent, fails loudly via core's explicit empty-secret check (exit 1) rather than skipping — the fix is real, modulo the residual gate-validation gap reported above.

Missing-secret fail-closed verified: core's first step errors non-zero on empty database_url or passphrase; both wrappers grant only `contents: read` + `actions: read` (least privilege, and the reusable workflow inherits caller permissions so the retention `gh api` read works).

Manual dispatch of production db-backup.yml is intentionally ungated and requires repo write access (dispatch cannot be triggered from forks); no defect found in that dimension beyond the staging gate-validation residual reported above.

backup_postgres.sh checksum handling is injection/format-safe: computed cd-into-dir with basename to defeat coreutils backslash-escape mode, then validated pure-hex before being written into meta.json and the .sha256 file.

findings.title: Manual dispatch could deploy a never-on-main SHA (green ci-proof/** run authorized; freshness step skipped, empty output passed the gate)
findings.symbol: deploy job, steps 'fresh' and 'Bu SHA uchun CI HAQIQATAN yashilmi'
findings.claim: At e60c213a the 'Nishon hali ham main tepasimi' step carries `if: github.event_name != 'workflow_dispatch'` (line 155), so on manual dispatch `steps.fresh.outputs.stale` is empty and the deploy step's condition `steps.fresh.outputs.stale != 'true'` (line 174) evaluates true. The CI-green check (line 132) filters only `r['name'] == 'CI' and r['event'] == 'push'` with no `head_branch == 'main'` filter, and ci.yml triggers on `push: branches: [main, "ci-proof/**"]`. Together: a green CI run on a ci-proof/** branch satisfies the gate and the SHA deploys to staging without ever having been on main.
findings.invariant: Only a SHA that is on main AND whose CI ran green from a push to main may reach the Railway serviceInstanceDeployV2 mutation, on every trigger path.
findings.attack_scenario: Write-access operator pushes commit X to ci-proof/foo; CI runs there and goes green. Operator (accidentally or deliberately) runs workflow_dispatch with commit_sha=X. sha-validate passes (valid hex40), freshness step is skipped (dispatch), its empty output satisfies `!= 'true'`, the CI check finds the green ci-proof push run and passes, and X — never reviewed onto main — is deployed to staging.
findings.evidence: e60c213a .github/workflows/staging-deploy.yml:132 `ci = [r for r in runs if r['name'] == 'CI' and r['event'] == 'push']` (no head_branch filter); :155 `if: github.event_name != 'workflow_dispatch'` on step id=fresh; :174 `if: steps.fresh.outputs.stale != 'true'` on the mutation step. Fixed at 38f1d750: freshness step has no `if:` and hard-fails on dispatch when SHA != main tip (lines 140-161), and the Python filter adds `head_branch == 'main'` plus local `head_sha == sha` re-check (lines 196-200). Classification: exists-on-main only, FIXED on p8.1. Not live-exploitable today: STAGING_DEPLOY_ENABLED ships unset, so the job-level gate (line 81) keeps the whole workflow inert at both SHAs.
findings.suggested_repro: Static only (do not trigger workflows): compare `git show e60c213a:.github/workflows/staging-deploy.yml` lines 132/155/174 against 38f1d750 lines 140-161/196-200; note ci.yml `on.push.branches` includes ci-proof/** at both SHAs.

verdicts.reasoning: The defect at e60c213a is provable by reading code alone; it is FIXED at the audited SHA 38f1d750 and inert at both SHAs (STAGING_DEPLOY_ENABLED unset). Broken path at e60c213a (.github/workflows/staging-deploy.yml, job `deploy`), all line numbers verified: (1) step id=fresh ('Nishon hali ham main tepasimi') carries `if: github.event_name != 'workflow_dispatch'` at line 155, so on manual dispatch it is skipped and `steps.fresh.outputs.stale` is the empty string; (2) the Railway mutation step's guard at line 174 is `if: steps.fresh.outputs.stale != 'true'` — empty != 'true' evaluates true, so the mutation step runs; (3) the CI-green step ('Bu SHA uchun CI HAQIQATAN yashilmi') filters at line 132 `ci = [r for r in runs if r['name'] == 'CI' and r['event'] == 'push']` with NO head_branch filter, and .github/workflows/ci.yml at e60c213a lines 22-23 triggers on `push: branches: [main, "ci-proof/**"]`, so a single green CI run from a push to ci-proof/foo satisfies the gate for a SHA that was never on main; (4) the sha-validate step only enforces 40-hex, not ancestry. No protective mechanism blocks this at e60c213a: the only remaining gate is the job-level `vars.STAGING_DEPLOY_ENABLED == 'true'` (line 82), an owner-controlled on/off variable that, once enabled per RELEASE_SAFETY_RUNBOOK.md §2, gates both trigger paths identically and does not restore the invariant. Confirmation of the fix at 38f1d750: step id=fresh (line 141) has no `if:` and hard-fails (`exit 1`, line 158) on workflow_dispatch when SHA != main tip; the CI filter (lines 196-200) adds `head_branch == 'main'`, a local `head_sha == sha` re-check (line 193), a pending-status rejection (line 211), and pagination. The fix commit's own comments explicitly describe the e60c213a hole, including the ci-proof/** vector, as a defect ('ILGARI NUQSON BOR EDI... ci-proof/** dagi yashil SHA... qo'lda staging'ga chiqarilishi mumkin edi'). Classification in the finding is accurate: exists on main e60c213a only, fixed on P8.1, not live-exploitable today because the gate variable ships unset — the P0 severity applies only to the window where an owner enables the workflow while main is still at e60c213a.
verdicts.protective_constraint_found: Only the job-level `vars.STAGING_DEPLOY_ENABLED == 'true'` condition (staging-deploy.yml line 82 at e60c213a), currently unset, which keeps the entire workflow inert on every path. It is an operational activation switch, not a logic constraint: once enabled it passes workflow_dispatch through unchanged, so it does not preserve the 'only main-push-green SHAs reach serviceInstanceDeployV2' invariant. No unique index, branch-protection-in-code, ancestry check, or other in-workflow mechanism blocks the dispatch path at e60c213a.
verdicts.repro_hint: Static diff only (do not trigger workflows): `git show e60c213a:.github/workflows/staging-deploy.yml` lines 82/132/155/174 vs `git show 38f1d750:.github/workflows/staging-deploy.yml` lines 141-161 (fresh step, no if:, dispatch hard-fail) and 193-211 (head_branch=='main' + head_sha + pending checks); `git show e60c213a:.github/workflows/ci.yml` lines 22-23 for the ci-proof/** push trigger present at both SHAs.

verdicts.reasoning: See above.
verdicts.protective_constraint_found: Job-level gate at e60c213a line 81-82: `if: vars.STAGING_DEPLOY_ENABLED == 'true' && ...`. This repository variable ships UNSET (per the workflow's own header comment and RELEASE_SAFETY_RUNBOOK activation plan), so the deploy job is skipped on every trigger path at both SHAs — the defect was never live-exploitable, only latent. Secondary constraints: workflow_dispatch and pushing to ci-proof/** both require repo write access (insider-only attack surface), and the RAILWAY_TOKEN secret must also be configured for the mutation to succeed.

GHA skipped-step-output semantics are documented platform behavior and need no live test.

findings.title: workflow_dispatch executes the gate from any ref while RAILWAY_TOKEN is a repo-level secret with no GitHub environment protection — gate is advisory for write-access actors
findings.symbol: deploy job (no `environment:` key; secrets.RAILWAY_TOKEN at line 229/38f1d750)
findings.claim: The deploy job binds `secrets.RAILWAY_TOKEN` but declares no GitHub `environment:` (verified: the only 'environment' occurrence at 38f1d750 is the Railway GraphQL variable at line 242). GitHub runs a dispatched workflow from the file at the chosen ref, and repo-level secrets are available to workflows on any branch. So every check the gate performs (SHA pinning, freshness, CI-green) constrains only the copy of the file on the ref being run — a write-access actor can push a branch with those steps deleted (or any new workflow that reads the secret) and deploy an arbitrary SHA, or exfiltrate the token, without touching main.
findings.invariant: The credential that performs staging deploys should only be usable by the reviewed gate on main (GitHub environment-scoped secret + protection rules restricting deployments to main), so the gate cannot be sidestepped by running a modified copy of itself.
findings.attack_scenario: After the owner enables the gate (RAILWAY_TOKEN secret + STAGING_DEPLOY_ENABLED=true), a collaborator with Write pushes branch `tmp` where staging-deploy.yml's fresh/CI steps are removed and the trigger accepts any input, then dispatches the workflow on ref=tmp with an arbitrary commit_sha; Railway deploys it to staging with zero gate checks. No admin rights and no main-branch change required.
findings.evidence: 38f1d750 .github/workflows/staging-deploy.yml has no `environment:` on the deploy job; grep for 'environment' matches only the GraphQL mutation string (line 242). Same at e60c213a. RELEASE_SAFETY_RUNBOOK activation steps add the secret at repo scope. Classification: both. Note the prior audit's B4 attacker (write-access dispatcher) is the same trust level this finding assumes, so it is inside the gate's own threat model; severity kept P1 rather than P0 because it needs a deliberately doctored ref (not an accident), targets staging only, and is recoverable via Railway rollback.
findings.suggested_repro: Static: confirm absence of `environment:` in the deploy job at both SHAs and that activation docs create RAILWAY_TOKEN as a repository secret rather than an environment secret.

verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed by reading the audited tree. (1) At 38f1d750, .github/workflows/staging-deploy.yml's `deploy` job declares no `environment:` key — `git grep -i environment 38f1d750 -- .github/workflows/staging-deploy.yml` matches only the ENVIRONMENT_ID constant (line 231) and the GraphQL mutation string (lines 242-243); no workflow in the repo uses GitHub environments. (2) The deploy step binds `RAILWAY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RAILWAY_TOKEN }}` directly. (3) RELEASE_SAFETY_RUNBOOK.md §2.5 step 2 creates the token as a plain repo secret verified via `gh secret list` (repository scope); no activation step creates a GitHub environment or deployment-branch policy. (4) The file carries `workflow_dispatch` with a `commit_sha` input. Under documented GitHub semantics, a dispatched run executes the workflow file at the chosen ref, and repository-scoped secrets are available to workflow runs on any branch — so every gate check (STAGING_DEPLOY_ENABLED `if:`, hex-SHA validation, main-tip freshness, CI-green verification, ci-proof exclusion) lives only in the copy being run and is void on a doctored branch. No protective mechanism survives scrutiny: `vars.STAGING_DEPLOY_ENABLED` is a repo variable readable from any ref and removable from the copy; `permissions: contents/actions: read` limits only GITHUB_TOKEN; the concurrency group merely serializes; test_staging_deploy_gate.py is an offline logic test; Railway's `serviceInstanceDeployV2` accepts any commitSha given the bearer token, and deleting the GitHub trigger (§2.5 step 4) does not scope the token. The gate's own B4 comments show a write-access dispatcher is inside its declared threat model (it hardens against non-main SHAs and heredoc injection from dispatch inputs), yet only the on-main copy is hardened — the invariant that the credential be usable only by the reviewed gate on main is achievable solely via an environment-scoped secret with deployment-branch protection, which is absent from both the workflow and the activation docs. Aggravating detail: §2.6 publishes the production environmentId (1d0edbf9-…) and step 2 sources the token from "Account → Tokens" (account scope), so a doctored copy could plausibly redirect ENVIRONMENT_ID to production, not just staging. Mitigations: at the audited SHA the gate is dormant (no secret exists yet — exposure begins only at activation), the attacker must hold Write access and push a deliberately doctored ref, and staging is recoverable via deploymentRollback — consistent with P1, not P0.
verdicts.protective_constraint_found: None. Candidates examined and rejected: `vars.STAGING_DEPLOY_ENABLED` if-gate (repo variable, present on all refs, and deletable from the dispatched copy); B4 freshness/CI-green/hex-SHA steps (exist only in the file at the run's own ref); `permissions: contents: read, actions: read` (scopes GITHUB_TOKEN only, not secrets.RAILWAY_TOKEN); concurrency group staging-deploy (serialization, not authorization); apps/server/tests/test_staging_deploy_gate.py (offline test of the on-main script); Railway trigger deletion per runbook §2.5 step 4 (removes the push path but does not scope the token). No GitHub environment, deployment-branch rule, CODEOWNERS or ruleset restricting workflow refs exists at the SHA.
verdicts.repro_hint: Static: `git show 38f1d750:.github/workflows/staging-deploy.yml` — confirm workflow_dispatch trigger, `secrets.RAILWAY_TOKEN` binding, and absence of any `environment:` job key (grep matches only ENVIRONMENT_ID/GraphQL text at lines 231/242). `git show 38f1d750:RELEASE_SAFETY_RUNBOOK.md` §2.5 step 2 — token stored via repo-scope `gh secret` (`gh secret list`), no environment creation step. Live proof post-activation (do NOT run against real staging): push branch tmp with the gate steps stripped from staging-deploy.yml, then `gh workflow run staging-deploy.yml --ref tmp -f commit_sha=<any 40-hex>` — the run executes tmp's copy with the repo-level RAILWAY_TOKEN available.

verdicts.reasoning: Verified at both 38f1d750 and e60c213a: the deploy job in .github/workflows/staging-deploy.yml declares no `environment:` key — the only 'environment' strings in the file are the hardcoded `ENVIRONMENT_ID` env constant and the `serviceInstanceDeployV2(environmentId:...)` GraphQL mutation (line 242 / line 190). RELEASE_SAFETY_RUNBOOK.md §2.5 step 2 creates RAILWAY_TOKEN as a repository-scoped secret ('gh secret list' verification), and it is an ACCOUNT token ('Account → Tokens'), so exfiltration is not even confined to the staging environment ID the workflow hardcodes. Runbook line 44 confirms main has no branch protection, so no required-review/CODEOWNERS control on .github/workflows/ exists either. Under documented GitHub semantics, workflow_dispatch executes the workflow file at the chosen ref, and repository secrets are available to workflow runs on any branch for write-access (non-fork) actors; the vars.STAGING_DEPLOY_ENABLED gate exists only in the `if:` of the reviewed copy and binds no other workflow file. Therefore every check the gate performs (SHA regex, main-tip freshness, CI-green pagination logic) is self-enforced by the very file a write-access attacker replaces: push branch `tmp` with those steps deleted and dispatch on ref=tmp, or simpler, push any new `on: push` workflow that reads secrets.RAILWAY_TOKEN. This is squarely inside the gate's own threat model — the B4 fixes and the runbook's explicit claim that manual dispatch 'darvozani chetlab o'tmaydi' (does not bypass the gate) treat the write-access dispatcher as an actor the gate must constrain, and that claim is false. No refuting mechanism found anywhere in the repo. The invariant (credential usable only by the reviewed gate on main) requires an environment-scoped secret with deployment-branch protection, which the code and activation docs provably do not establish. Provable by reading the workflow, the runbook, and applying documented GitHub platform semantics — no runtime test needed. P1 severity is fair: requires a deliberate write-access insider/compromised collaborator, targets staging, recoverable via Railway rollback; but the account-scoped token makes the exfiltration branch of the attack potentially reach beyond staging.
verdicts.protective_constraint_found: None. Checked: (1) no `environment:` on the deploy job at either SHA; (2) runbook creates RAILWAY_TOKEN at repo scope via gh secret, as an account-level Railway token; (3) runbook line 44 documents main branch protection is absent (404), so no review gate on workflow file changes; (4) vars.STAGING_DEPLOY_ENABLED only gates the reviewed copy's `if:` and does not restrict secret availability to other refs or other workflow files; (5) no Actions policy restricting workflows/refs is documented anywhere in the repo.
verdicts.repro_hint: Static: `git show 38f1d750:.github/workflows/staging-deploy.yml | grep -n "environment"` → only ENVIRONMENT_ID constant and GraphQL variable, no job-level `environment:` key; `git show 38f1d750:RELEASE_SAFETY_RUNBOOK.md` §2.5 step 2 (repo secret via `gh secret list`) and line 44 (no branch protection). Fix direction: move RAILWAY_TOKEN into a GitHub environment (e.g. `staging`) with deployment-branch policy restricted to main, add `environment: staging` to the deploy job, and protect .github/workflows/ via branch protection + CODEOWNERS.

findings.title: Fire-and-forget Railway mutation: no post-deploy status verification, and TOCTOU between the freshness/CI reads and the mutation
findings.symbol: step 'Railway'ga AYNAN shu SHA ni deploy qilish' (38f1d750 lines 225-256)
findings.claim: The commit point is the serviceInstanceDeployV2 POST. The response is only checked for GraphQL `errors`; the returned deployment id is never polled, so a deploy that Railway accepts but that fails to build/boot leaves the workflow green. The freshness read (lines 140-161) and CI-green read (166-223) are not atomic with the mutation: main can advance (or be force-rewound) in the seconds between the check and the POST, and — acknowledged in the workflow's own comment — a runner killed after the POST deploys invisibly with no record of outcome.
findings.invariant: A green gate run should imply staging is actually running the stated SHA (or the run reports failure); the SHA verified fresh/green should be the SHA that ends up deployed.
findings.attack_scenario: Push A goes green; deploy run for A passes fresh at t0; at t0+5s main is force-pushed to drop A (e.g. leaked secret rewrite); mutation at t0+20s still deploys A — a commit no longer on main — and the run reports success. Separately: Railway accepts the mutation but the build crashes; workflow is green, operators believe staging updated, subsequent 'AVVAL SERVER, KEYIN KLIENT' client releases (CLAUDE.md rule) are cut against a staging that never picked up the server change.
findings.evidence: 38f1d750 lines 246-256: `curl ... -d @payload.json > resp.json` then Python checks only `d.get('errors')` and prints `d.get('data')` truncated; no deployment-status query. Concurrency comment (lines 60-66) explicitly concedes a killed job after the mutation 'deploy baribir davom etadi, lekin biz natijani ko'rmaymiz'. Identical logic at e60c213a.
