findings.suggested_repro: Static: verify resp.json handling contains no follow-up GraphQL deployment status query and no retry/rollback on non-error null data.

verdicts.reasoning: Provable by reading .github/workflows/staging-deploy.yml at 38f1d750. (1) Fire-and-forget: the deploy step ('Railway'ga AYNAN shu SHA ni deploy qilish') POSTs the serviceInstanceDeployV2 mutation via curl into resp.json, then runs a Python heredoc that only does `if d.get('errors'): sys.exit(...)` and `print('deploy boshlandi:', json.dumps(d.get('data'))[:200])` before `rm -f resp.json`. There is no follow-up GraphQL deployment-status query, no polling of the returned deployment id, no retry, and no health check — the job exits 0 the moment Railway ACCEPTS the mutation, regardless of build/boot outcome. I hunted for compensating mechanisms and found none: uptime.yml at the same SHA monitors only PRODUCTION (`BASE: https://savdoos-production.up.railway.app`) and never compares a commit SHA; RELEASE_SAFETY_RUNBOOK.md §2 step 7 does check `/api/v1/health` build.commit against the new SHA, but only as a one-time MANUAL activation live-test, not per deploy. Notably the verification primitive exists and is unused: apps/server/app/api/v1/health.py:42 exposes RAILWAY_GIT_COMMIT_SHA, so the workflow could poll staging's build.commit but does not. (2) TOCTOU: the freshness step (`gh api repos/$REPO/commits/main`) and the CI-green step each read GitHub once; the mutation fires seconds later with no re-check, and the workflow's own concurrency comment concedes the killed-runner variant verbatim ('deploy baribir davom etadi, lekin biz natijani ko'rmaymiz'). No lock, no post-mutation reconciliation. Severity-tempering context the report should carry: (a) the workflow ships DISABLED (`vars.STAGING_DEPLOY_ENABLED == 'true'` gate; per project state it has never been enabled — staging currently deploys via Railway's own checkSuites=true trigger), so today this is a latent design defect, not a live exposure; (b) on a Railway build failure the previous deployment keeps serving, so the harm is a false-green run / operator misbelief, not an outage; (c) the force-push TOCTOU self-corrects on the next CI cycle for the rewritten main (push event → new CI → new gated deploy, serialized by the `staging-deploy` concurrency group), and the stale-skip check already closes the queued-deploy ordering race — the residual window is the few seconds between the tip read and the POST, which no in-repo mechanism can make atomic; (d) the specific downstream attack (client releases cut against a stale server) is partially blunted by CLAUDE.md release step 0, a mandatory manual production-route check (`GET /api/v1/receipt/profile` must not 404) before any client release — manual, single-route, production-only, so a mitigation, not a refutation. Net: the invariant 'green run implies staging runs the stated SHA' is not enforced anywhere in the repo; the P2 severity is fair given the disabled gate and mitigations.
verdicts.protective_constraint_found: None that enforces the invariant. Partial mitigations only: STAGING_DEPLOY_ENABLED variable gate (workflow dormant, never enabled); `staging-deploy` concurrency group + stale-skip freshness check (closes queued-deploy ordering race but not the seconds-wide read-to-POST window); Railway keeps last-good deployment on build failure; RELEASE_SAFETY_RUNBOOK.md §2 step 7 manual build.commit verification at activation time only; CLAUDE.md release step 0 manual production route probe before client releases. uptime.yml watches production only and checks no SHA.
verdicts.repro_hint: Static inspection suffices: `git show 38f1d750:.github/workflows/staging-deploy.yml` — last step's Python block checks only d.get('errors') then prints d.get('data') truncated; grep confirms no second GraphQL call (no `deployment(`/`deployments(` status query) and no curl to the staging health endpoint, while apps/server/app/api/v1/health.py:42 shows build.commit is available to poll.

findings.title: Stale-skip silently drops a green commit forever when the next commit's CI is red — staging stops updating with a green run log
findings.symbol: step id=fresh stale branch (38f1d750 lines 158-161) + job if (lines 87-90)
findings.claim: On the workflow_run path, a deploy run whose SHA is no longer main tip sets stale=true and exits green, on the stated assumption that 'a separate run will handle the newer commit' (comment line 160). But if the newer commit's CI concludes failure, its deploy run is skipped at the job `if:` (`workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'`), so neither commit deploys and there is no retry: the last tested-green commit A never reaches staging, and every run in the chain is green or skipped, giving operators a false 'nothing pending' signal. GitHub's concurrency queue (cancel-in-progress:false keeps at most one pending run, cancelling older pending ones) adds a second path to the same silent drop.
findings.invariant: Every CI-green main commit either deploys to staging or a visibly failed/actionable run explains why; a green audit trail should not coexist with staging silently pinned to an old SHA.
findings.attack_scenario: Staging runs old commit X. Push A (green) then push B before A's deploy run reaches its fresh check; A's run: TIP=B != A, stale=true, green skip. B's CI is red: B's deploy run never starts (job if). Result: staging stays on X although A was fully tested; nothing is red in the Staging Deploy workflow, and the team ships client releases assuming server change A is live (CLAUDE.md server-before-client rule).
findings.evidence: 38f1d750 lines 158-161 (notice + stale=true, exit 0) and lines 87-90 (job gate requires conclusion=='success' for workflow_run). No mechanism re-dispatches the newest green SHA. Fail-safe in direction (nothing untested ships) hence P2. Classification: both (e60c213a lines 154-171 identical semantics for the workflow_run path).
findings.suggested_repro: Static reasoning over the two conditions; observable later in run history as a green 'skipped' deploy run followed by no deploy run for the red successor.

verdicts.reasoning: Provable from .github/workflows/staging-deploy.yml at 38f1d750 alone. (1) Job gate `jobs.deploy.if` requires `github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'` on the workflow_run path, so a red-CI successor B yields a gray skipped run, never a red one. (2) The `id: fresh` step, on the workflow_run path with TIP != SHA, emits a ::notice claiming "yangiroq commit uchun alohida run bajaradi" (a separate run handles the newer commit), sets stale=true and exits 0 (green) — that claim is false precisely when B's CI is red, so green commit A never deploys and no run fails. (3) No protective mechanism exists: no scheduled reconciler among the 7 workflows at this SHA; RELEASE_SAFETY_RUNBOOK.md offers only Railway deploymentRollback (backward, not forward); and the obvious operator recovery — workflow_dispatch with A's SHA — is HARD-REJECTED by the same fresh step (dispatch + non-tip => exit 1). Both behaviors are deliberately pinned by apps/server/tests/test_staging_deploy_gate.py (test_AVTOMATIK_yolda_ESKIRGAN_SHA_jimgina_SKIP line 360; test_QOLDA_chaqiruvda_ESKIRGAN_SHA_QATTIQ_RAD_etiladi line 350) — the tests freeze the gap rather than close it. Severity correctly bounded at P2: direction is fail-safe (nothing untested ships); B's red CI run is visible in the CI workflow (so the repo is not entirely green — but that red explains B's failure, not that staging is pinned pre-A, while A's deploy run affirmatively and falsely reports being handled); the drop lasts only until the next green tip, whose deploy carries A's content; and the workflow is currently dormant (STAGING_DEPLOY_ENABLED unset), making the defect latent until activation. The concurrency-queue secondary path is weaker than claimed: a replaced pending run shows as cancelled, which is visible, not silent-green.
verdicts.protective_constraint_found: None that closes the gap. Checked: (a) workflow_dispatch recovery for A — rejected by design (fresh step exits 1 for non-tip SHA on dispatch, pinned by test_staging_deploy_gate.py line 350); (b) Railway's own GitHub trigger as backstop — runbook activation step 4 deletes it (deploymentTriggerDelete) before enabling this workflow; (c) scheduled reconciler — ls-tree of .github/workflows/ at 38f1d750 shows none; (d) test suite — pins the silent-skip behavior as intended rather than guarding against the red-successor combination. Partial mitigants only: red CI run on B is visible in the CI workflow, and CLAUDE.md's server-before-client rule mandates probing the production endpoint (GET /api/v1/receipt/profile, 404 => no client release) before releases, which would catch one class of the "assume A is live" mistake.
verdicts.repro_hint: No test needed; observable statically. To witness in run history once enabled: push A (CI green), push B before A's deploy run executes its fresh check; A's Staging Deploy run concludes success with notice "Nishon eskirgan ... yangiroq commit uchun alohida run bajaradi"; B's CI concludes failure; B's Staging Deploy run shows all jobs skipped; staging /api/v1/health build.commit still shows pre-A SHA; gh workflow run staging-deploy.yml -f commit_sha=<A> then fails with "Nishon main tepasi EMAS".

findings.title: Single-page run listing made the manual CI-green check fail exactly when needed (Uptime pollution) — availability defect, fail-closed
findings.claim: At e60c213a the check reads one API page (`gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs?head_sha=$SHA&per_page=100"`). Uptime binds ~96 runs/day to the default-branch HEAD SHA, so about a day after a commit becomes tip, the real CI run falls off page 1 and the gate dies with 'CI run TOPILMADI' — the manual deploy path is unusable precisely for a stable main tip. Direction is safe (no deploy), so P2 not P1.
findings.invariant: The gate's authority query must observe all workflow runs for the SHA regardless of how many unrelated scheduled runs share it.
findings.attack_scenario: Operator enables the gate and dispatches yesterday's (still-tip) main SHA; 100 newest runs for that SHA are Uptime/Backup entries; the CI run is on page 2; check exits 1; deploy blocked despite green CI.
findings.evidence: e60c213a line 128 (no --paginate). Fixed at 38f1d750 line 180: `gh api --paginate --jq '.workflow_runs[]' ...` into JSONL, plus explicit `status != 'completed'` pending check (line 211). Classification: exists-on-main only, FIXED on p8.1.
findings.suggested_repro: Static diff of the two check steps; run counts per SHA are documented in the workflow's own header comment (d916b9b -> 8 suites, Uptime every 15 min).

verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed by reading the code; no protective constraint exists at e60c213a. (1) At e60c213a, .github/workflows/staging-deploy.yml step "Bu SHA uchun CI HAQIQATAN yashilmi" runs exactly `gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs?head_sha=$SHA&per_page=100" > runs.json` — one page, no `--paginate`, no server-side `event=push` filter (which would have excluded scheduled runs and been the protective mechanism; it is absent). The Python filter `ci = [r for r in runs if r['name'] == 'CI' and r['event'] == 'push']` then hits `sys.exit("::error::Bu SHA uchun \`CI\` run TOPILMADI — deploy qilinmaydi.")` when empty. (2) The pollution source is real and documented in the same repo at the same SHA: .github/workflows/uptime.yml has `cron: "*/15 * * * *"` (96 runs/day), plus db-backup.yml nightly and restore-rehearsal.yml weekly; scheduled runs bind head_sha to the default-branch tip — the staging-deploy.yml header comment itself states this ("Uptime (har 15 daqiqa)... DEFAULT BRANCH HEAD'iga bog'lanadi, ya'ni AYNAN deploy qilinayotgan SHA'ga", measured d916b9b -> 8 suites). GitHub's actions/runs listing is newest-first, so after ~25 hours as tip the 100 newest runs for that SHA are all scheduled runs and the one CI push run (the oldest) is on page 2 -> ci == [] -> exit 1. (3) No other mechanism saves the manual path: the freshness step "Nishon hali ham main tepasimi" has `if: github.event_name != 'workflow_dispatch'`, so a dispatched still-tip SHA goes straight to the broken check; the workflow_run-triggered path is unaffected only because it fires seconds after CI completes, which is exactly why the defect surfaces on manual dispatch — the recovery/rollback path. (4) The fix at 38f1d750 is a direct admission and repair: `gh api --paginate --jq '.workflow_runs[]' ... > runs.jsonl`, an own re-check `r.get('head_sha') == sha`, a tightened authority filter adding `head_branch == 'main'` (B4), and an explicit `status != 'completed'` pending rejection; its inline comment (B4) restates this exact failure ("bir kundan keyin CI run birinchi sahifadan TUSHIB QOLARDI va tekshiruv 'CI TOPILMADI' bilan yiqilardi"). Direction is fail-closed (exit 1, no Railway mutation reached), so availability-only, consistent with P2. Classification "exists on e60c213a only, fixed at 38f1d750" is accurate. The single runtime assumption (newest-first API ordering) is documented GitHub behavior and is corroborated by the repo's own fix commentary.
verdicts.protective_constraint_found: None at e60c213a. Candidates checked and absent: no `event=push` or `--paginate` on the gh api call; the staleness step is explicitly skipped for workflow_dispatch (`if: github.event_name != 'workflow_dispatch'`) so nothing intercepts before the broken check; the STAGING_DEPLOY_ENABLED gate merely keeps the workflow dormant and does not bear on behavior once enabled, which is the finding's premise. The pagination + head_sha re-check + head_branch filter + pending check exist only at 38f1d750.
verdicts.repro_hint: Static: `git diff e60c213a 38f1d750 -- .github/workflows/staging-deploy.yml` shows the single-page `gh api ... per_page=100` replaced by `--paginate --jq '.workflow_runs[]'` (B4 comment narrates the exact failure). Arithmetic: uptime.yml cron */15 = 96 runs/day > 100-run page within ~25h of a commit becoming main tip. Dynamic (if ever needed): on a SHA that has been main tip >25h, `gh api "repos/OWNER/REPO/actions/runs?head_sha=$SHA&per_page=100" --jq '[.workflow_runs[].name]'` returns only Uptime/DB Backup entries and no CI.

findings.title: Concurrency pending-slot eviction can silently drop the deploy of the newest main SHA
findings.claim: With `cancel-in-progress: false`, GitHub keeps at most ONE pending run per concurrency group and cancels the previously pending run when a newer run is triggered. Trigger order for `workflow_run` follows CI *completion* time, not commit order (the workflow's own header notes CI duration varies 9-30 min). So a deploy run for the NEWEST main SHA sitting in the pending slot can be evicted by a run triggered by a later-finishing CI of an OLDER SHA (or by a re-run of an old failed CI that goes green — re-runs also emit `workflow_run: completed`). The evicted run never executes; the surviving older-SHA run then self-skips via the freshness check (`stale=true`, exit 0, run GREEN). Result: the newest green commit is never deployed, and nothing fails — the dropped run shows as 'canceled', the survivor as 'success'.
findings.invariant: For every green CI run on main tip, either a deploy of that SHA (or a newer one) eventually executes, or a visible failure is raised.
findings.attack_scenario: Pushes X then Z land on main. CI(Z) is green; its deploy run R_Z queues as pending behind a currently running deploy run R_A. Before R_A finishes (~1-2 min window, wider when Railway/API is slow), CI(X) — slow or manually re-run — completes green and triggers R_X, which evicts R_Z (canceled). R_A finishes; R_X runs, sees tip=Z != X, emits `stale=true`, skips, exits green. Staging silently stays on the pre-Z deployment until the next push; no alerting exists (runbook §9 open item), so the gap can persist for days.
findings.evidence: Lines 68-70: `concurrency:\n  group: staging-deploy\n  cancel-in-progress: false` — nothing protects the pending slot. Lines 158-161: stale path is `::notice` + `echo "stale=true"` + green exit, relying on 'a separate run for the newer commit is queued' (comment line 159) — an assumption the pending-slot cancellation falsifies. Identical concurrency block and stale-skip semantics at e60c213a (only the step order moved).
findings.suggested_repro: In a sandbox repo with the same concurrency block: start run A (sleep 120), trigger run B, then trigger run C; observe B is auto-canceled and only A,C execute. Map B=newest SHA, C=older late CI.

verdicts.reasoning: Attempted refutation failed; every element of the claim verifies at 38f1d750. (1) `.github/workflows/staging-deploy.yml` declares workflow-level `concurrency: group: staging-deploy / cancel-in-progress: false`. GitHub's documented semantics for this config: at most one running + one pending run per group, and when a new run is queued while one is pending, the PREVIOUSLY PENDING run is canceled; ordering in a group is explicitly not guaranteed. Since the trigger is `workflow_run` on CI completion, trigger order follows CI finish time, not commit order — the workflow's own header admits CI takes 9-30 min and that an older commit's CI can finish later, and even states "Navbatning O'ZI yetarli emas" (the queue alone is not enough). So a pending deploy run for the newest SHA Z can be evicted (canceled) by a run triggered by a later-finishing CI of an older SHA X, including a manual re-run of an old failed CI that goes green (re-runs emit workflow_run:completed with head_branch=main, passing the job `if:`). (2) The survivor R_X then hits step id `fresh` ("Nishon hali ham main tepasimi"): tip=Z != X, and on the workflow_run path it emits `::notice`, writes `stale=true`, exits 0 — GREEN. Both downstream steps are gated `if: steps.fresh.outputs.stale != 'true'`, so nothing deploys. The justifying comment — "yangiroq commit uchun alohida run bajaradi" (a separate run for the newer commit will do it) — is exactly the assumption the pending-slot eviction falsifies; there is no re-dispatch of the evicted SHA anywhere. (3) No compensating mechanism exists: `uptime.yml` polls only production /health and /health/ready, never the deployed SHA or staging; no other workflow detects staging/main drift; RELEASE_SAFETY_RUNBOOK.md contains zero mentions of concurrency/pending/cancel, and its §2.4 activation plan step 4 DELETES the Railway GitHub trigger (`deploymentTriggerDelete`), making this workflow the ONLY automatic deploy path once enabled — no Railway-side push trigger would cover the dropped commit. §9 confirms stronger-than-email alerting is an unbuilt open item, and a run with conclusion `cancelled` does not fire GitHub's failure notification (that fires on `failure`), so the invariant's "visible failure" branch is not satisfied either: the dropped run shows canceled, the survivor shows success. (4) The window is narrow (three overlapping runs; the pending phase lasts roughly one deploy-job duration, ~30-90s) and the gap self-heals on the NEXT green CI on main — both are severity arguments consistent with P2, not refutations; with no further pushes the staging gap persists indefinitely. Only residual caveat: the eviction is GitHub platform behavior (documented, stable), not repo code, so the exact-timing demonstration still benefits from the sandbox repro. Note the workflow is currently dormant (STAGING_DEPLOY_ENABLED unset per P8 memory); the defect is in the design that the runbook prescribes activating.
verdicts.protective_constraint_found: None. Searched for: (a) any re-dispatch/retry on the stale path in staging-deploy.yml — absent (silent `::notice` + `stale=true` + exit 0, deploy steps skipped); (b) staging-SHA drift monitoring — uptime.yml checks only production /health//health/ready, never a deployed SHA; no other workflow in .github/workflows/ compares staging to main tip; (c) a backup deploy path — RELEASE_SAFETY_RUNBOOK.md §2.4 step 4 deletes the Railway GitHub trigger on activation, so none remains; (d) documentation of the pending-slot risk or alerting on canceled runs — runbook has zero hits for concurrency/pending/cancel and §9 lists alerting as unbuilt. The freshness check (step `fresh`) protects against deploying a stale SHA but is itself the mechanism that turns the dropped-newest-SHA case into a green no-op.
verdicts.repro_hint: Sandbox repo with a workflow using `concurrency: {group: g, cancel-in-progress: false}` and a single job `sleep 120`. Dispatch run A; while A runs, dispatch B (pends), then dispatch C. Observe B's conclusion becomes `cancelled` without executing, C pends then runs — mapping B=deploy of newest main SHA (evicted), C=late-finishing CI of an older SHA whose deploy run then stale-skips green. Verify no failure notification is emitted for B (conclusion is cancelled, not failure).

findings.title: No code-level interlock against Railway's own push trigger — dual deploy paths race, ordering enforced only by runbook prose
findings.symbol: deploy job / mutation step 'Railway'ga AYNAN shu SHA ni deploy qilish' (lines 225-256)
findings.claim: The workflow's own header (lines 30-34) admits that if `STAGING_DEPLOY_ENABLED=true` is set while Railway's GitHub push trigger (id b46dc634-..., currently live per runbook §2.7) still exists, 'IKKI yo'l bir vaqtda deploy qiladi' — two deployers race. Yet the deploy job never queries `project.deploymentTriggers` to verify the old path is deleted before firing `serviceInstanceDeployV2`. The safe ordering (delete trigger at step 4 BEFORE variable at step 6) exists only as prose in RELEASE_SAFETY_RUNBOOK.md §2.4/§2.5 (lines 125-150); P8.1 fixed the prose contradiction (B1/B2) but added no enforcement. The gate's concurrency group covers only its own runs — the Railway push path is outside it, so serialization and the freshness fact-check protect nothing against it.
findings.invariant: While the CI-gated deploy path is enabled, it is the ONLY automated deployer of staging, so 'gate green' implies 'what is running on staging passed CI'.
findings.attack_scenario: Owner performs activation out of order (or restores the trigger per §2.6 and forgets to flip the variable back — runbook line 211 warns exactly this, again prose-only). Push N+1 lands with red CI. With the trigger at checkSuites=false, Railway deploys the CI-red N+1 immediately; the gate correctly refuses it. Staging now runs untested code while the gate workflow's log shows only green/skipped runs — the gate reports control it does not have. With checkSuites=true the race becomes last-write-wins between the trigger's deploy and the gate's mutation for the same SHA (double deploy, mid-flight replacement during smoke tests).
findings.evidence: Lines 30-34 (both SHAs): '3. VA Railway'dagi GitHub trigger'i O'CHIRILADI ... Aks holda IKKI yo'l bir vaqtda deploy qiladi'. The mutation step (lines 225-256) checks only RAILWAY_TOKEN presence and GraphQL `errors`; no deploymentTriggers query, no post-check. Byte-identical risk at e60c213a.
findings.suggested_repro: Static: confirm no `deploymentTriggers` query exists in the workflow (git grep deploymentTrigger 38f1d750 -- .github/workflows returns nothing). A one-request GraphQL read before the mutation, failing when a trigger targets the same environment/service, closes it.

verdicts.reasoning: The literal observation is true: at 38f1d750 the deploy step in .github/workflows/staging-deploy.yml ("Railway'ga AYNAN shu SHA ni deploy qilish") checks only RAILWAY_TOKEN presence and GraphQL errors, and no deploymentTriggers query exists anywhere in code (git grep hits only prose in RELEASE_SAFETY_RUNBOOK.md and a workflow header comment). But the concrete attack cannot be realized, because layered protective constraints already hold: (1) The gate ships disabled — the job's `if: vars.STAGING_DEPLOY_ENABLED == 'true'` makes the workflow a no-op, so a dual-deployer state cannot arise without deliberate owner activation. (2) The finding's harmful branch requires the live trigger at checkSuites=false, citing §2.1 (measured 2026-09-28); but §2.6's manifest in the SAME audited document (read 2026-09-29, RELEASE_SAFETY_RUNBOOK.md line 191) records checkSuites=TRUE — the §2.4 step-1 interim mitigation was already executed, and the §2.6 restore mutation (line 204) hardcodes "checkSuites":true, so no documented path recreates the false state; downgrading it requires an undocumented ad-hoc GraphQL mutation. (3) In the fully dual-active misconfiguration with checkSuites=true, BOTH deployers independently require CI green (Railway's Wait-for-CI cancels on failure; the gate additionally enforces main-tip freshness), so the stated invariant "what runs on staging passed CI" survives — the residual race is a double deploy of the SAME CI-green SHA, staging-only churn, not untested code. (4) §2.7's live observation shows the trigger path currently creates zero deployments even for green CI (staging frozen at d916b9b) — the racing path is empirically inert. (5) Blast radius: production has 0 deployment triggers (§2.1/§2.6) and staging holds no customer data (§3.3), so there is no financial-safety exposure. Reaching the claimed harm requires two compounded, thrice-warned-against owner errors (undocumented checkSuites downgrade AND leaving the variable on), against §2.5's STOP-gated ordering including step 5's mandatory empty-push proof that the old path is dead before step 6 enables the new one. A preflight deploymentTriggers read before the mutation would be worthwhile defense-in-depth, but its absence is a hardening opportunity, not a provable P1 defect.
verdicts.protective_constraint_found: Two independent gates already guard the claimed invariant: (a) the workflow-level kill switch `vars.STAGING_DEPLOY_ENABLED` (unset → job never runs, only one deployer exists); (b) the live Railway trigger b46dc634 runs with checkSuites=true (RELEASE_SAFETY_RUNBOOK.md §2.6 manifest, read 2026-09-29, line 191) — Railway's own Wait-for-CI cancels any deploy whose CI run fails, so even the dual-active misconfiguration cannot put CI-red code on staging; the §2.6 restore snippet recreates the trigger with checkSuites:true and prod has zero triggers. The residual worst case is a same-SHA double deploy to staging.
verdicts.repro_hint: To convert this to a real finding one would have to show a documented/likely path that leaves the trigger at checkSuites=false while STAGING_DEPLOY_ENABLED=true; none exists at 38f1d750 (§2.6 restore hardcodes checkSuites:true, §2.5 orders trigger deletion + empty-push verification BEFORE the variable). Suggested hardening (not a repro): add a preflight GraphQL `project.deploymentTriggers` read in the deploy step, failing when any trigger targets environmentId 7eb2e84f-.../serviceId 4c0164e3-... .

verdicts.reasoning: The static observation is accurate (grep confirms .github/workflows/staging-deploy.yml at 38f1d750 contains no project.deploymentTriggers query; the only mention is comment line 32, and the concurrency group 'staging-deploy' serializes only the gate's own runs). But the P1 attack chain fails against the state recorded at this same SHA. (1) The finding's premise 'trigger currently checkSuites=false per §2.7' is wrong: RELEASE_SAFETY_RUNBOOK.md §2.6 records the trigger manifest measured 2026-09-29 with checkSuites=true, and §2.7 is titled 'O'lchangan holat: checkSuites=true dan keyin staging TO'XTADI' — the workflow header's 'checkSuites=false' line is stale P8 text superseded by the P8.1 manifest. (2) With checkSuites=true, Railway itself blocks a CI-red push (§2.7 quotes Railway semantics: failure immediately cancels the deploy), and ci.yml at this SHA runs on every push to main with no paths filter, so no main push can have a skipped CI; the 'staging runs untested code while the gate log shows green/skipped' scenario therefore needs an extra unmodeled owner act (flipping checkSuites to false) beyond the misordering the finding posits. (3) The exact 'restore per §2.6 and forget the variable' path the finding cites recreates the trigger via a mutation that HARDCODES "checkSuites":true — so even that error keeps the second path CI-gated. (4) The checkSuites=true 'double deploy / last-write-wins' branch is measured infeasible at this SHA: §2.7 documents read-only evidence that the push trigger currently converts main pushes into ZERO Railway deployments (no WAITING/SKIPPED/QUEUED record; staging health stuck at d916b9b1), and instructs resolving this before activation; even with a working trigger, both paths deploy only CI-green main SHAs, so the residual harm is a redundant redeploy of green code mid-smoke — an operational nuisance, not a breach of 'staging runs only CI-passed code'. (5) 'Prose-only' also overstates: §2.5 steps 4-5 gate on empirical checks (deploymentTriggers must return empty; an empty-commit push must produce no deployment in 10 min). The suggested pre-mutation GraphQL read is a reasonable defense-in-depth improvement, but the claimed P1 invariant breach cannot be made concrete without stacking multiple owner misactions, one of which contradicts both the recorded live trigger state and the restore procedure's hardcoded value.
verdicts.protective_constraint_found: Independent platform-level interlock on the second deploy path: the Railway push trigger's checkSuites=true (manifest measured 2026-09-29, RELEASE_SAFETY_RUNBOOK.md §2.6) makes Railway itself refuse CI-red deploys, and ci.yml (on: push: branches: [main, "ci-proof/**"], no paths filter) guarantees every main push carries a real CI suite. The §2.6 restore mutation hardcodes "checkSuites":true, preserving this interlock through the 'restore and forget' error path. Additionally, §2.7's measured evidence shows the push trigger currently produces no deployments at all, so the dual-deployer race is presently physically inert.
verdicts.repro_hint: Verdict would flip to PLAUSIBLE only with evidence that (a) the live trigger is actually checkSuites=false (run the §2.6 read-only query: railway api 'query($id:String!){project(id:$id){deploymentTriggers{edges{node{id checkSuites}}}}}' --var id=32171ad7-cd7a-4eb8-8080-4806250fd1b8) contradicting the §2.6 manifest, or (b) after the webhook path is repaired, a demonstration that a red-CI main push produces a Railway staging deployment while STAGING_DEPLOY_ENABLED=true. The cheap hardening (pre-mutation deploymentTriggers read in the 'Railway'ga AYNAN shu SHA ni deploy qilish' step, failing when any trigger targets environmentId 7eb2e84f.../serviceId 4c0164e3...) is still worth filing as a P3 defense-in-depth suggestion.

findings.title: Mutation is fire-and-forget: TOCTOU after gate checks, no post-deploy verification, and the kill-switch variable is never re-checked
findings.symbol: step chain fresh (141-161) -> CI check (166-223) -> mutation (225-256)
findings.claim: Three related gaps around the commit point, all on both SHAs: (1) TOCTOU — freshness (`gh api repos/.../commits/main`) and CI-greenness are read minutes before the `serviceInstanceDeployV2` call with no re-check, so a SHA that has left main (e.g. an emergency force-push removing a leaked secret) can still be deployed; (2) nothing after the curl verifies the Railway deployment's status — a mutation accepted but failing to build/boot leaves the run green (the workflow parses only GraphQL `errors`), and the workflow's own concurrency comment (lines 62-64) concedes that a job killed after the mutation deploys invisibly, yet `cancel-in-progress: false` does not prevent a human clicking 'Cancel workflow' or a runner loss at exactly that point; (3) `vars.STAGING_DEPLOY_ENABLED` is evaluated only in the job-level `if:` (line 87-90) — a run already admitted (running, or queued in the concurrency group) completes its deploy even after the owner flips the variable to false, contradicting the runbook's rollback claim (line 150: 'variable'ni false qiling — darvoza darhol yopiladi').
findings.invariant: The deployed artifact equals what the gate verified at the moment of deployment, the run's conclusion reflects the deployment's real outcome, and disabling the gate stops all not-yet-fired mutations.
findings.attack_scenario: Owner force-pushes main to drop tip T (secret committed). A dispatch run for T that passed freshness seconds earlier proceeds to deploy T to staging; run shows green; no status poll or alert reveals that staging now runs a commit no longer on any branch. Separately: owner sees a bad deploy starting, sets STAGING_DEPLOY_ENABLED=false as the runbook instructs — the queued next run still deploys.
findings.evidence: Lines 141-161 read main tip once; line 226 `if: steps.fresh.outputs.stale != 'true'` is the only guard on the mutation step; lines 244-256 end with parsing resp.json and `rm -f` — no deployment-status query, no re-read of tip or vars. Same structure at e60c213a (steps merely reordered).
findings.suggested_repro: Code inspection suffices; for (3), GitHub's documented behavior is that job `if:` is evaluated at job start, never re-evaluated mid-run.

verdicts.reasoning:
Read .github/workflows/staging-deploy.yml, RELEASE_SAFETY_RUNBOOK.md and apps/server/tests/test_staging_deploy_gate.py at 38f1d750. The three absences are directly provable from the file; no compensating mechanism exists anywhere at the SHA.

(1) TOCTOU — CONFIRMED, but narrower than claimed. The mutation step's only guards are the job-level `if:` and `if: steps.fresh.outputs.stale != 'true'`; neither the main tip nor anything else is re-read after step `fresh` (the step runs `gh api "repos/$REPO/commits/main"` exactly once). However the window is seconds (three consecutive steps in one job), not "minutes", and the mutation pins `commitSha:$SHA`, so the deployed bytes are exactly the CI-verified commit — the only racy property is the "still main tip" policy. A force-pushed-away commit stays fetchable by SHA on GitHub, so the attack scenario (staging runs an orphaned commit) is concrete; exposure is bounded to staging and self-heals only after the new tip's CI (9–30 min per runbook §2.1) triggers a superseding run.

(2) No post-deploy verification — CONFIRMED. After the curl, the step parses resp.json for GraphQL `errors` only, prints "deploy boshlandi", `rm -f resp.json`, end. No deployment-status poll. The workflow's own concurrency comment concedes the blind spot ("Railway mutatsiyasi yuborilgandan keyin job o'ldirilsa, deploy baribir davom etadi, lekin biz natijani ko'rmaymiz"). I searched for a compensating monitor: uptime.yml polls only `savdoos-production.up.railway.app` — staging is unmonitored; the runbook's health check on staging (§2.5 step 7, `build.commit` + `/health/ready`) is a one-time manual activation step, not per-deploy. test_staging_deploy_gate.py pins only the gate conditions (enabled var, freshness, CI-green), nothing about outcome. So a mutation accepted but failing to build/boot leaves the run green and nothing alerts — provable by reading alone. Note the workflow explicitly scopes itself as "faqat DARVOZA" (gate only), so this is a documented design limit rather than a silent bug, but the invariant "run conclusion reflects deployment outcome" indeed does not hold.

(3) Kill-switch — CONFIRMED for a RUNNING job only. `vars.STAGING_DEPLOY_ENABLED` appears exactly once, in the job-level `if:` (verified by grep of the file); no step re-reads it, and GitHub never re-evaluates a job `if:` mid-run, so a job already executing completes its mutation after the owner flips the variable. Runbook §2.5 step 6 rollback text "variable'ni false qiling — darvoza darhol yopiladi" is therefore accurate only for not-yet-started runs; residual exposure is the one in-flight job (~tens of seconds). The QUEUED-run half of the claim is NOT provable from code and is plausibly false: a run pending on the workflow-level concurrency group has not started its jobs, and the job `if:` (including the `vars` lookup) is evaluated when the job actually starts, which may pick up the flipped value — this needs a live test, and the finding's own repro note asserts GitHub behavior it does not cite.

No protective constraint refutes the core: there is no re-check, no status verification, no mid-run gate, and no staging monitor at this SHA. Severity assessment (P2, staging-only, gate itself still dormant — STAGING_DEPLOY_ENABLED not set per runbook) is consistent with the code.
verdicts.protective_constraint_found: Partial mitigations only, none closing the gaps: (a) `commitSha` is pinned in the mutation payload, so the deployed artifact is byte-identical to the CI-verified SHA — the TOCTOU affects only the "still main tip" policy, not code integrity; (b) `concurrency: group: staging-deploy, cancel-in-progress: false` serializes runs and the stale-skip plus a superseding run for the new tip self-heals staging within one CI cycle (9–30 min); (c) runbook §2.5 step 7 mandates manual `build.commit`/`/health/ready` verification, but only at activation time; (d) uptime.yml exists but polls production only — no staging coverage.
verdicts.repro_hint: Sub-claims (1) and (2) need no repro — the YAML shows no re-read of `repos/$REPO/commits/main` or of `vars` after step `fresh`, and nothing after the curl except parsing `errors`. For sub-claim (3)'s queued-run half (the only unproven part): in a scratch repo, create a workflow with workflow-level concurrency `cancel-in-progress: false` and a job `if: vars.FLAG == 'true'` whose single step sleeps 120s; dispatch it twice so run 2 queues behind run 1, flip FLAG to false while run 2 is pending, and observe whether run 2's job runs or is skipped when the group frees. If skipped, the finding's queued-run claim is wrong and only the in-flight-job exposure (~tens of seconds) remains.

findings.title: P8.1 B3 fix makes workflow_dispatch permanently exempt from the staging-backup gate, not just during activation
findings.claim: The B3 fix changed the gate from `vars.STAGING_BACKUP_ENABLED == 'true'` to `vars.STAGING_BACKUP_ENABLED == 'true' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'`. The justification (comment lines 63-71) is the one-time pre-activation validation run of runbook §3.6, but the exemption is unconditional and permanent: the owner's gate variable can never again stop a manual staging dump. Any actor with Actions-write can run pg_dump against STAGING_DATABASE_URL and publish the (GPG-encrypted) artifact to the PUBLIC repo even when the owner has deliberately set the gate to false — e.g. during a staging restore/migration window when a concurrent dump would capture an inconsistent snapshot that quiescence-fingerprinting only WARNS about (non-quiescent capture is not a failure in _db-backup-core.yml). The e60c213a form had the inverse defect (silent skip, B3); P8.1 traded a false-negative for a gate that no longer gates dispatch.
findings.invariant: An owner-controlled gate variable set to false prevents all runs of the gated job except through an explicitly time-bounded exception.
findings.attack_scenario: Owner sets STAGING_BACKUP_ENABLED=false to freeze backups during a staging DB rebuild. A collaborator (or an automation with a repo-scoped token) dispatches staging-backup.yml; the dump runs against the half-migrated database, the fingerprint mismatch is only a warning, and a 'successful' but inconsistent staging artifact lands in the public repo's artifact store — later restorable by restore-rehearsal-style tooling as if valid.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/staging-backup.yml:72-74 at 38f1d750: `if: >-\n      vars.STAGING_BACKUP_ENABLED == 'true' ||\n      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'`. At e60c213a the line was `if: vars.STAGING_BACKUP_ENABLED == 'true'` (silent-skip defect instead).
findings.suggested_repro: Static: contrast db-backup.yml (deliberately ungated, documented) with staging-backup.yml where a gate exists but is dispatch-bypassable. A time-bounded alternative: gate dispatch too, and have §3.6 use a temporary variable flip for the validation run.

verdicts.protective_constraint_found: Four independent mechanisms: (1) the repo's own production backup workflow `.github/workflows/db-backup.yml` at 38f1d750 has `workflow_dispatch: {}` with NO gate at all, so an Actions-write actor can already dump PRODUCTION on demand — the staging dispatch exemption grants that actor nothing new; (2) a `vars.*` job-`if:` can never bind a write-access actor on workflow_dispatch anyway, because dispatch executes the workflow file from the caller-chosen ref (push a branch with the `if:` deleted, dispatch that ref; repo-level secrets flow in — neither staging-backup.yml nor _db-backup-core.yml uses an `environment:` protection rule); (3) the "inconsistent artifact restorable as if valid" path is structurally closed: `restore-rehearsal.yml` selects runs only from `actions/workflows/db-backup.yml/runs` (line 130) and hard-fails unless the artifact name starts with `savdoos-db-` (lines 174-177), while staging is forced to prefix `savdoos-staging-db` exactly so it can never be consumed as production, and non-quiescence is not silent — `_db-backup-core.yml` records `capture_quiescent=false` in the artifact's `*.meta.json`; (4) the owner retains dispatch-covering freezes: disable the workflow in the Actions UI, or delete the `STAGING_DATABASE_URL` secret, which makes the core's "Sirlarni tekshirish" step `exit 1` fail-closed before any pg_dump runs.
verdicts.reasoning: The finding's factual quote is correct: at 38f1d750, `.github/workflows/staging-backup.yml` lines 72-74 read `if: vars.STAGING_BACKUP_ENABLED == 'true' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'`, so the variable no longer gates manual dispatch. But the claimed invariant ("owner gate variable set to false prevents all runs") is invented, not a repo invariant. The workflow's own comment block documents the variable as a SCHEDULE switch with rollback semantics "variable'ni false qiling; jadval darhol to'xtaydi" (the schedule stops), and the B3 comment explicitly states manual dispatch runs while the schedule stays gated — this is a documented, deliberate design mirroring `db-backup.yml`, where production dispatch has never been gated at all. Against the finding's postulated attacker (Actions-write collaborator/token), the gate was never a security boundary: (a) that actor can already dispatch an ungated production dump via db-backup.yml, a strictly worse capability than the staging dump; (b) even if the `if:` also gated dispatch, workflow_dispatch runs the chosen ref's workflow definition, so a write-access actor bypasses any vars-based gate by dispatching a modified branch — repo secrets are not environment-protected. So P8.1 traded away no real protection. The concrete harm chain also fails: the dump is `pg_dump -Fc` (scripts/backup_postgres.sh), a single-snapshot, transactionally consistent capture — a mid-rebuild dump is logically stale, not corrupt; non-quiescence is recorded fail-visible as `capture_quiescent=false` in `*.meta.json` (plus a ::warning), not hidden; the artifact and both fingerprints are AES256/GPG-encrypted (public-repo download requires BACKUP_PASSPHRASE); staging holds only demo tenants per the workflow header; and restore-rehearsal tooling structurally refuses staging artifacts (production-workflow run lookup + mandatory `savdoos-db-` prefix, deliberate failure otherwise), so the artifact cannot be "restored as if valid" production. Finally, an owner who genuinely needs to freeze staging dumps during a rebuild has two dispatch-covering controls: disabling the workflow (Actions UI) or removing the `STAGING_DATABASE_URL` secret, which the core's secret-check step turns into a hard failure before any connection is made. What remains of the finding is a style preference (a time-bounded exemption would be tidier than a permanent one), not a violated safety property.
verdicts.repro_hint: If the team wants defense-in-depth anyway: gate dispatch too and have runbook §3.6 flip a temporary variable for the one validation run — but note this still does not constrain a write-access actor, who can dispatch a modified ref or the ungated db-backup.yml; the real control is workflow-disable or secret removal.

findings.title: No backup-before-deploy coupling: staging deploys can be enabled with staging backups off and never validated
findings.symbol: deploy job if: (lines 87-90) vs staging-backup.yml gate
findings.claim: STAGING_DEPLOY_ENABLED and STAGING_BACKUP_ENABLED are fully independent variables; the deploy job performs no check that a staging backup exists or is recent before firing a deployment whose app boot runs DDL against the staging database (boot-time schema DDL is the project's deploy model per repo docs). Nothing prevents the activation order deploy-gate-first/backup-gate-never; the ordering lives only in the runbook ('Yoqish tartibi (shu ketma-ketlikda)', RELEASE_SAFETY_RUNBOOK.md line 338 area). Additionally restore-rehearsal.yml only ever restores `savdoos-db-*` (production-prefix) artifacts (pick step queries `workflows/db-backup.yml/runs`), so staging artifacts — the very ones that would matter before a risky staging deploy — are never rehearsed on either SHA.
findings.invariant: A schema-mutating deploy path is not enabled for an environment before a working, restorable backup path for that environment exists.
findings.attack_scenario: Owner enables STAGING_DEPLOY_ENABLED (skipping §3.6 backup activation). A green main commit carrying a destructive boot DDL deploys to staging and corrupts staging data; zero staging backups exist, and even if one dispatch backup had run, its restorability was never proven because restore-rehearsal hardcodes the production backup workflow. Staging state (used for acceptance of the first-merchant gate) is unrecoverable except by re-cloning prod.
findings.evidence: staging-deploy.yml:87-90 references only STAGING_DEPLOY_ENABLED; git grep STAGING_BACKUP 38f1d750 -- .github/workflows/staging-deploy.yml returns nothing. restore-rehearsal.yml pick step (lines ~130): `gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/workflows/db-backup.yml/runs?status=success..."` — staging-backup.yml runs are never candidates. Identical at e60c213a.

verdicts.reasoning: The finding's raw observations are accurate: at 38f1d750 the deploy job gate (.github/workflows/staging-deploy.yml, `if:` at the `jobs.deploy` block) tests only `vars.STAGING_DEPLOY_ENABLED` + CI success + main-tip; no reference to STAGING_BACKUP_ENABLED or backup artifacts exists anywhere in that file, and the runbook's deploy activation checklist (RELEASE_SAFETY_RUNBOOK.md §2.5, steps 0-8) contains no backup prerequisite. The scheduled restore-rehearsal pick step queries only `workflows/db-backup.yml/runs` and filters `savdoos-db-*`. But the finding fails as a defect for four reasons. (1) Wrong baseline: the invariant ('deploy path not enabled before backup path exists') was never held for staging and is not something P8 regressed. staging-deploy.yml's own header and §2.5 document that staging ALREADY auto-deploys on every main push via Railway's pre-existing GitHub trigger, with zero staging backups — and §2.5 step 4 deletes that ungated trigger BEFORE step 6 enables the new gate. So the feared activation order (deploy-gate-first/backup-gate-never) leaves staging strictly SAFER than today's status quo: the same deploys happen, now CI-gated. The workflow adds a gate to an existing path; it does not open a new schema-mutating path whose enablement could precede backups. (2) The attack trigger is not concrete: per the project's deploy model as pinned in restore-rehearsal.yml's smoke steps, boot runs only `python -m app.initdb` (additive DDL); destructive rewrites (e.g. 2026-09-17.uuid-client-columns-v1) are explicitly NOT run at boot ('Boot uni O'ZI bajarmaydi') and require the operator-driven `app.tools.schema_migrate` with preflight + `--commit` + a system-identifier allowlist env var — a 'green main commit carrying a destructive boot DDL' contradicts the audited deploy model. (3) The harm is refuted by the repo's own recovery model, which the finding itself concedes: staging-backup.yml's header states staging holds no customer data ('staging'da RPO talabi yo'q (mijoz ma'lumoti yo'q)'), the data 'is recreated' ('Ma'lumotning o'zi qayta yaratiladi'), and the documented pre-P8 practice was manual prod-clone before deploy (Phase 6A). 'Unrecoverable except by re-cloning prod' describes the designed recovery path, backed by nightly prod backups whose restore IS rehearsed weekly. (4) The staging-rehearsal claim is overstated: restore-rehearsal.yml's `artifact` job accepts `workflow_dispatch` with `backup_run_id` + `artifact_name`, and the 'Run va artefaktni tekshirish' step matches an explicit `artifact_name` exactly with NO `savdoos-db-` prefix requirement — a staging-backup run's `savdoos-staging-db-*` artifact is manually rehearsable on this SHA. Moreover staging restorability is structurally covered: staging uses the identical `_db-backup-core.yml` (single shared implementation, chosen precisely to avoid copy drift), the identical `BACKUP_PASSPHRASE` (§3.6: same passphrase by design), and the core's encrypt step (`encrypt_evidence.sh`, 'Shifrlash + OCHIB TEKSHIRISH') performs a decrypt round-trip at capture time before deleting the plaintext — so an undecryptable staging artifact fails loudly at backup time, and a rotated/lost passphrase is caught weekly by the production-artifact rehearsal that uses the same secret and same restore scripts. What remains is a runbook-ordering process note with demo-data-only blast radius and a documented recovery path — not a P2 financial-safety defect.
verdicts.protective_constraint_found: Layered: (a) RELEASE_SAFETY_RUNBOOK.md §2.5 step 4-before-6 ordering means enabling STAGING_DEPLOY_ENABLED replaces (never adds to) the pre-existing ungated Railway push-deploy path, so backup-less staging deploys are the long-standing baseline, made strictly safer by the CI gate; (b) destructive DDL is excluded from boot by design — `app.initdb` at boot is additive, rewrites require operator-run `app.tools.schema_migrate` preflight/apply with SAVDOOS_SCHEMA_MIGRATE_ALLOWED_SYSTEM_IDENTIFIERS allowlist (production sysid deny-listed); (c) staging recovery model is prod re-clone from nightly `db-backup.yml` backups whose restorability IS rehearsed weekly; (d) staging artifacts share the exact backup code (`_db-backup-core.yml`), passphrase, and capture-time encrypt+decrypt verification (`scripts/encrypt_evidence.sh`), and are manually rehearsable via restore-rehearsal.yml workflow_dispatch (`backup_run_id` + `artifact_name` — the exact-name branch has no production-prefix filter).
verdicts.repro_hint: To demonstrate the residual (process-level) gap anyway: enable STAGING_DEPLOY_ENABLED with STAGING_BACKUP_ENABLED unset and observe staging-deploy.yml's deploy job fires with zero backup checks; to counter-demonstrate the mitigations, dispatch restore-rehearsal.yml with a staging-backup run id and artifact_name=savdoos-staging-db-<...> and observe the staging artifact restores through the same verified pipeline.

findings.title: Production DB endpoint and username can leak into public Actions logs via unsuppressed client stderr
findings.claim: On any connection or auth failure, pg_dump's stderr (and a SQLAlchemy/psycopg2 traceback from `python -m app.tools.db_fingerprint`) is written unfiltered to the Actions log of a PUBLIC repo. libpq error text includes the resolved host, IP, port and user of the Railway TCP proxy (e.g. 'connection to server at "...proxy.rlwy.net" (IP), port NNNNN failed: password authentication failed for user "postgres"'). The workflow's own comments state Actions logs are the weakest boundary (readable without any GitHub account), and password is the ONLY protection on that proxy endpoint. Exists on BOTH e60c213a and 38f1d750 (files byte-identical). The script carefully suppresses stderr for its psql metadata probes (`2>/dev/null || echo '<unknown>'`) but not for the pg_dump call itself: `"$PG_DUMP" -Fc --no-owner -f "$DUMP" "$DATABASE_URL" || fail "pg_dump yiqildi..."`. The two fingerprint steps in _db-backup-core.yml likewise run with DATABASE_URL set and no stderr filtering.
findings.invariant: Nothing that narrows the attack surface of the production database (reachable host, port, role name) may appear in publicly readable logs; only the logical DB name label is permitted (the repo's own stated rule in backup_postgres.sh header: 'URL/parol NEChIQARILMAYDI').
findings.attack_scenario: Railway rotates the DB password or the proxy hiccups one night; the 22:30 UTC db-backup run fails; pg_dump prints the full libpq connection-failure line naming host+port+user into the public log. Anyone watching the public repo's Actions tab now has the exact reachable production Postgres endpoint and role and can run an online password-guessing attack; password is the sole barrier (no IP allowlist / client certs on a Railway TCP proxy).
findings.evidence: scripts/backup_postgres.sh: metadata probes use `2>/dev/null` but the dump does not: `"$PG_DUMP" -Fc --no-owner -f "$DUMP" "$DATABASE_URL" || fail "pg_dump yiqildi — backup OLINMADI."`. .github/workflows/_db-backup-core.yml 'Barmoq izi' steps run `python -m app.tools.db_fingerprint --json > ...` with `DATABASE_URL: ${{ secrets.database_url }}` and no stderr handling; an engine connect failure raises OperationalError carrying libpq's host/port/user text (apps/server/app/tools/_common.py get_engine_and_session imports the app engine, which connects lazily inside the tool). GitHub secret-masking masks the URL string itself but NOT the host/port/user substrings emitted separately by libpq. Classification: exists on BOTH (blob 8c6d6f4c / 23bec7f4 identical at e60c213a and 38f1d750).
findings.suggested_repro: Read-only: run `DATABASE_URL='postgresql://postgres:wrong@somehost.example:5432/railway' ./scripts/backup_postgres.sh /tmp/x` locally and observe libpq stderr naming host/port/user — the same text would land in the public Actions log. Do NOT trigger the real workflow.

verdicts.reasoning: See above.
verdicts.protective_constraint_found: Partial only, and only for the pg_dump leg: scripts/lib/pg_client.sh pg_client_require_ge runs before pg_dump in scripts/backup_postgres.sh; its psql version probe uses 2>/dev/null and fails closed with a sanitized message on any connection/auth failure, so pg_dump never emits a connection-failure line in the primary attack scenario. No such protection exists for the two db_fingerprint workflow steps (which run first): db_fingerprint.main() has no except clause, _common.has_cash_schema has no try/except around the first connect, and no ::add-mask:: is registered anywhere in .github at this SHA.
verdicts.repro_hint: Local, read-only, no workflow trigger: in apps/server with the package installed, run `DATABASE_URL='postgresql://postgres:wrongpass@127.0.0.1:59999/railway' python -m app.tools.db_fingerprint --json` and observe the uncaught sqlalchemy.exc.OperationalError traceback on stderr naming host, port and user — exactly what the "Barmoq izi (dumpdan OLDIN)" step would write to the public Actions log. For the pg_dump leg, note `./scripts/backup_postgres.sh` with the same bad URL exits earlier with the sanitized "server versiyasini aniqlab bo'lmadi" error, never reaching pg_dump.

findings.title: GitHub's 90-day public-repo cap silently halves the documented 180-day monthly production retention; workflow stays green with only a ::warning
findings.symbol: steps 'Saqlash muddatini hisoblash' and 'Haqiqiy saqlash muddatini tekshirish'
findings.claim: db-backup.yml requests retention_monthly=180, but the repo is public and GitHub caps artifact retention at 90 days. Both the pre-computation check (`if [ "$DAYS" -gt 90 ]; then echo "::warning::..."`) and the post-upload verification (`if got < want: print("::warning::...")`) emit warnings only — the run concludes SUCCESS. So every monthly-tier production backup is retained for half the documented period, forever, with a green nightly signal and no failure email (GitHub only mails on failed runs, never on warnings). The header comment in db-backup.yml acknowledges the cap, but PRODUCTION_OPERATIONS_RUNBOOK/RPO language and the tier design (14/56/180) still describe 180 days. Exists on BOTH SHAs (files identical).
findings.invariant: A backup run may only report success when the artifact's actual expires_at satisfies the retention policy the tier was designed for — or the policy itself must be corrected to what is achievable (90), so the documented RPO is never silently false.
findings.attack_scenario: Day 120 after an incident is discovered (e.g. slow data corruption from a bad migration noticed a quarter later), the operator goes to restore the 1st-of-month artifact per the runbook's 180-day monthly tier — it expired at day 90. All nightly runs were green the whole time; the only trace was a ::warning annotation nobody is alerted on. Recovery point is permanently lost.
findings.evidence: _db-backup-core.yml retention step: `if [ "$DAYS" -gt 90 ]; then echo "::warning::$DAYS kun so'raldi... maksimumi 90 kun."` (no exit). Verification step: `if got < want: print("::warning::GitHub saqlash muddatini %s -> %s kunga QISQARTIRDI...")` — warning, not `::error` + non-zero exit. db-backup.yml passes `retention_monthly: 180` and its own header admits '180 kunlik oylik bosqich amalda 90 kun bo'ladi'. Classification: exists on BOTH (matches the known-open 'retention shortening only warns' item; NOT fixed by P8.1).
findings.suggested_repro: Static: compare requested 180 vs GitHub docs' 90-day public-repo maximum; confirm both code paths use ::warning with no failure. Runtime proof would need a real 1st-of-month run (forbidden here).

verdicts.protective_constraint_found: None. Both retention checks in _db-backup-core.yml ("Saqlash muddatini hisoblash" and "Haqiqiy saqlash muddatini tekshirish") emit ::warning without failing the run; no other workflow archives the monthly artifact elsewhere; the runbook's §3.3 retention table (180 days) carries no 90-day caveat. The header comments in db-backup.yml/_db-backup-core.yml acknowledge the cap but are documentation of the gap, not a mechanism preventing it.
verdicts.repro_hint: Static proof suffices: `git show 38f1d750:.github/workflows/_db-backup-core.yml` — grep both `::warning` sites and confirm neither is followed by `exit 1`/SystemExit; `git show 38f1d750:.github/workflows/db-backup.yml` shows `retention_monthly: 180`; `git show 38f1d750:PRODUCTION_OPERATIONS_RUNBOOK.md` line 194 shows the uncorrected 180-day promise. findings.title: P8.1 B3 dispatch exemption removes the only validation of the schedule gate: a mistyped STAGING_BACKUP_ENABLED value silently disables nightly staging backups forever
findings.claim: The P8.1 gate is `vars.STAGING_BACKUP_ENABLED == 'true' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'` (exact lowercase string compare). The runbook §3.6 enablement order is: add secret -> manual dispatch (must be green) -> set variable. Post-B3, the manual-dispatch validation step no longer exercises the `vars` half of the gate at all (dispatch short-circuits it), so setting the variable to 'True', 'TRUE', ' true' or any other spelling is never caught: the operator sees a green manual run, sets the variable, and every scheduled run thereafter is SKIPPED — gray, not red, and GitHub sends no notification for skipped runs. This reproduces the exact 'silent no-backup' failure class (11 nights of false success) the file's own comments say the design exists to prevent. On main (e60c213a) the gate was `if: vars.STAGING_BACKUP_ENABLED == 'true'` — a different bug (B3: dispatch itself silently skipped); the residual described here is specific to the fixed form.
findings.invariant: The enablement procedure must prove the SCHEDULED path will actually run (i.e., the validation run must evaluate the same predicate the schedule will), or a skipped scheduled backup must produce an alert.
findings.attack_scenario: Operator follows runbook §3.6: manual dispatch is green (gate bypassed), then types STAGING_BACKUP_ENABLED=True in the GitHub Variables UI. Cron 21:30 fires nightly; `'True' == 'true'` is false; job skips. No artifact, no red run, no email. Weeks later a bad staging migration needs the pre-release snapshot the runbook promises — none exists since enablement day.
findings.evidence: 38f1d750:.github/workflows/staging-backup.yml: `if: >-\n  vars.STAGING_BACKUP_ENABLED == 'true' ||\n  github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'`. GitHub Actions `==` on contexts is case-insensitive for the operands' string comparison ONLY for boolean literals, not for arbitrary strings with whitespace/typos; and skipped jobs generate no failure notification. The file's own comment predicts the failure mode: nightly gray runs become 'odatiy' and real absence goes unnoticed. Classification: exists-on-p8.1 (residual gap of the B3 fix); on main the analogous silent-skip hit the dispatch path instead (the original B3).
findings.suggested_repro: Static: evaluate the `if:` expression semantics for vars value 'True' vs 'true' (GitHub `==` is case-insensitive per docs — but leading/trailing whitespace or values like '1'/'yes' still fail); at minimum the §3.6 procedure demonstrably never evaluates the vars predicate before relying on it.

verdicts.reasoning: The finding fails on both of its factual pillars. (1) The concrete attack ("operator types STAGING_BACKUP_ENABLED=True; 'True' == 'true' is false; nightly job skips forever") is wrong: per GitHub's official expressions documentation, `==` between two string operands is a case-insensitive comparison for ALL strings — the finding's evidence claim that case-insensitivity holds "ONLY for boolean literals" is fabricated and appears nowhere in the docs. 'True', 'TRUE', 'tRuE' all satisfy `vars.STAGING_BACKUP_ENABLED == 'true'` (.github/workflows/staging-backup.yml, job `backup` if:), so the schedule runs. The only realistically likely misspelling class (capitalization) is absorbed by the platform. (2) The claim that the B3 dispatch exemption "removes the only validation of the schedule gate" is false because that validation never existed in any version: RELEASE_SAFETY_RUNBOOK.md §3.6 orders the steps secret (1) -> manual dispatch (2) -> set variable (3), so the dispatch always ran BEFORE the variable existed. Under the pre-B3 gate (`if: vars.STAGING_BACKUP_ENABLED == 'true'` alone, main e60c213a) the dispatch evaluated vars as '' and silently skipped — that was bug B3 itself. No version's step 2 ever evaluated the operator-typed value, so B3 removed nothing; the alleged residual is not a regression of the fix. What survives is only the speculative vector of an operator typing '1', 'yes', or a whitespace-padded value — which requires contradicting the exact literal `STAGING_BACKUP_ENABLED=true` printed in RELEASE_SAFETY_RUNBOOK.md:342, the rollback line ('false'), and the workflow's own enablement comment (step 3), and this exposure is identical pre- and post-B3. The gate's 'true'/'false'/'' contract is additionally locked by mutation-tested expression evaluation in apps/server/tests/test_backup_schedule_and_runbook.py (_eval_backup_gate, test_B3_variable_QOYILGACH_jadval_ISHLAYDI, test_B3_JADVAL_variable_YOQLIGIDA_ISHLAMAYDI). The accurate fragments of the finding (skipped runs are gray with no email; restore-rehearsal.yml only exercises production `savdoos-db-*` artifacts, never staging ones) are pre-existing, self-disclosed limitations — runbook §3.5 explicitly lists weak failure visibility as an open item (§9) — not a defect introduced or masked by the P8.1 B3 fix. Per the audit's default, the attack as stated cannot be made concrete.
verdicts.protective_constraint_found: GitHub Actions expression `==` performs case-insensitive string comparison on all string operands (documented platform semantics), so every capitalization variant of 'true' satisfies the gate `vars.STAGING_BACKUP_ENABLED == 'true'`; the exact enablement literal is pinned in three places (RELEASE_SAFETY_RUNBOOK.md §3.6 step 3, the rollback instruction, and the workflow's enablement comment), and apps/server/tests/test_backup_schedule_and_runbook.py mutation-tests the gate expression's semantics for '', 'false', 'true' across schedule and dispatch events.
verdicts.repro_hint: If the residual is still deemed worth closing: a runbook step 4 ("after setting the variable, run `gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/actions/variables/STAGING_BACKUP_ENABLED --jq .value` and confirm it equals 'true' exactly, or wait for the first 21:30 UTC run and confirm it is not 'skipped'") would validate the typed value; note the exposure only materializes for values like '1', 'yes', or whitespace-padded strings, never for case typos.

findings.title: Publicly downloadable backup artifacts still carry a plaintext meta.json and dump checksum revealing DB size trend, schema set, object count and server version
findings.symbol: Upload artifact step path list / backup_postgres.sh meta.json writer
findings.claim: P8/P8.1 encrypted the fingerprints (row counts, ledger sums) precisely because artifacts on this public repo are downloadable by any authenticated GitHub account — but `*.meta.json` and `*.dump.sha256` are still uploaded plaintext. meta.json contains: logical database name, `size_bytes` and `toc_objects` of the full production dump, `server_version` (exact PG minor), `schemas_present`, and the sha256 of the PLAINTEXT dump. A nightly public series of size_bytes/toc_objects is a business-volume growth curve (the same class of magnitude leak the fingerprint encryption was added to stop, just coarser), and the exact server minor version fingerprints the publicly reachable proxy endpoint for known-CVE targeting. The plaintext-dump sha256 additionally gives an offline confirmation oracle for any party who obtains a candidate dump. Exists on BOTH SHAs (core identical) and is acknowledged in the header comment — but the acknowledgment predates the fingerprint-encryption rationale, which logically extends to size/version.
findings.invariant: Nothing derived from production data contents or magnitude, and nothing that fingerprints the reachable production server, appears unencrypted in artifacts of a public repository.
findings.attack_scenario: A competitor or attacker with any GitHub account downloads savdoos-db-* artifacts nightly (or scrapes expires_at/meta via API), plots size_bytes over months to estimate merchant/transaction growth, and reads server_version=18.x to select exploits against the Railway TCP proxy endpoint (whose host/user may additionally leak per the log finding).
findings.evidence: _db-backup-core.yml upload path list: `backups/*.dump.gpg`, `backups/*.sha256`, `backups/*.meta.json`, plus encrypted fingerprints — meta and sha256 have no .gpg. scripts/backup_postgres.sh writes meta.json with `"database": "$DBNAME", "server_version": "$PGVER", "schemas_present": "$SCHEMAS", "size_bytes": $SIZE, "toc_objects": $OBJECTS, "sha256": "$SHA"`. The encrypt step then appends encrypted-file checksums into the same plaintext meta.json. Classification: exists on BOTH.
findings.suggested_repro: Download any savdoos-db-* artifact from the public repo's Actions UI with an ordinary GitHub account and open the .meta.json (read-only; no workflow trigger needed).

verdicts.reasoning: The core claim is provable by reading the code at 38f1d750 (and the identical core at e60c213a — the P8.1 diff touches neither file). (1) .github/workflows/_db-backup-core.yml, "Upload artifact" step, ships `backups/*.sha256` and `backups/*.meta.json` with no .gpg suffix, alongside `*.dump.gpg` and the two encrypted fingerprints. (2) scripts/backup_postgres.sh writes into meta.json exactly the claimed fields: `"database": "$DBNAME"` (SELECT current_database()), `"server_version": "$PGVER"` (SHOW server_version — exact PG minor), `"schemas_present"`, `"size_bytes": $SIZE`, `"toc_objects": $OBJECTS`, and `"sha256": "$SHA"` of the PLAINTEXT dump. The workflow's encrypt step then merges sha256_encrypted/encrypted_size_bytes into the same plaintext meta.json. (3) The workflow's own comments establish the threat model: the repo is public ("private=false" verified 2026-09-28) and any signed-in GitHub account can download artifacts — the exact rationale used to encrypt the fingerprints (commit 14d29c2) and scrub run logs (9a31175). No protective constraint exists: no auth gate beyond any-GitHub-account, no aggregation/rounding of size_bytes, and the 90-day artifact cap does not stop a nightly scraper from accumulating a size_bytes/toc_objects growth series. The stated invariant ("nothing derived from production magnitude and nothing fingerprinting the server appears unencrypted in public artifacts") is violated on its face. Two corrections to the finding, which reduce but do not remove severity: (a) the sub-claim that the header acknowledgment "predates the fingerprint-encryption rationale" is FALSE — the header line "Artefaktda OCHIQ qoladigan yagona narsalar — *.meta.json ... va *.sha256" was written in 14d29c2, the same commit that introduced fingerprint encryption, so this is a contemporaneous, consciously accepted residual, not an overlooked leftover; (b) the "offline confirmation oracle" from the plaintext-dump sha256 is weak: pg_dump -Fc embeds a creation timestamp, so the hash only confirms possession of that exact stolen file (whose holder already has the data), not a reconstructed candidate. The remaining substance — nightly plaintext size/object-count trend (business-volume curve) plus exact server minor version fingerprinting the publicly reachable Railway proxy, in artifacts of a public repo — stands as written, deliberate acceptance notwithstanding, since the same P8/P8.1 rationale (magnitude leakage) logically covers size_bytes/toc_objects and was applied inconsistently.
verdicts.protective_constraint_found: None. The only barriers are (a) a signed-in GitHub account to download artifacts — explicitly deemed insufficient by the workflow's own comments when it encrypted the fingerprints — and (b) the 90-day public-repo retention cap, which limits lookback per point in time but not a nightly scraper building a long series. Neither prevents the leak.
verdicts.repro_hint: Static: read the Upload artifact path list in .github/workflows/_db-backup-core.yml (backups/*.sha256, backups/*.meta.json — no .gpg) and the meta.json heredoc in scripts/backup_postgres.sh at 38f1d750. Live confirmation (read-only, ordinary GitHub account): download any savdoos-db-* artifact from the public repo's Actions UI and open the .meta.json.

findings.title: Single shared symmetric passphrase across production and staging with no key identifier in metadata makes rotation silently strand old artifacts and widens blast radius
findings.claim: Staging deliberately reuses production's BACKUP_PASSPHRASE ('production bilan BIR XIL parol ishlatiladi'). All backups are gpg --symmetric AES256 under that one passphrase, and neither meta.json nor the artifact name records any key identifier/version. Consequences: (a) the passphrase is the ONLY barrier on full-production dumps any GitHub account can download, and it is now exercised by two environments' procedures and visible to anything with Actions-secrets scope (the known-open '5 foreign GitHub Apps' item); (b) if it is ever rotated, artifacts within the 14/56/90-day retention window become undecryptable with the current secret and there is no metadata field telling the operator which passphrase an old artifact needs — the weekly restore rehearsal would go red with a bare gpg decrypt failure, and a real disaster-day restore of a pre-rotation artifact fails unrecoverably unless the old value was archived out-of-band (the runbook prescribes no passphrase escrow/rotation procedure). Exists on BOTH SHAs.
findings.invariant: Every encrypted artifact must be decryptable throughout its retention window, which requires either a stable escrowed key or a key-id recorded per artifact; and compromise of a lower-trust environment's tooling must not decrypt production history.
findings.attack_scenario: Owner rotates BACKUP_PASSPHRASE after the staging enablement (or after removing a suspicious GitHub App). Three weeks later production data is corrupted; the operator pulls the 1st-of-month artifact — gpg: decryption failed. meta.json contains sha256_encrypted but no key hint; the old passphrase was never escrowed. The backup existed, was green nightly, and is unrecoverable.
findings.evidence: staging-backup.yml: `passphrase: ${{ secrets.BACKUP_PASSPHRASE }}` with header comment mandating reuse; scripts/encrypt_evidence.sh uses only `--symmetric --cipher-algo AES256 --passphrase-fd 0` (no key id, no recipient); _db-backup-core.yml's meta rewrite adds sha256_encrypted/environment/capture_quiescent but no key-version field; RELEASE_SAFETY_RUNBOOK.md prescribes no rotation/escrow step. Classification: exists on BOTH.
findings.suggested_repro: Static: grep meta.json fields written in _db-backup-core.yml and backup_postgres.sh for any key identifier (none); confirm runbook has no passphrase escrow/rotation section.

verdicts.reasoning:
The finding's factual observations are partially accurate but its two consequences collapse on inspection of the audited SHA (38f1d750).

(1) The "rotation silently strands old artifacts / no escrow or rotation procedure in the runbook" claim is directly contradicted by RELEASE_SAFETY_RUNBOOK.md at this SHA, which contains an explicit, prominent BACKUP_PASSPHRASE rotation procedure with escrow. Section 7 ("Sir almashtirish") flags it as the most dangerous item: "**⚠️ `BACKUP_PASSPHRASE` — eng xavfli band.** Uni almashtirish **barcha mavjud shifrlangan nusxalarni ochib bo'lmaydigan qiladi**" and prescribes, in order: (a) test-restore the latest artifact with the OLD passphrase first (Restore Rehearsal, artifact mode), (b) save the old passphrase in the password manager labeled "eski nusxalar uchun" (for old backups) — "o'chirmang" (do not delete), (c) only then set the new value and immediately run + test-restore a fresh backup. The general rules section additionally mandates "Har qiymatni **parol menejerida** oldindan saqlang" (escrow every secret value before setting it). §6.5 repeats the residual-risk warning ("eski shifrlangan nusxalar **faqat eski parol bilan** ochiladi — parolni yo'qotmang") and §6.4 P1 orders rotation AFTER a verified old-passphrase restore. §7.0 even corrects the exact misconception in the attack scenario: rotating the GitHub secret does NOT make old artifacts undecryptable — the old passphrase still opens them; only new artifacts diverge. So the invariant's disjunction ("stable escrowed key OR key-id per artifact") is satisfied by the escrow branch: the scenario "the old passphrase was never escrowed" requires the operator to violate three explicit, bolded runbook steps, which is operator error against a documented control, not a code/process defect. With a single rotation event whose date is known and artifact names/meta carrying timestamps, the missing key-id field is at most a convenience gap: gpg symmetric decrypt with the escrowed "eski nusxalar uchun" entry resolves any ambiguity in one try.

(2) The "widened blast radius" claim adds nothing concrete: staging-backup.yml passes `secrets.BACKUP_PASSPHRASE` from the SAME repository's Actions secrets store into the SAME reusable workflow (`_db-backup-core.yml`) that production's db-backup.yml already uses. There is no second, lower-trust secret store or environment holding the passphrase — anything with Actions-secrets scope on this repo could already reach it via the production workflow before staging existed. The reuse is a deliberate, comment-documented decision ("ikkinchi parol = ikkinchi yo'qotish xavfi, foydasi yo'q" — a second password is a second loss risk) in both staging-backup.yml and RELEASE_SAFETY_RUNBOOK.md line 331, and cross-environment artifact confusion is structurally prevented by the distinct `artifact_prefix: savdoos-staging-db` (restore-rehearsal.yml deliberately fails on multiple `savdoos-db-*` matches).

Verified-true residue: meta.json (rewritten in `.github/workflows/_db-backup-core.yml`, "Dump + checksum + metadata" and the sha256_encrypted rewrite step, lines ~226-235) records sha256_encrypted, encrypted_file, encrypted_size_bytes, capture_quiescent, fingerprint_file, environment — no key-version field; scripts/encrypt_evidence.sh uses only `--symmetric --cipher-algo AES256 --passphrase-fd 0`. Adding a passphrase-generation-label to meta.json would be a reasonable hardening nicety, but as stated (P2, "silently strand", "runbook prescribes no escrow/rotation") the finding is refuted by the existing protective mechanism: RELEASE_SAFETY_RUNBOOK.md §6.4/§6.5/§7 escrow-before-rotate procedure with mandatory pre-rotation restore verification.
verdicts.protective_constraint_found: RELEASE_SAFETY_RUNBOOK.md §7 (audited SHA 38f1d750): mandatory pre-rotation escrow procedure for BACKUP_PASSPHRASE — (1) test-restore latest artifact with old passphrase, (2) keep old passphrase in password manager labeled "for old backups", never delete, (3) only then rotate, then immediately take and test-restore a new backup; plus the general rule to store every secret value in the password manager before setting it, and §6.5's explicit "old backups open only with the old passphrase — do not lose it" warning. Blast-radius half: both environments draw the passphrase from the same repo-level Actions secrets store into the same reusable _db-backup-core.yml, so staging reuse grants no principal any decryption capability it did not already have.
verdicts.repro_hint: Not needed (refuted statically). To re-verify: git show 38f1d750:RELEASE_SAFETY_RUNBOOK.md — see §6.5, §7.0 table and the "BACKUP_PASSPHRASE — eng xavfli band" block (~lines 574-623); git show 38f1d750:.github/workflows/_db-backup-core.yml — meta rewrite step confirms no key-id field (the only true residue).
